Before the variable-length digest port, `CasGc.cpp` condemn-sweep and several `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites used `hexToU128` inside `catch(...) { continue; }`, silently classifying every SHA-256 blob as foreign and causing a permanent leak or false-clean fsck result.
A predecessor PUT that completes after successor recovery can create a late older-epoch log invisible to the successor and later snapshots; a missed `+1` edge is a data-loss class, not merely a leak.
Unconditional staging-to-blob copy is unsafe because the read path does not rehash bodies, so overwriting a live object can expose a torn or short body as valid data.
A dedup shortcut that adopts an existing blob after HEAD without the condemn check can reference a blob pending GC deletion and violate edge-before-observe, causing data loss.

The positive fail-closed CAS GC baseline guard remained untested at HEAD even though the guard survives at `CasGc.cpp:927`; the fresh-pool tests covered only the pass case and a different adopted-seal guard.
`RunFileReader::next` trusts an un-checksummed `record_count` from the block head and can index beyond the block payload, violating `CasRunFile`'s fail-closed corruption contract.

The EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE invariant in `Build::observeAndAdmit` was guarded only by `chassert(precommitted)`, so release builds could adopt an existing incarnation without durable precommit and watermark protection.
`dropRefBestEffort` silently swallows rollback failures; a correlated backend outage can leave a permanently live phantom ref because GC reclaims only unreferenced objects.

Before consolidation, `RetryStrategy` recognized HTTP 412 while `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` and `copyObjectConditional` used only exception name/message checks, missing stores such as RustFS that leave the exception name unparsed.

The `Build::promote` owner-liveness closure guard is a race-only defensive backstop: both legitimate removal paths, abandon and `dropNamespace` cancellation, satisfy `requireAlive` before the closure, while only a narrow promote-versus-`dropNamespace` race reaches the closure guard.
A S38 post-restart finding reported `txn_id 2-0 not strictly greater than greatest applied 2-MAX` after a seal `{2,MAX}`, indicating that sequence zero should not exist.
The `adoptEvidence` relink lifecycle exposure was tracked independently from the abandoned §5 optimization and required a separate investigation.
The fetch-by-relink residual requires a `stageManifest` stall across at least two GC folds, every replica dropping the part ref, and a deposed leader firing `deleteExact(h,t1)` after promote.
The planned §5 spare-heal transition reintroduced the removed `clearSparedMeta` behavior by clearing a tombstone while the blob retained condemn-time token `t1`.
A spare that clears a tombstone can advertise a blob as Clean at token `t1`, allowing a stale deposed-leader `deleteExact(h,t1)` to delete the live body.
A token-preserving `adoptEvidence` recovery path can re-reference a condemned blob at token `t1`, invalidating the premise that all in-degree recovery uses fresh-token resurrection.
The original `CaMetaAbsenceClean.tla` gate was false-green because `GcSpareHeal` atomically reset `queuedDeletes`, unlike the real code.
The separate adoptEvidence exposure exists because the destination's durable edge is committed after the body-time adopt evidence and the trusted promote path can defer absent-body detection to fsck.

The original fetch-by-relink correctness hole was that the sender released its part before the receiver committed its ref, leaving no in-degree overlap during a sufficiently long precommit stall; the affected reports were `#42` and `#43`.

The MOVE-to-CA implementation has two independent defects: the part-path parser routes files under `<table>/moving/<part>/` to the literal ref `moving`, and `DataPartStorageOnDiskBase::clonePart` copies files through separate autocommit transactions that a CA disk cannot use for a multi-file part.

Scenario S36 found that TO-CA MOVE was unimplemented: the generic mover copied files independently, producing `Code 236 promote: ref 'moving' already names a different committed manifest` or `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for a column file.
Without install-time materialization, the COW overlay grows across successful flushes and later `working = rt->state` copies regress toward copying all rows touched over the object's lifetime.

Review finding №10 is a real TSan data race on the plain `std::function` event sink because `setEventSink` runs after `Pool::open` starts the renewal thread, although the traced timing refutes crash-grade overlap.

Review finding №13 is real hardening: telemetry emitted after durable ref publication must not turn a successful operation into a caller-visible failure; post-durable emission should catch, log, and continue.

Review finding №20 is split: decoder identity fields need hygiene checks, duplicate JSON keys already throw `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and fold seals lack a key-to-generation binding that could corrupt the GC cursor or cause premature deletion.
Review finding №21 is real: casting a decoded `uint64` version to `uint32` before validation turns `4294967299` into version `3` and can bypass compatibility checks.

Review finding №25 is latent terminal-transaction hardening: a failed `commit` can leave `PartStaging::published=true`, causing a hypothetical retry on the same transaction object to skip work and report success.
Review finding №26 is a real stale-payload mechanism but deferred because the only production appender is the single-writer, per-mutation-unique `MergeTreeMutationEntry::writeCSN` path.
The structural defect is that `MergeTreeData::Transaction` treats disk durability as a nested side effect of its commit, while rollback never calls an undo or abort operation on the disk transaction.

Six ASan stack-use-after-scope findings were caused by a reference-capturing event sink writing to a local `events` vector after that vector had been destroyed while the owning `Pool` was still being torn down.

`CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell` had a heap-use-after-free because `const Layout & layout = store->layout()` was used after `store.reset()` freed the `Pool` containing the referenced `Layout`.

The S13 quiesce wedge was associated with a `partAccess` use-after-free and a mutex that blocked `gcHealth` for an entire GC round; the fix split round serialization from pointer publication and was validated by a clean third S13 attempt.
The CAS review triage confirmed a scheduler/`cas_store` shutdown use-after-free race and an event-sink assignment/read data race; task T9 fixed both in commit `846a4f62a62`.
A future mutation path that bypasses `applyOpInPlace` would desynchronize the ref-ledger counters; the debug `chassert` is the immediate detector for this invariant violation.

The first `TrustedReplay` validation-elision design failed open on double-owner history; the correction runs the cross-owner check unconditionally and makes snapshot duplicate-owner validation fail closed.

Concurrent part workers exposed a latent `CasRefLedger` defect: a leader throwing before carve could leave its `RefMutationItem` in `rt->pending`, allowing a follower to invoke a dangling by-reference `build_ops` closure.
The former interleaved ref-ledger carve could lose already-popped items when `seen_refs`, batch, or `owned_items` allocation threw, leaving waiters blocked and callback lifetimes unsafe.

If the hidden transaction is a removal, GC can delete blobs that the recovered writer view still references, producing a dangling committed manifest; if it is an addition, GC over-protects blobs; without a covering snapshot, recovery can repeatedly fail with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
Plain GET absence cannot safely authorize writer-epoch re-minting because it flattens transport or access failures into not-found; lifecycle decisions must use the authoritative probe outcome.
Same uuid plus same epoch plus an unfenced body does not prove the body came from the current writer, because a vanished epoch object can let a second same-uuid process re-mint the same pair.

If both epoch and mount control objects are wiped under a live mount, a same-pair twin can still exist briefly; the residual design relies on the surviving writer fencing on its next beat rather than allowing silently persistent dual writers.
The ref lane can lose a durable transaction from its in-memory view and then permanently hide that transaction behind a snapshot, making the defect data-loss class.

A residual post-commit exception window remains around `eraseView` and `ContentAddressedTransaction::publishStaging`'s `out_slot`: fallible work can occur after a durable commit is made but before the commit is recorded in the caller's slot.
Two current catalog rows sharing a `life_id` are `CORRUPTED_DATA`, not a first-row-wins condition; catalog mutation, REBUILD, decommission, fold adoption, and destructive GC fail closed on that cut.

Before the authoritative flip, an empty catalog can make `result.frontier_complete = universe_authoritative && result.frontier_proven == result.frontier_namespaces` evaluate as `0 == 0`, falsely clearing destructive suppression; an empty universe must not count as a complete frontier.

`_ckpt.life_epoch` can receive legitimate contributions from both `CasRefCatalog::completeCreation` and the first `NamespaceBirth` chunk, and treating every different present value as corruption would wedge resumed creation and restart-before-first-write sequences.

A current catalog life can have an empty key space while a dead incarnation of the same logical namespace has objects; filtering dead keys and walking the current life can then falsely prove the frontier complete and enable destruction.

If the catalog is absent, a sentinel fallback such as `stageATransition(ns)` can make real-incarnation namespaces look empty and let a damaged catalog produce a complete frontier; an un-cataloged namespace must be unproven rather than walked at a fabricated key.

`ReplicatedMergeTreePartCheckThread` can treat a CA disk's transient `INVALID_STATE` caused by a missing mount lease as a broken part because `isRetryableException` in `checkDataPart.cpp:70` does not list `INVALID_STATE`; the current remediation detaches the part, removes it from ZooKeeper, and queues a fetch.

The LIST-liar regression tests intentionally pin current defective behavior: a hidden middle record produces `under_lie.unchecked == 1` and `under_lie.reachable == 0`, while a hidden tail transaction can make fsck report a clean result over a ref set missing an acknowledged publish; fixing `recoverRefTable` is expected to make these tests fail until their assertions are updated.

Exactly two CA transient throw sites can cause destructive misclassification: `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1111` (`TransientNotLive`) and `:1163` (probe `Indeterminate`), both on the READ plane.

`isTransientRecoveryError` at `CasRefLedger.cpp:89-97` is a CA-internal denylist-shaped classifier with an unsafe default; it guards ref-recovery re-drive at `:1085` but is not reachable from the lifecycle-gate throw because recovery reads bypass `ref_request_controller`.

If the catalog names namespace `N` at life `Y` while `N`'s objects and shard-0 fold cursor belong to life `X`, the frontier walk can prove a complete frontier without probing `X` and destructive GC can delete live blobs from `X`.

`CasFsck.cpp` resolves `life` for `walkRefStream` but omits it when calling `crossEpochFromSeal`, so a namespace drop-and-recreate during the walk can make fsck report a false unconsumed-closing-seal verdict.

`runFsckImpl` obtains its namespace universe from `Pool::listNamespaces`, which is only a union of backend `LIST` results, so a live catalog namespace omitted from `roots/` and `cas/refs/` listings is never checked and fsck can report clean.

After `_cleanup` and the cleanup item are gone, legal removal debris and fabricated catalog-entry loss can be byte-identical, so an anomaly classifier cannot accept one and reject the other without another durable evidence object.
`CasRefCatalog::read` currently treats an absent catalog as a virgin empty catalog, so a permanent `Retired`-only design would allow catalog loss after `_ckpt` deletion to reopen a name for birth.

After `_cleanup` is removed, a legal removal and fabricated entry loss can both appear as an absent catalog entry with surviving canonical life-qualified debris, so the two cases cannot be separately classified from store contents alone.

`CaGcDestructiveGateCore.tla` pins `UniverseAuthoritative == TRUE` without a sabotage, so the authoritative-universe term of the production `frontier_complete` gate is not load-bearing in the model and is false in production today.
The B90 `ThreadGroup` fix makes a borrowed child retain a `shared_ptr` to its parent group so background work cannot use freed parent counters.

The B37 `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` fix throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when `current_writer` is absent instead of relying on a release-build `chassert` no-op; a missing `logs_dir` remains normal for storages that do not materialize empty directories.
The CAS event sink has an unsynchronized assignment/read race because renewal threads can read a shared `std::function` while `setEventSink` assigns it.

A propagating telemetry exception after durable ref publication can leave transaction state inconsistent: the caller sees failure while a live ref exists and the transaction lacks the ref for success or rollback.
Safety-critical CAS decoders accept incomplete or duplicate records and unbound fold generations, so a misplaced seal can authorize skipped references.

A truncated blob can be admitted as a dedup hit because `PartWriteTxn::observeAndAdmit` checks only `hr.size >= blob_header_len` and does not compare the payload size with the caller's expected `source.size`.

A skipped live manifest `+1` can cause exact-token deletion of a blob still referenced by that manifest after another owner's `-1` folds, because exact-token deletion protects against replacement but not an owner edge absent from GC state.

The orphan-manifest sweep's premise that an unowned manifest has no folded edges is false after a precommit `+1` folds, leaving stranded in-degree edges with no possible `-1` after the manifest is deleted.

Applying a successor observation through an old resolver handle violates `NoOldHandleRetarget`; the observation must be attributed to the runtime in the current slot, not to the stale resolver runtime.

A sealer must merge `_ckpt` by semantic maximum rather than write back a stale sampled body, because stale write-back can regress the base to 0 and make the next mount report an empty namespace over live data.
A CAS ref-prefix enumeration can omit durable ref-log objects: Probe A observed two holes at 16:47:38 that were missing from the pre-fold scan while HEAD verified both objects as present.
B207 was fixed by re-resolving referencing refs in `runFsck` when the initial HEAD is absent; only a current ref over an absent object is classified as dangling.

With the cleanup budget temporarily forced from 5000 to 2, `ManifestCleanupDrainsEntireRoundWithNoSkips` reproduced the leak class by deleting 2 of 5 manifest bodies and leaving 3 survivors; the test passed after the cap was removed.
resolveWedgeOnce must recheck the exact stored admission generation, transaction or operation identity, and bytes under state_mutex after I/O before adoption, acknowledgement, or unwedge
Stage B must require a named R3 sabotage/control pair covering delete-before-adoption and nomination-contaminates-B2 or unmatched-remove variants before C++ implementation
PartManifest.payload_digest is persisted but is not generally validated by Store::readManifest, so it is not currently a complete integrity guarantee
B1 and B2 are undefined for repaired and certified-void records when logs_applied counts only fully folded listed logs and repair paths bypass TxnApplyLedger::open
Fsck can report clean after an incomplete hot frontier because it silently skips absent snapshot logs and disappearing covered logs and cannot detect a whole omitted namespace
RefTxnId allocation can wrap ref_sequence at UINT64_MAX, making a real log id indistinguishable from a seal anchor; the protocol also needs prev < txn_id, cycle detection, and a resource bound
A NeverBorn recovery seal needs a specified zero sealed_from exception and seal-aware fsck handling; otherwise a healthy pool whose newest snapshot is synthetic remains unchecked
An absent _seal_latest cannot prove clean history because deletion, rollback, or loss can make a published authority appear absent; absence must be a hold or corruption condition
After any ambiguous send, a later definite rejection does not prove a ref ID is reusable because the earlier request can still land and occupy the key.
When an ambiguous ref append's exact GET remains absent, the current wedge can remain Unresolved forever and keep the namespace unavailable until an externally induced remount.

Incarnation-qualified physical keys alone do not make a hot-reader catalog mismatch rejection guarantee true because a reader without a catalog read, local fence transition, or bounded refresh cannot observe a remote replacement.
Path reconstruction is fragile because the abstraction boundary erases the MergeTree object structure, requiring independently evolving path grammars to continue agreeing.

If `Gc::fold` reads a record only when its key appears in the round's LIST hint, a durable checkpoint-committed ref log omitted by LIST is treated as absent, leaving the namespace held and making the frontier incomplete so destructive work is suppressed.
Issue `B140` was caused by `reuseBlob` transferring a blob hash without transferring its `cas_owner` protection, allowing GC to delete a blob still referenced by a committed part.
An asynchronous condemn-marker write failure must not be swallowed: graduation to `delete_pending` requires confirmed durable `Condemned` evidence, otherwise the entry carries to a later round.
An acknowledged-then-lost `INSERT` was fixed by closing the disk transaction in `renameParts`, making the part durable before the Keeper commit that acknowledges it.
Concurrent FETCH fan-out can tear the shared `detached` ref on `LocalObjectStorage`, because readers race an in-place truncating rewrite; S3 PUTs are atomic and do not have this specific tear.

A concurrent ref drop during mutable-only commit can throw through `MergeTreeTransaction::afterCommit`, whose `noexcept` boundary calls `std::terminate`; the race needs a recoverable no-op or an earlier detection path.

`RunRef::checksum` is serialized but not validated by consumers, while block and footer CRC32C remains the only checked streaming corruption guard; removing CRC32C before enforcing the run checksum would weaken detection.

`RunFileReader::next()` can read past a block when an unchecksummed `rec_count` is inflated; the fix must cover the whole block header with CRC and use bounds-checked reads with exact-consumption validation.
The `allow_stale` resolve path can use a ref dropped up to the 200 ms cache TTL ago, but no assertion enforces that `shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` is shorter than GC condemn-to-graduate latency.
The flat-combining write queue can block every writer queued on one `(namespace, shard)` behind a stalled leader, and a transient leader failure can fail the entire carved batch.
An incorrect `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` can cause a later GC round to delete still-referenced objects because the rebuilt baseline drives subsequent retire decisions.

Before the fix round, the post-listing post_listing_cut.life_index.resolve(candidate.life_id) call was uncaught, so an ambiguous catalog life ID threw CORRUPTED_DATA and aborted fsck instead of recording a lifeless_keys finding; the corrected code catches CORRUPTED_DATA, records the key, and continues.

Deriving baseline cursor authority from the full successor set incorrectly treats a catalog-only row as a parent cursor and bypasses `CasRefGc.BaselineGuardRefusesWhenSnapshotSurvivesWithoutLogsOrCursor`.
Resolving a namespace from the current catalog on every stale read lets a stale reader observe successor bytes; retaining the open-time `NamespaceLifeId` prevents that defect.

Capturing only a namespace name in a table-file `CaInlineWriteBuffer` and resolving it during finalization can change life 2's token and replace `life-2-stable\n` with `life-1-delayed\n`; retaining the open-time `NamespaceLifeId` prevents this defect.

Routing `CatalogAfterListBackend`'s simulated concurrent catalog probe through `CountingBackend::get` caused `CasNamespaceJanitor.PostListCatalogCutProtectsConcurrentCreationWithOneGet` to observe two gets instead of one; the probe must use `InMemoryBackend::get` and document the intentional bypass.
Using early projection or sub-part commits to make staged files readable creates windows in which orphan temporary metadata or blobs can remain after an exception.

A borrowed `ThreadGroup` can outlive its parent counters when asynchronous or background work retains the query thread group after the query ends, causing use-after-free in parent counters or memory-tracking corruption.

`LocalObjectStorage::listObjects` could throw a filesystem exception if a file disappeared between directory iteration and the subsequent `file_size` or metadata stat, whereas an object store would omit the vanished object.
`MergeTreeDeduplicationLog::addPart` and `dropPart` could dereference a null `current_writer` in a release build because they relied only on `chassert`.
Single-table `SYSTEM` commands that cast directly to a table must unwrap `TableProxy` first; otherwise a `DETACH`/`ATTACH` followed by `SYNC REPLICA` can fail even without CAS.
A buffer-constructor deadlock affected the rename forwarder; the rename forwarder was reverted while the mutation forwarder remained and was covered by test 05021.

The in-memory part image without a carried-forward projection can cause `MergedBlockOutputStream.cpp` to finalize checksums from the wrong image, `MergeTask.cpp` to make the wrong projection decision, and `DataPartsExchange.cpp` to omit the projection during fetch.

The `registerCarriedForwardProjectionForCA` workaround bypassed the disk transaction and led to B63, where a carried-forward projection had `rows_count=0` and a `SELECT` silently lost part of an aggregate.
`LocalObjectStorage::tryGetObjectMetadata` must treat directories as non-objects and a file or directory that vanishes during metadata lookup as `nullopt`, matching object-store snapshot semantics.
A child `ThreadGroup` must retain a `parent_thread_group` `shared_ptr` so the parent remains alive while child trackers point to it through raw pointers.
`MergeTreeDeduplicationLog::addPart` and `dropPart` must replace the release-no-op `chassert` with a fail-closed `LOGICAL_ERROR` when `current_writer` is null.

An R5-round review found a CRITICAL trust-flip bug where finding #19's guard made `CasProbe` vacuous on Native S3 pools: wrong-dialect probe tokens were being rejected locally before ever going over the wire, at three call sites in `CasProbe.cpp:93,143,172`; the fix applies a live-dialect probe at all three sites plus a reachability test that pins non-vacuousness.

A two-model adversarial consult found that E1's fail-closed elision (obsoleted by E2 since the ownership check became O(1)) traded away fail-closed behavior on the core invariant: a double-owner input can silently drift the owned-manifest index, and a drifted index lets `LiveAppend` manufacture fresh invalid durable history, risking GC premature delete.

An xhigh two-model review found E5's fast path unreachable in production flush: the `working` copy held a second reference to the base, keeping `use_count()` at 2 so the unique-owner fast path never fired and the slow O(N) path always ran; fixed by an xfix round (item A, working-lifetime) making the 1700x speedup real, confirmed by a paired ProfileEvents counter in the follow-up soak.

A codex-only finding in the xhigh review identified that the rename-forward change in `StorageTableProxy` caused a Buffer-constructor DEADLOCK, requiring the rename forward to be reverted (xfix item D).

A StorageProxy virtual-forwarding audit found roughly 60 unforwarded virtuals (about 45 that must be forwarded), including a CRITICAL silent-empty `backupData`; `mutate` forwarding was correct, rename forwarding moved to `StorageTableProxy`, and `detach` forwarding was dropped.

Three distinct lazy-proxy bugs were found during this round: (1) `StorageProxy` forwarded `mutate` but not `checkMutationIsPossible`, so a lazy proxy rejected all mutations (`MATERIALIZE TTL` -> `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`); (2) the proxy's cached metadata lacked TTL info, breaking `MATERIALIZE TTL` a second way after the first fix; both were fixed and validated by the narrowed stateless test 05021.

The current fsck oracle assumes a snapshot ID is also a log ID and silently skips a recovery seal on that assumption, rather than reporting the skip as checked; and repeated per-held-namespace anchor/repair GETs on every folding round are rate-bounded only by the scheduler, with no cumulative bound or backoff.

SEC-4: a pool-write-capable party (or a corrupt/huge object) can place a valid-CRC, valid-framing but enormous shard or manifest directly in S3; decoders (`decodeRootShard`, `decodePartManifest`) validate magic/version/CRC/journal-integrity but a valid giant body still allocates on decode, causing OOM in readers and the GC folder (GC folds whole journals). Recommendation: enforce absolute decode-side size/element caps independent of the write path, and stream large journals in the fold.

SEC-5: key builders route through `checkNamespace`, `namespaceFileKey`, and `mountpointObjectKey`, which reject empty segments, the reserved `_files`/`_manifests`/`_precommits` names, `..`, leading/trailing `/`, and `//`, but `checkNamespace` itself does not reject a `..` segment; this is safe only because the backend is an object store with literal (non-normalized) keys, so a filesystem-backed or path-normalizing backend would be vulnerable to traversal. Recommendation: reject `..` in `checkNamespace` so the invariant does not silently depend on backend key semantics.

The CA transient-classifier audit flags two ErrorCode-consistency mistags on the Mount plane: `CasServerRoot.cpp:261`'s 100-attempt CAS loop is coded `CORRUPTED_DATA` while sibling sites use `ABORTED`, and `:241` bundles `ContainerAbsent`/`AccessDenied`/`Indeterminate` together as corruption; both are contained but inconsistent.

D1 (definitely duplicated): 412/PreconditionFailed detection is reimplemented 3-4 times (`S3::Client::RetryStrategy`, `removeObjectIfTokenMatches`, `copyObjectConditional`) via `getExceptionName()=="PreconditionFailed"` or message-string matching; a differently-worded store body could silently misclassify a conditional-write outcome at any one site.

D3 (mostly duplicated with meaningful differences): three separate conditional-write retry regimes exist for the same class of operation — `CasRequestController` (ref lane: single-attempt client, budget, fence-gated, resolve-before-reissue), plain-object `casPutObject`/`casRemoveObject` loops (`MAX_CAS_ATTEMPTS=100`, default retry policy), and `CasBuild`'s local loops (`max_attempts=8`) — and only the ref lane implements the lease-deadline model; the plain-object gap is a real hazard.

D9: `ObjectStorageBackend` implements overlapping token-policy logic (native ETag vs emulated vs Generation) independently across `head`/`list`/`casPut`/`deleteExact`/`supportsListTokens`, corroborated by a past real incident (the `EmulatedSingleProcess` list-vs-head token mismatch); this is called out as the highest-value consolidation target in the report.

Risk register #8 (Medium, confirmed): the destructive `GC REBUILD` verb (which overwrites `gc/state` and, when no disk is given, loops over ALL CA disks) shares one access right with the benign per-round `GC` verb (`AccessType.h:351`; `InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp:1004,1010`), so an operator cannot grant "run a round" without also granting disaster-recovery rebuild, and a broad accidental `SYSTEM ... GC REBUILD` rebuilds every pool. Suggested action: a dedicated access right; consider requiring an explicit disk for rebuild.

Risk register #13 (Med-Low, confirmed): `WriteSettings.h:36-63` adds six S3 knobs including `shared_ptr<const S3::Client> s3_client_override` to a hot, widely-included, copied-per-write struct, whose `operator==` compares the pointer — this creates refcount traffic on hot write paths, surprising equality semantics, and a wide recompile blast radius. Suggested action: measure; consider a narrower CA-path-only struct.

The claim that a rewritten CAS `fsck` oracle is "seal-aware" is overstated: current `fsck` discovers snapshots and logs solely via untrusted `LIST`, silently skips namespaces when expected evidence is unavailable, and has no `unchecked` term for a missing or pointer/seal-mismatched authority, so it could be implemented by special-casing synthetic snapshot IDs while still accepting a listed ghost as clean.

Fetch-by-relink has no retention pin: the sender is fire-and-forget and releases the source part while the receiver's `precommitAdd` edge-PUT can stall, so if the source part goes Outdated and GC completes at least two folds before the edge lands, the sender's blob is reclaimed while the receiver's build still promotes successfully, yielding a committed manifest naming a deleted blob discoverable only by fsck; this is the umbrella review's top blocker (risk score 85).

An explicit `<use_fake_transaction>true</use_fake_transaction>` on a `content_addressed` disk is silently honored, causing `createTransaction()` to return a per-file autocommit `FakeDiskTransaction` with no commit point and breaking atomic manifest/ref publish; proposed fix is to throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` at registration when the key is explicitly true on a CAS disk.
A live ref must resolve through present keys; an absent key is a surfaced storage exception rather than a silent empty read (INV-NO-DANGLE).
CasRequestController::putIfAbsentControlled gates every attempt by the fence and remaining deadline, resolves uncertain writes by exact GET, and treats differing existing bytes as CORRUPTED_DATA.
Build::promote validates the manifest, checks the precommit owner, revalidates required blob leaves, and publishes the precommit-to-committed binding only after those checks.
GC must not delete an object while any session pin or committed reference names it, preserving `INV_NO_LOSS` and `INV_NO_DANGLE`.
Deterministic GC artifacts such as in-degree runs and fold seals must be byte-identical on collision, otherwise GC fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A crash before the round CAS leaves the prior generation authoritative; the next pass reruns from a fresh attempt and previously issued exact-token deletes are idempotent through `NotFound` or `TokenMismatch`.
Source-edge activation is set union and removal is set difference, so refolding either operation is idempotent.
Any clamp anomaly sets `suppress_destructive` for the pass, preventing graduation and pending or exact-token deletes until a clamp-free pass.
A retired entry whose in-degree recovers above zero is spared even when it is already `delete_pending`.
If an exact delete reports `created_delete_marker = true`, GC throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` because versioning tombstones can violate `INV_NO_RETURN`.
A rebuild over trimmed journals fails closed with `CORRUPTED_DATA` when no healthy adopted baseline exists, rather than silently under-counting live edges.
GC ordering is biased toward over-counting: crashes may delay reclamation, but must never make GC under-count a live reference.
A point-in-time `HEAD -> 404` is not durable absence; unreadable bodies clamp the fold and any clamped pass suppresses destructive decisions.
Per-hash metadata is an advisory freshness point-read, not the blob lifetime linearization point; exactness remains with the in-body incarnation tag and exact-token body delete.
Backend tokens must satisfy `head(k).token == prior get(k).token` only when the bytes are unchanged; this contract makes token-based decoded-shard caching safe.
CA tests write objects through the same production codecs used by readers, so the fixtures exercise real format round trips rather than white-box state pokes.

The test suite scripts concurrency hazards through backend subclasses and does not use sleeps to reproduce races; only `gtest_cas_part_folder_access.cpp` and `gtest_cas_ref_writer.cpp` use real `std::thread`.

CA tests are single-process, single-threaded, and clock-free for GC scenarios; genuine concurrency correctness rests on backend primitives, TLA+ models, and integration or soak tests rather than gtests alone.

`CaIncarnationCore.tla` proves `INV_NO_DANGLE`, `INV_NO_LOSS`, `INV_NO_RETURN`, and `INV_JOURNAL_COVERAGE` across adversarial writers, GC leaders, split-brain, resurrection, overwrite, and trimming scenarios.
A writer publish gate must consult durable `deadTok[h]` as well as in-flight retired state; consulting only retired state can admit a physically dead token after deletion.
The build-root model proves that both structural build-root reachability and fail-closed commit are necessary to prevent adopted-blob dangles; either half alone is insufficient.
`CaB140DangleMerge.tla` proves that trim gating and storing the fold cursor with committed snap edges are jointly necessary and sufficient to prevent trim-before-durable dangles.

`CaGcAckFloorZombie.tla` proves that two-phase `delete_pending` is required when two leaders interleave: a deposed leader may execute only deletes justified by pending state published before its pass.
The safety floor must be latched no later than the fold cut; reading it after the cut could graduate over a commit invisible to that pass's in-degree view.

`CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla` proves the root-local part-manifest invariants including no dangle, no loss, no return, journal coverage, single ownership, manifest-body validity, in-degree correspondence, and attempt-scoped visibility.
Only the adopted attempt's artifact may be consulted by GC decisions; a deposed leader's artifacts must remain reader-invisible.
A clamped GC pass may hold back a landed reference, but must declare the clamp and suppress graduation and pending deletes until a later clamp-free pass consumes the held reference.
`ca-fsck` classifies a live ref naming a missing object as `dangling`, which is an `INV-NO-LOSS` violation and the only hard reachability class.
A persistent `unaccounted` object outside the whole GC view is anomalous under INV-2, while an object created and dropped between rounds may be transiently `unaccounted`.
`ca-fsck` audits ref streams arithmetically using dense IDs `1..T` within `(namespace, writer_epoch)` and exact-key reads starting at `_ckpt.checkpoint`'s successor.
The GC safety assertion is `{preview deletes} ⊆ {ca-fsck unreachable}`.
Positive scenarios assert that `system.content_addressed_log` contains no `read_missing`, `dangling_access`, `corrupt_dangle`, `corrupt_decode`, `snap_journal_incoherent`, or `exception` events.
`readManifest` fails closed with `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` and `INV-NO-DANGLE` when a live ref names a missing manifest.
`readManifest` rejects a body whose self-described ref does not match the journal `ManifestRef` or whose `root_namespace_id` does not match the owning namespace with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A live committed manifest ref structurally protects its referenced blobs from GC because the fold cannot mark them zero-in-degree, and deletion additionally waits through condemn and `delete_pending`.
The current CAS safety model assumes one-live-object semantics; versioned-bucket marker stacks and version-specific conditional behavior are unmodeled.

CAS failure handling is conservative: lost folds, stale snapshots, duplicated records, and crashed leaders can only postpone reclamation because in-degree is an idempotent set of source edges rather than a counter.

The CAS safety triad is no-dangle, no-loss, and no-return: live references resolve through present keys, deletion requires durable retirement and later zero reachability with the exact token, and a retired `(kind, hash, token)` cannot become a valid dependency again.
An operation with an uncertain conditional-write outcome is treated as `PrecommitState::Uncertain`, which behaves as `NotAttempted` for admission and as `Durable` for cleanup.
`writer_epoch` is durable-monotone and never reissued, and every re-materialization of a fixed `(namespace, shard)` carries a strictly greater incarnation to close ABA.
CAS crash safety is intentionally asymmetric: every crash point may leak objects, but no crash point loses acknowledged data or creates a dangling reference.

A writer that adopts a blob token must have observed a non-`Condemned` marker after its precommit edge became durable, so the next GC fold can spare the blob; a resurrection changes the token and makes a stale `deleteExact` return `TokenMismatch`.
`writer_epoch` is durably monotone, while `build_sequence` resets on process start; global ordering is the lexicographic pair `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)`.

GC computes `suppress_destructive` once from anomalies, carried holds, and incomplete frontiers, and threads it through merge, ref cleanup, and namespace janitor so destructive decisions cannot diverge.

The planned shard incarnation is the existing `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` pair, represented as `ShardIncarnation`, with `{0,0}` meaning unstamped; a recreated `(ns, shard)` must receive a strictly greater pair under `INC-MONO`.
The planned ref-shard reclaim is fail-closed on a concurrent revive: an append changes the token, `deleteExact` returns `TokenMismatch`, and the shard survives with its new content.
A revive append after a shard tombstone changes the object token, so `deleteExact` returns `TokenMismatch` and the shard survives; an idle-but-live empty shard without a tombstone is retained.
D1 requires `THM-NO-RETURN`, `INV-NO-DANGLING`, `INV-NO-ABA`, and `INV-NO-BLOB-LEAK`; the last requires every `-1` edge to be folded before its carrying shard is deleted.

Copy-forward verification requires a valid envelope, matching object kind, and recomputed logical hash equal to the key hash; any mismatch or 404 is fail-closed, with corruption reported as `CORRUPTED_DATA` and a lost-race 404 as `ABORTED`.

`CaGcAckFloorCore` models copy-forward as minting and binding a fresh incarnation only while the blob is present and the current token is visible in the writer's loaded retired view; there is no absent-source copy-forward arm.
The ack-floor redesign rejects old schema versions fail-closed: schema versions are bumped, malformed data yields `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and future versions yield `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
A GC pass must durably write retired-list and snapshot runs before the `gc/state` CAS that publishes `round := K`, so any reader observing round K can load retired-list version K.

A mounted writer acknowledges a GC round only after it has loaded that round's retired list, drained all old-view `mutateShard` calls, and installed the new view; the advertised `observed_gc_round` never exceeds the installed and drained view.
GC fence-outs complete before discovery and their writers' last commits are therefore durable before the sweep begins.

A pending delete is terminal: a pending entry with recovered in-degree is spared and logged loudly, while re-executing a pending delete is safe at any leader staleness; a failed CAS cannot publish a zombie leader's fresh decisions.

A delete at pass K is safe because a writer with view `V ≥ condemn_round` sees the retired token and recreates it, while a writer with `V < condemn_round` must have been terminated or fenced out before the sweep and its commits are folded into the same merge.
The heartbeat drain proves that a server advertising `observed_gc_round = A` has no in-flight commit using a view below A.
Streaming run reads verify per-block and footer CRCs and treat a short or truncated stream as `CORRUPTED_DATA`, never adopting a partial parse.

If `snap_generation > 0` but the adopted fold seal, a referenced run, or a referenced retired object is absent or corrupt, GC must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` rather than treating the artifact as an empty baseline.

The rebuild is live-conservative: events after a shard read remain above the recorded cursor for the next regular round, a live precommit with an absent body clamps the cursor below its transition, and new condemnations wait for mount acknowledgements past the rebuilt round.
The GCS dialect throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` for an `If-None-Match` value other than `*` and for a non-numeric `If-Match` value, rather than silently changing conditional semantics.
The GCS dialect throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before sending a conditional `CompleteMultipartUpload`, identified as POST with an `uploadId` query parameter and no `partNumber`.

`RunFileReader(Backend &, const String & key)` treats an absent run, truncated stream, or CRC failure as `CORRUPTED_DATA`; the borrowed constructor is a zero-copy `std::string_view` over caller-owned bytes.

Before applying each queued closure, the leader snapshots the in-memory `RootShard`; if the closure throws, the snapshot is restored, that promise receives the exception, and the remaining batch items continue.

The load-bearing GC safety invariant is: no destructive decision is ever made on a not-fully-folded snapshot; any pending-delete graduation forces a FOLD before deletion so a protective `+1` is observed.

The required `CaGcRoundDeferCore` TLA+ gate must establish `NoOverDelete` and `EventuallyFolded`; sabotage allowing graduation on a stale snapshot must produce a `NoOverDelete` counterexample, and sabotage removing the defer bound must produce an `EventuallyFolded` counterexample.
The mount protocol invariant `FENCE-COSTS-EPOCH` requires that no write lands under a `(uuid, epoch)` incarnation after that incarnation has been fenced.

The TLA+ gate requires the old adopt path to violate `NoPermanentWedge` and same-epoch resurrection after a fence to violate `FenceCostsEpoch`; the fixed model must permit fence-to-new-epoch remount recovery.

S35 rapid same-name rotation preserved the resurrect invariant: no dangling content, reclaimable residual drained to zero, no revived condemned object, and the final recreated table remained queryable with replica agreement.
The force-Read guard never reclaims a live precommit: a build at or above the floor, a future epoch, or a missing watermark is spared, and `Build::promote` remains a fail-closed backstop.
A lost R5 round CAS may repeat the same force-Read and exact precommit removal, but the fold cursor advances past the removal transition so the `-1` is folded only once.
The `SkipParksDeadPrecommit` TLA+ bug configuration must violate `LiveDeadPrecommitReclaimed`, while the fix configuration with watermark-dead force-Read must satisfy it under weak fairness.
The resurrect fix must not condemn a current blob with `cur_edges > 0`; that case remains on the existing `spared` or recovery branch.
The resurrect-reupload rule is idempotent under R5 retry because it is a pure function of the edge stream and current HEAD, and an existing entry for the current token is not reset or duplicated.
The event sink is best-effort and does not participate in CAS decisions or block them, so adding lifecycle events does not change protocol safety.
`decodePartManifest` rejects an entry whose path is less than or equal to the preceding path with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, thereby rejecting out-of-order entries and non-adjacent duplicate paths.

An idempotent `republishRef` re-drive compares destination and source manifest entries, re-syncs destination mutable files when needed, and drops the source only when content matches; differing content raises `ABORTED` and leaves the source intact.
The Phase 2 style guard is a best-effort textual check that rejects raw committed-ref mutation tokens in wiring files while exempting `Core/` and `CachedPartFolderAccess.*`.

Every retained-view hit first re-resolves the ref and validates equality of `(manifest_id, mutable_files)`; an exact match returns the view without a manifest operation, a mutable-only mismatch clones around the same decode, and a manifest mismatch rebuilds the view.

`ForceFresh` and `StrictValidate` never serve a retained view; `ForceFresh` re-proves the manifest body through `readManifestShared` on every call, while `StrictValidate` also never retains the result.
Missing refs and failed view builds are never cached; views above `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` are served but bypass retention.

With retention disabled, answers and the read call graph remain identical to the existing behavior; with retention enabled, only manifest-body liveness validation on validated `CachedForLoad` hits is deferred.
Mutable per-part answers always come from the freshly resolved `Resolved::mutable_files`, never from an unvalidated retained view.
`ForceFresh` always invokes `readManifestShared`, whose mandatory manifest `HEAD` re-proves body existence while a matching token can reuse the decode without a `GET` or re-decode.

`republishRef` uses a fresh source read; when the destination is already committed it compares content, re-syncs mutable files, and drops the source for equal content, while a different-content destination is a conflict.
The write ordering `precommitAdd`, blob validation, then `promote` is unchanged by the facade, and no cached view is used as write evidence or reachability state.

The wiring style rule forbids the tokens `->dropRef(`, `->updateRefPayload(`, `->dropNamespace(`, and `->promote(` outside `CachedPartFolderAccess.*`; `Core/` is exempt because it implements the protocol.
A view is published only after `readManifestShared` validates the body, and fill failures propagate as exceptions and are never cached.
Write-path source reads use `ForceFresh` and re-prove the manifest body with a mandatory `HEAD` on every call, so write evidence is never taken from a retained view.
The cache is process-local and non-durable, adds no TLA+ transition, and participates in neither publication nor reachability decisions.
A different committed manifest at the destination of Build::promote is a reachable durable conflict and must be refused with ErrorCodes::ABORTED, not LOGICAL_ERROR.
The TLA+ model's RefFreeFor guard permits a ref to own at most one committed manifest, so the C++ promote guard is a model-alignment requirement.
republishRef must not drop the source when the destination is committed to different content; it throws ErrorCodes::ABORTED instead.

PROMOTE-OVER-COMMITTED-LEAK is a liveness and space leak rather than a dangling-reference or data-loss violation; INV_NO_DANGLE, INV_NO_LOSS, and INV_COMMIT_FAILCLOSED still hold in the described failure.
The combined changes preserve INV_NO_DANGLE and INV_NO_LOSS; a different-content republish conflict fails closed without silently losing the source content.
The EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE conclusion is that publishStaging orders stageManifest → precommitAdd → putBlob → promote, so every blob observation occurs after a durable protecting edge.
A tokened blob condemned between putBlob and promote must be resurrected from the writer's own source so an ordinary CA-over-S3 INSERT succeeds without exposing a retryable ABORTED to the client.
Tokened resurrection runs only after the promote owner-liveness check, so an abandoned build aborts without producing an orphan incarnation.
Resurrection is placed after owner-liveness validation rather than in the pre-pass because the build's precommit is the tokened blob's only protection.

The tokenless promote backstop applies to present-condemned tokenless adoptEvidence leaves revealed after the in-closure refresh; absent tokenless leaves and unknown leaves still fail closed with ABORTED.
isCopyForwardableTokenless is true only for a Blob dependency with no token, representing adoptEvidence with an independent committed owner; tokened or missing dependencies are not copy-forwardable.
The absent branch remains unchanged because copyForwardFromCondemned requires a present object to GET and cannot recreate an absent tokenless blob.
The copy-forward backstop is idempotent under CAS retry and terminates because a successful copy-forward produces a fresh token absent from the fixed in-closure snapshot.

The production publish order stageManifest → precommitAdd → putBlob → promote is the EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE protocol: every blob observation occurs under a durable closure edge naming the manifest's hashes.

Adoption of an existing incarnation requires a durable precommit closure, so the Phase A plan adds chassert(precommitted) to both observeAndAdmit overloads; fresh uploads before precommit remain watermark-protected.

The formal Gate A positive model removes tokened revalidation, the view drain, and writer fence refresh while preserving invariants; order, adoption-check, and non-tokened presence-check sabotages must fail.
The reduced promote loop skips tokened leaves as edge-protected, but checks every non-tokened leaf for presence and fails closed on absent or condemned no-dep leaves.
The Phase A ordering guard treats dedup adoption before durable precommit as unsafe because an adopted blob carries the original writer's build_id and is not covered by the newborn-debris watermark.
Promote K3 point-reads metadata for non-tokened leaves; absent bodies still abort, condemned copy-forwardable leaves are copied forward, and tokened leaves remain skipped under EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE.
The invariant `INV-META-BODY` requires a present meta to imply a present body; it is maintained by creating bottom-up (body then meta) and deleting top-down (meta then body).
Every meta write carries a fresh `incarnation` `UInt128` nonce because content-derived S3 etags would otherwise allow a clean-meta ABA; the nonce makes each meta encoding and etag unique.

The TLA+ model `CaMetaDescriptorRaw.tla` is the authority for the writer-GC state machine, whose required transitions are `FreshUpload`, `Adopt`, `Resurrect`, `BirthCompletion`, `GcCondemn`, `GcSpare`, and `GcDeletePhaseA/B/C`.
Replay starts at `folded_seq + 1`, or at sequence one for an empty base; a gap before the maximum observed sequence is an exception that disables destructive actions for that namespace.
Every reachability effect in a candidate ref base is resolved before the fold seal, destructive GC action, and generation `CAS`; any required manifest-body failure aborts the whole attempt.

If a late manifest-body failure occurs after tentative output runs or reachability artifacts are finalized, those artifacts remain unadopted; the fold seal is not written, `gc/state` is not changed, and no destructive GC or writer-log deletion occurs.

The failure table requires a lost GC generation CAS to leave the attempt unadopted and delete no logs, while a stop after a successful CAS treats the new fold as authoritative and repeats covered-log deletion later.

Source-edge run readers fail closed on `key_schema != 1`, wrong run kind, unknown `token_type`, truncated payload, an edge row at `source_id = 0`, a sentinel row at nonzero `source_id`, unknown row type, or duplicate sentinel; missing adopted seal or missing `condemned_summary` at `snap_generation > 0` makes `graduationDue` return true.

The fold seal is the exact recovery base: it names every authoritative base `RunRef`, its checksum, and non-overlapping row-key bounds, and consumers never select a run merely because `LIST` found it.
A writer-log key conflict is an exception and must not be bypassed by skipping to a later sequence.

A corrupt adopted fold seal or ref run causes writable startup and destructive maintenance to fail closed; an unknown future format version produces the repository's future-format exception rather than falling back to an older format.

The typed source-edge run opener rejects an active edge with `source_id = 0`, a zero marker or condemned row with a nonzero source id, unknown row types, and more than one sentinel row per blob with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
Each shard's `CondemnedSummary` is derived solely from that shard's written run bytes, making the summary a deterministic function of the sealed artifact.
New seals have a total `condemned_summary` map over `gc_shards`; pure ref-carry shards copy the parent summary entry verbatim, and a missing entry is an integrity signal rather than zero.
For `snap_generation > 0`, a missing or undecodable adopted seal, or a seal without `condemned_summary`, makes `graduationDue` return true so the forced fold surfaces the integrity loss.
Destructive redelete actions may execute only for `delete_pending` rows read from the prior durably adopted run; a fresh `head_blob` observation is write-only until durable adoption.

Run and seal adoption continue to use `putDeterministicArtifact`: `putIfAbsent` collisions must be byte-equal or fail with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and `gc/state` adopts the generation and attempt through the seal.
A divergent artifact under an attempt-pinned key is rejected as `CORRUPTED_DATA`; the round aborts and the next round refolds under a fresh attempt instead of adopting stale edge bytes.
Once a hash is `Condemned`, observing `Clean` means either the condemned body is absent or a writer has already changed its incarnation token.
`BlobRef` may be constructed only when the algorithm and digest are born together at the write mint or read together by a durable-form parser; all other code copies an existing `BlobRef`.

Before writing any blob, manifest, or ref naming an algorithm, a node must durably CAS-union that algorithm into `algos_used`; the union loop rereads after conflicts and recomputes from the fresh value.

A validator with a stale local `algos_used` cache refreshes `_pool_meta` on every miss for a known algorithm and accepts only if the authoritative set contains it; an unknown-to-the-build algorithm remains `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
With no `blob_hash` setting or with `cityhash128`, blob hash values and keys remain byte-for-byte identical to the existing cityHash128 convention.

Snapshot coverage and GC fold coverage are independent: snapshot `X` lets a writer omit logs through `X`, while the folded cursor proves that those logs no longer need to be read for edge discovery; both are required before log deletion.
Snapshot and log bodies are deterministic and repeat key-derived identity fields; a snapshot is never renamed or copied when created, and logs remain under their original keys.
Snapshot rows are sorted by canonical bytewise `ref_name`, then by `ManifestRef`; duplicate rows, noncanonical names, invalid identifiers, and unsorted fields are rejected.

State-growing operations are admitted only if both the encoded snapshot and encoded namespace-removal transaction remain below their respective hard budgets; an oversized operation fails closed before object creation.

Replacing an existing committed ref requires an explicit `owner_transition` removal before promotion; silent displacement is forbidden because GC derives edges from explicit operations rather than state diffs.

If a selected snapshot or tail body disappears between recovery `LIST` and `GET`, the writer restarts with a fresh `LIST`; absence is not corruption and recovery never falls back to an older plausible snapshot.

An uncertain ref-log create is never treated as failed when an exact-key GET finds absence; the append lane remains wedged until identical bytes are observed, a whitelisted definite rejection is proven, or the writer unmounts.
A `PreconditionFailed` ref-log create always resolves through exact-key observation: identical bytes mean success of the earlier attempt, while different bytes are corruption.
The snapshot published by the writer is an integrity oracle: fsck can replay the snapshot and tail and compare the deterministic bytes, with divergence treated as corruption.
GC resumes pagination exactly after the last key returned by the previous page; opaque continuation tokens are usable only when the backend documents equivalent positioning semantics.
A ref fold aborts without partial delta or destructive authorization when a key, transaction body, operation, or input-visibility condition is malformed or ambiguous.

Namespace cleanup deletes only exact keys captured by its own enumeration and never uses a prefix wildcard; after recreation, exact keys from the removed incarnation cannot name newly created objects.
If the existing destination is condemned, resurrection copies from the writer's staging object and never reads or copies the condemned blob key as the resurrection source.
Recovery must not promote a precommit whose staged copy is not verifiably complete; it must re-drive promotion from the surviving staging object or abort recovery of that build.

The add-only TLA model requires both adopting `FoldRound` and deposed `FoldAbort` folds to leave meta unchanged on spare, while only writer fresh-upload or resurrection may change present `Condemned` to `Clean` with a token change.
The add-only safety gate uses split two-leader actions—capture snapshot, execute pre-CAS side effects including `deleteExact`, then attempt adoption—to expose stale-redelete races.

The two-leader regression must verify that after a spare the marker remains `Condemned`, a writer resurrects to a fresh token `t2`, and stale `deleteExact(t1)` returns `TokenMismatch` or `Replaced` without removing the live body.

The Phase 2 SHA-256 implementation must port the `CasGc.cpp` condemn sweep and `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites in the same change that widens the digest; otherwise the pool silently leaks every SHA-256 blob.
The reader recovery invariant is `Replay(newest visible valid snapshot, surviving later logs) = Replay(full history)` for every reader that completes, including readers that restart.
Cleanup must not remove an object still needed by a completing reader, and namespace recreation must not observe a stale delete.
An exact-key GET that finds absence after an uncertain put-if-absent result never yields `DefiniteFailure`; the controller may retry the same key within budget.

Ref log decoding rejects zero transaction-ID fields, exceeds neither `ref_txn_max_ops` nor `ref_txn_max_bytes` except for the removal-class exception, rejects non-canonical clean relative ref names, and requires body `ns` and `txn_id` to match key-derived fields.
`applyRefLogTxn` applies a complete transaction atomically or throws, never mutating state on throw; the same validator is used by writer, recovery, fsck, and snapshot construction.

Ref state rejects birth on a non-`Removed` table, requires exact owner bindings, preserves promote atomicity, checks expected manifest refs for payload updates, requires owners to be empty after removal transitions, rejects operations after `Removed` except birth, and requires strictly increasing transaction IDs.
The replay equation requires replaying a snapshot followed by its tail to equal replaying the full log history, and `admits` enforces both snapshot and removal admission budgets incrementally.
Malformed ref keys or bodies abort ref folding for the round without adopting a partial delta.
ABA is impossible in the immutable namespace model because `RefTxnId` is strictly increasing and a recreated namespace cannot reuse an ID matched by a stale delete.

Five gap tests closed the audit's unit-testable fail-closed gaps: the CAS GC baseline guard, one-operation-per-ref batch cut, mountpoint get/remove round trip, unknown owner-kind rejection, and invalid ref-log-body fold abort.
The audit found no remaining fail-closed branch that was both unit-testable and unjustified after the gap tests and integration/soak dispositions.

CAS correctness requires distinguishing definitely committed, definitely not committed, and uncertain protocol-write outcomes; generic SDK retries cannot provide that distinction for conditional CAS writes.
A client timeout proves only that ClickHouse received no conclusive response within the wait; it does not prove that S3 rejected or cancelled the request, so the object may appear later.

For `putIfAbsent`, an internal retry can create the object on the first attempt and then receive `PreconditionFailed` on a repeated `If-None-Match: *`, so `PreconditionFailed` must be resolved against the exact key and deterministic body.

An uncertain tokened conditional overwrite cannot always be resolved as success because a later overwrite may have replaced the intended bytes; ambiguity must fail closed when the intended state cannot be proven.

Before each CAS retry, the controller records the preceding exact outcome, checks operation and lease budgets plus the local fence, resolves an uncertain result when required, and preserves the same key, body, conditions, and writer epoch unless a new logical operation is explicit.

After an uncertain immutable conditional create, identical deterministic bytes at the exact key prove commit, a different valid object is a conflict, absence permits another attempt only after budget checks, and read errors or unprovable identity remain uncertain.
The final local fence check prevents an ACK after observed fence loss but cannot atomically prove that the remote mount object was still owned when another S3 object was created.

`Build::observeAndAdmit` must throw `LOGICAL_ERROR` when the ADOPT path is reached with `precommitted == false`; fresh uploads before precommit remain legal because their watermark protection differs from adopted incarnations.

`Store::reportImpossibleInterference` responds to impossible foreign bytes with a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, `ForeignInterference` event, `tripMountLost()`, and `scheduleRemount()`, while a single background diagnostic GET stays off the caller's critical path; a ref-lane wedge also fails closed before allocating a new id.
Foreign-write detection on the CAS hot path is limited to incidental signals from operations already being performed, such as conditional-PUT token mismatches or unexpected bytes at an owned key.
An incidental interference signal causes `LOGICAL_ERROR`, a fail-closed mount fence, and bounded remount recovery; diagnosis may issue requests only in a background path.
A failed recovery-seal PUT prevents the mount from opening writable; the next attempt allocates a fresh epoch and a strictly larger seal ID.
The writer retains `fence_ok` verification before and after every conditional ref-log PUT, including `CasConditionalWriteFenceLostPostWrite`.
A CAS repoint uses the standard Build path, preserving precommit-before-observe (`EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE`), and old manifests are retired by the normal GC fold without introducing a new GC invariant.
A same-manifest re-promotion remains an idempotent no-op, and a different committed ref still raises `ABORTED` when `allow_repoint` is false.

A compressed CAS object uses one zstd frame with XXH64 checksum enabled; its declared content size is checked against the per-type cap before allocation, and a body-magic mismatch with the policy is `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

CAS integrity checks include key-to-body binding where applicable, seal-held whole-file CityHash128 verification for runs at the end of every full read, and regeneration and verification of padding zones to prevent smuggling.

The format test harness covers round-trip, golden text, truncation at every line boundary, future `v`, wrong `type`, tolerant and strict unknown keys, critical `!` keys, duplicate keys, over-cap declared sizes without allocation, and padding or banner mutation; uncompressed bit-flip detection remains delegated to `fsck` and MergeTree load checks.
Phase-1 decoding maps malformed, truncated, over-cap, wrong-type, duplicate-key, and whitespace input to `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and future `v` or unknown `!`-prefixed keys to `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.

Every v3 format registers a `FormatBatteryCase` containing an id, stored-byte encoder, decoder, and optional canonical-text golden; the battery exercises decode-of-encode, truncation, future-version, wrong-type, and leading-garbage failures.

A live snapshot has no `remove_txn_id`; a removed snapshot has `remove_txn_id` and empty `committed` and `precommits`; and every snapshot satisfies `snapshot_id >= *sealed_from` when `sealed_from` is present.

`decodeRefLogTxn(data, expected_ns, expected_txn_id)` and `decodeRefTableSnapshot(data, expected_ns, expected_snapshot_id)` reject a body whose namespace or transaction/snapshot ID differs from the key-derived expected values.
Refsnaplog codecs retain validation of canonical clean `ref_name` values and non-zero `ManifestRef` and `RefTxnId` fields.
Blob-meta lifecycle operations use the backend etag `Token` for conditional updates; they do not use a byte comparison of the encoded meta body.
Malformed, truncated, wrong-type, unknown-state, and over-cap blob-meta input maps to `CORRUPTED_DATA`, while a future `v` or unknown `!` key maps to `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.
Every `cas_run` consumer must stream the whole object, accumulate its checksum, and verify it against the referencing `RunRef.checksum` before the records affect a deletion decision.
The `cas_run` checksum uses the same streaming chained CityHash128 routine on write and read, covering the entire stored object including header, records, and trailer.
`cas_run` is `RecordStream` with `Strict` keys and `PinnedRaw` storage, and its byte-deterministic output is required for `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption.

Malformed, truncated, trailer-count-mismatched, checksum-mismatched, unknown-kind, out-of-order, duplicate, and over-`line_cap` run data is rejected with `CORRUPTED_DATA`; future `v` and unknown `!` keys use `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.

String sorting by `(b, s)` must equal the existing binary `(algo, digest, source_id)` byte order; fixed-width lowercase hexadecimal rendering makes this property hold by construction and it is pinned by a golden test.
Part-manifest integrity is provided by the whole-object zstd frame, `payload_digest`, the entry-count trailer, and fsck rather than the deleted per-block `CRC32C` framing.

Part-manifest encode and decode enforce canonical paths, ascending order with duplicate rejection, valid blob references, mutually exclusive Blob/Inline placement fields, namespace/ref matching, and entry/encoded-byte caps.
`payload_digest` is CityHash128 over the canonical text body with the digest rendered as zero hex during hashing, and decoding recomputes and verifies it.
The envelope decoder parses JSON from byte zero and then requires every remaining pre-newline header byte to be an ASCII space; any other byte or missing newline is `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
Bad envelope type, truncation, pad violations, duplicate keys, and over-256-byte headers are `CORRUPTED_DATA`; future `v` and unknown `!` keys are `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.
The superseded protocol's zero-gap ordering was `[sender-ref] → [sender-ref + pin] → [pin] → [pin + receiver-ref] → [receiver-ref]`, so the sender created protection before releasing its part.
Decomposition follows state and lock ownership boundaries: every component owns its mutexes wholesale, no lock changes the state it covers, and no lock-acquisition order changes.
The renames change only C++ identifiers and file names; persisted bytes, key layouts, log/error/event text, ProfileEvents, metric names, and protocol vocabulary remain unchanged.

The source-layout invariants prohibit persisted-byte, key-layout, log/error/event, metric, lock-coverage, and lock-order changes, and require move commits to contain no content edits and content commits to contain no moves.

`DiskObjectStorageTransaction::commit` and `tryCommit` validate in release builds that an eager transaction has an empty `operations_to_execute` queue, preventing methods that bypass `dispatch` from silently creating a second timeline.

There is no atomic backend operation spanning several refs, so existing commit-time compensation for refs newly created before a later publication failure remains necessary; dropping an existing ref is not valid rollback for a failed repoint.

The retry-later helper covers the escaping retry-later throws in `CasPartWriteTxn.cpp` and `CasRefLedger.cpp`, while internal `ABORTED` control-flow signals, startup/decommission failures, live-lock brakes, genuine content conflicts, and GC-internal values retain `ABORTED`.

The retry-later API has both `throwCasWriteRetryLater(const String & why)` and `makeCasWriteRetryLaterExceptionPtr(const String & why)`, and both carry `ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR` with the same message shape.

The one-pipeline transaction design gives each CA disk transaction one mutable transaction-private overlay updated at call time, makes every transaction-scoped read observe it, and reserves durable publication for disk `commit`.

The only permitted shared-code changes in the one-pipeline design are `transactionIsStagingOverlay()`, `tryCreateWriteBuffer(...)`, the generic `dispatch()` funnel, and a release-build assertion that eager transactions leave `operations_to_execute` empty.
For a staging-overlay storage, `dispatch(op)` invokes `op(metadata_transaction)` immediately; for ordinary object storage it appends the operation to `operations_to_execute` for FIFO replay.
The release-build eager-transaction guard throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before publication if `transactionIsStagingOverlay()` is true while `operations_to_execute` is non-empty.
Recovery correctly fails closed when a foreign seal object is undecodable; the zstd frame check closed the earlier F3-1a decode-laxity finding rather than introducing a product bug.
If a CA clone fails, its self-created transaction is undone and the exception is rethrown; a successful clone is then opened with `create(..., initialize=true)`.
Both L1 identity routing and L2 whole-part atomicity are required: L2 alone still collides on ref `moving`, while L1 alone still autocommits per file and can raise `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

`RefTableState::committed` is replaced by an ordered COW map so copies in `CasRefLedger::flushRefBatch` and `applyRefLogTxn`/`admits` cost O(touched rows), while behavior, snapshot bytes, admission decisions, and errors remain byte-identical.
`RefCowMap` has no mutable-reference iterator: a row update must copy the found `RefCommittedRow`, modify it, and write it back with `insert_or_assign`.

The ref-table isolation invariant remains that leaders copy state under `state_mutex`, validate and PUT without the lock, and reacquire the lock only to install the result, while readers hold the lock for their entire in-place read.
Sharing `std::shared_ptr<const map>` introduces no new locking: trial copies retain private overlays, installation swaps state under `state_mutex`, and detached snapshots encode outside the lock.
The CAS event sink must be installed in `PoolConfig` or `Pool::open` before `mountWritable` starts the renewal thread; `setEventSink` is retained only as a pre-open test hook.
A content-addressed transaction that fails `commit` is terminal: later `commit` or `tryCommit` must throw `LOGICAL_ERROR` instead of retrying the failed object.

The S22 fix must route blob-meta conditional writes through a controller that resolves ambiguous attempts by token and byte checks, and must propagate exhaustion rather than swallow a metadata write failure.

The `hasActiveTransaction` guard is required because `commitTransaction` resets the storage transaction pointer and calling it on a closed transaction raises `LOGICAL_ERROR`; repeated `renameParts` is therefore idempotent.

A `renameParts` failure occurs after parts are already `PreActive`, so rollback removes the in-memory parts and their disk data; a partial multi-part publish is covered by the same rollback, and no Keeper multi is reached.
In CAS tests, `LOGICAL_ERROR` is reserved for invalid states or violated invariants and must not be used as a generic injected-operation failure.

The CAS mount and part-write negative tests classify foreign lease incarnations, foreign-writer renewals, double starts, post-`abandon` operations, cross-namespace manifests, unsatisfied dependencies, and wrong blob sizes as genuine invariant violations rather than transport faults.
The S38 clamp-starvation condition is fail-closed and does not revive or delete anything, but it violates the observability contract that a late log is reported.

The project's `LOGICAL_ERROR` policy reserves it for gross application-invariant violations; ordinary external failures should use an appropriate external-error code, while an external condition that makes ClickHouse state violate an invariant may still be a valid `LOGICAL_ERROR`.

The CasJsonWriter migration keeps validation such as `checkCanonicalRefName`, `checkManifestRef`, and `checkBudget` in place; `CasJsonWriter` performs no I/O and only propagates `std::bad_alloc` from buffer growth.

A debug-only `chassert` recomputes both body totals from scratch after each applied operation, and randomized property tests compare the incremental sizes with full encoder sizes to catch counter drift.
A debug-only recompute-and-compare `chassert` and the existing `AdmitsExactnessPropertyTest` are required to detect drift between incremental counters and full encoder sizes.

The promote-path counter decrement may occur before a later validation exception because `applyRefLogTxn` mutates a scratch copy and installs it only after the whole transaction succeeds; the partially updated scratch state is discarded on failure.

CAS recovery retries `NETWORK_ERROR` and transport-class S3 errors from direct `backend.list` and `backend.get` calls, but fails fast on `CORRUPTED_DATA`, format/decode errors, `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and the `kRefRecoveryMaxRestarts` runaway brake.
The fix plan rejects skipping `promote`'s manifest GET-back because CA storage treats rereading and re-proving identity as a fail-closed invariant.
Malformed CAS outcome-log digest widths must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` before `fromHex`, rather than exposing `BAD_ARGUMENTS` from the hex decoder.

The `RefTableState` experiments must not change persisted or wire bytes, the canonical ordered snapshot encoding, ref-log transaction format, legal state transitions, transition preconditions, or ledger concurrency design.
A not-fully-mounted CAS disk must not be treated as erased: benign-absent answers are safe only after positive establishment of data erasure; otherwise access must fail loudly.

The six CAS operation classes are Factory, Probe, ContentRead, Write, Remove, and Admin; transient and `IdentityLost` states throw for every class except Factory, while `Vanished` Probe answers absent/empty and Remove succeeds as a no-op.

The CAS phased engine preserves per-part `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` ordering, so the EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE invariant remains intact while work is reordered across parts.
If a submission group unwinds while outstanding, pending items are canceled under the queue mutex and already-carved items are awaited before teardown so their closures cannot dangle.
An operation that exceeds the 4 KiB per-operation cap fails alone, so a pathological head item cannot cause an empty-flush livelock.

On a phased-commit failure, every pool task and outstanding ledger item is drained before rollback; exact rollback uses `dropRefIfMatches` and a preallocated POD outcome slot published immediately after durable promote.
Each worker writes rollback information into a preallocated, index-addressed per-part slot so a post-promote `bad_alloc` cannot lose a durable ref's outcome.
Worker tasks capture only non-owning transaction references, and rollback or destruction may begin only after an exception-safe join has drained every worker.
Exact rollback records `{ns, ref, manifest_id, created}` inside the serialized `appendRefOps` builder and removes a ref only when `dropRefIfMatches` still sees that exact manifest.
The first worker exception is rethrown after draining; later worker exceptions are logged and swallowed so they cannot mask the first failure.

After any `appendRefOps` return or throw, every `RefMutationItem` must be done or owned by a still-blocked caller; no item may remain pending for a future leader after its caller's closure state is gone.

The phased cross-part design preserves semantic equivalence rather than byte identity: folded ref-to-manifest bindings, manifest entries, blob payloads, in-degree, and clean metadata must match, while ref-log packing, IDs, timestamps, and incarnation tags may differ.

A batch failure preserves sequential atomicity semantics: earlier members may remain committed, `renameParts` throws before Keeper block-ID registration, and rollback uses exact-manifest matching rather than inventing a new all-or-nothing promise.

In the central CAS operation gate, `Factory` is never gated; `TransientNotLive` and `IdentityLost` throw for every other class; and `Vanished` returns truthful absent/empty for Probe, typed errors for reads/writes/admin, and no-op success for Remove.

The parallel-write implementation plan requires an exception-safe drain before rollback: all task handles, outcome slots, and exception slots are preallocated, and the drain waits without calling throwing `get()`.

`PartWriteTxn::mergeBlobUploadResults` must prevalidate all results and apply them with build-and-swap or equivalent no-throw replacement so a merge failure leaves the transaction build completely untouched.

If any blob-upload task fails, the join drains every task and merges no result; publish fails, the precommit is abandoned, staging cleanup follows the existing policy, and successful sibling bodies remain ordinary GC-reclaimable zero-edge debris.
Upload tasks must capture owning or value state, and the callback runner must be scoped so its destructor drains tasks before captured storage is destroyed, including when dispatch throws.

If chunk N fails after earlier chunks committed, chunks before N remain successful and only chunk N plus the unattempted remainder fail; after any committed chunk, later exceptions are contained within the tenure and a leader whose item already succeeded returns that committed result.
A vanished selected ref-log object causes candidate discard and a bounded fresh LIST restart, whereas decode or apply corruption discards the candidate and propagates immediately without re-listing.

`DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` covers only the pre-existing candidate move and atomic tail-counter bumps; candidate construction, logging, events, survivor completion, exception creation, notification, and `materializeCommitted` remain outside the deny region.

A gate-1 `yes` proves the exact transferred manifest was the committed binding at confirmation, no removal was durable or in flight past admission, no durable-but-unapplied transaction existed, and the responder was the live writer; any removal appended afterward is ordered after confirmation.

`CasEventDispatcher::emit` serializes concurrent delivery, invokes the sink outside its mutex, and queues reentrant emissions for the already-running drain loop instead of recursively acquiring the delivery lock.

`uploadPendingBlobs` uses `ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal` inside the scope owning captured storage, propagates the query `ThreadGroup`, always drains tasks including dispatch throws, and performs no partial merge on failure.

The stage-1 carve test seam distinguishes plan allocations (`PlanSeenRefs`, `PlanBatchGrow`, `PlanReserveOwned`) from publish and validation phases, and requires every plan-phase failure to leave already-selected items either retryable or never popped.
