The TLA+ gate adds the authoritative epoch-presence guard, decommission terminal-mount policy, and negative controls showing that removing the guard or blindly minting epoch 1 over a live mount reaches a same-pair two-writer state.

The `PostDurableInstall` `CarvePhaseForTest` hook fires after `putIfAbsentControlled` returns `Committed` and before the candidate is installed, providing the test seam for post-durable failure injection.

`RefApplyState` has `Clean`, `ApplyPending`, and `Poisoned` states; a successful commit, conclusive PUT failure, definite failure, or absent wedge resolution clears `ApplyPending`, while a post-durable install failure transitions to `Poisoned`, which later successful flushes must never clear.
A `Yes` from `confirmExactRef` excludes stale-cache, pending, in-flight, wedge, poison, and fence ambiguity but does not prove that the recovered runtime replayed every durable journal record.

The confirm fence rule is evaluated last, so gate-0 `No`, gate-1 `No`, and every `Unknown` reach the same caller outcome; future code must not treat `No` as authoritative without hoisting the fence rule.

The stage-1 composition review found no Pool/ledger/dispatcher/semaphore lock cycle; the dispatcher releases its mutex before invoking the sink, and condemned-local admission ends before event and metadata work.

A committed transaction that produced blob deltas but whose deltas reached no shard reducer causes the GC round to throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` before the seal write, adopt nothing, reclaim nothing, and direct recovery through `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD`.

The CAS ref-chain design makes absence decidable through per-namespace contiguous ids, point reads, conditional writes, and an exact committed-through frontier; a pool-wide allocator that creates per-namespace gaps makes absence undecidable without a certificate.

A missing intermediate epoch or a checkpoint frontier after an `EpochSeal` in the same numeric epoch is `CORRUPTED_DATA`; consumers must not shortcut a fold, recovery, `fsck`, or orphan sweep around it.

A checkpoint snapshot may never name an `EpochSeal`; before accepting a nonempty `checkpoint_snapshot_id`, every reader exact-reads the matching `_log` and rejects an `EpochSeal` before reading the same-id `_snap`.

An opaque life id with no catalog entry is inert debris and never evidence of damage; the only exported catalog deletion transitions are exact-CAS cancellation of a complete terminal `Creating` row and exact-CAS deletion of a complete, unheld `Removing` row with cleanup evidence.

A writer-mount recovery that may have landed beyond the durable frontier exact-reads one deterministic successor; matching valid bytes permit the fenced checkpoint contribution, different bytes or an invalid successor are corruption, and absence permits the conditional retry.

The delete-site in-degree re-read is normative: a `+1` landing after a namespace probe but before condemnation can be protected by the existing `deleteExact` liveness re-check even when no rematerialization path runs.

REBUILD reconstructs ref-life coverage and edges from the catalog, exact `_ckpt.committed_through`, and finite arithmetic tails, condemns nothing, and preserves holds; fsck uses the same catalog-authoritative universe and treats `chain-broken` as fatal in both summary and exit code.
`waitForWriteGrace` never changes admission: after it returns, the caller must capture a fresh `fenceGeneration()` and run the unchanged fence check.

When grace is enabled and a Mode 1 remount completes, the plain write captures the new fence generation; when Mode 2 re-arms via `setMountDeadline`, the generation remains unchanged and the write proceeds under the same valid incarnation.
With `write_grace_ms == 0`, the extra wait call early-returns, generation capture and admission checks occur as before, and the observable write behavior is byte-identical to the pre-feature path.
`slotOccupy` leaves byte comparison and operation adjudication to its caller; a conflict followed by a missing occupant is `Unresolved`, never fabricated `Created`.
`CasRefProtocol.cpp:433` rejects any applied ref id that is not the successor of the greatest applied id with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, enforcing dense per-epoch streams on the read side.

Before a wedge retry acts on I/O results, it re-acquires the install lock, verifies the exact stored generation/transaction identity/bytes, and reruns `checkFenceOrThrow`; stale results perform no acknowledge, unwedge, or install.

Recovery captures one `admitted_generation` and uses it for slot occupancy, `_ckpt` publication, and the final install-lock fence check; it must not install state after a fence bump during the I/O window.

The temporal deletion closure has three normative arms: newly condemned blobs are not deleted in the same round, source-backed/tokened adoption rematerializes a fresh incarnation protected by token mismatch, and tokenless relink orders receiver `+1` durability before source-edge release.

Fsck walks arithmetic streams, reports physical objects above `_ckpt.checkpoint` as uncommitted debris, reserves `unchecked` for genuinely unproven cases, and returns clean for a healthy arithmetic pool.

The `_ckpt` object is a fixed-size product of scalar monotone facts whose encoded size is `O(1)` in the number of refs, files, transactions, and writer epochs; maps and other cardinality-growing state belong in separate immutable objects or ledgers.
`Poisoned` is distinct from wedge: it means a durable transaction may be missing from the cached view, so it blocks snapshot publication and triggers re-recovery.
A namespace in `Creating` must not publish ref data; stale-`Creating` reconciliation is permitted only after the creator fence is terminal and must use an exact observed-entry token.

A reverse catalog index maps every catalog state to `life_id -> NamespaceLifeId{name, incarnation}`; a duplicate current `life_id` is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, makes both rows unresolvable, and causes catalog mutations, REBUILD, decommission, fold adoption, and destructive GC to fail closed.

Recovery grounding uses `_ckpt.checkpoint_snapshot_id` as the only snapshot base and `_ckpt.committed_through` as the inclusive frontier; it never derives a base, genesis, frontier, or stop condition from stream `LIST` results.
`Creating` namespaces are never recovered or published; `Live` and `Removing` namespaces require a readable `_ckpt` with `life_epoch`, and a life id absent from the catalog is not recovered.

A committed ref chunk follows log `PUT` → `_ckpt.committed_through` GET/CAS → in-memory install and acknowledgement → allocation of the next id; an unresolved log/frontier window remains in `NeedsRecovery`.
The writer/recovery model replaces `nextId` with a single at-most-one in-flight `pendingSlot`, derives `NextSlot` from durable and sealed ids, and tracks ambiguous attempts in `ambiguousEver`.

A recovery walk uses `ckpt` as its base, advances by arithmetic expected-id reads rather than listing hints, and closes the epoch by occupying the next slot with a seal or adopting a matching in-flight straggler.
The model's cleanup guard permits only log ids at or below `ckpt.base`, and a missing base with an unchanged checkpoint token is corruption rather than a normal recovery outcome.
A fold hold set after an expected-next 404 with a higher durable id may be cleared only by folding through the offending id; clearing it on another absent probe is unsafe.
A different token at an immutable manifest key is illegal ABA; the sweep retains the manifest and surfaces the condition instead of deleting it.

The parser remains catalog-independent and accepts a dead incarnation's syntactically valid key; fold and REBUILD filter keys whose parsed incarnation does not match the current catalog entry before grouping.

Stage A treats the ref stream as arithmetic: transaction ids are dense within each `(namespace, writer_epoch)` pair, recovery advances by exact-key reads, and a dead epoch is closed by an `EpochSeal` at the exact id that the dying predecessor's next PUT would have used; object listing is only a hint.

When the survivor object is removed from the refused recreated prefix, the same prefix bootstraps cleanly and the new life starts empty rather than absorbing the old life: checksum `0\t0` versus life 1's `200\t18123181848219261492`.
Recovery uses `_ckpt` plus an arithmetic tail and seal CAS-walk; LIST seeds candidates and supplies `_cleanup` markers but is never a census of durable records.

The ref-chain model covers per-namespace contiguous ids, in-band `slot-occupy` seals for epoch transitions, `_ckpt`-gated recovery, arithmetic fold intake, a durable frontier hold, and LIST-as-zero-trust-hint behavior through named sabotage and control configurations.

The v9 regression pair establishes that treating a scan as truth breaks recovery (`CaRefTableSnapshotLogCore_sab_scanistruth` is red) while omitting all records from the listing is harmless under arithmetic intake (`CaRefDeltaIntakeCore_v9_hintomission` is green).

The Write plane cannot produce a destructive broken-part classification, the Mount plane's `MountFencedException` is caught at `CasPool.cpp:687`, and GC-plane exceptions are contained by `catch (...)` in `CasGcScheduler`.

`PrecommitState` must be set to `Uncertain` before the ambiguous precommit append; weakening that ordering can make a later-resolved committed precommit look never committed and cause its body to be deleted.

A no-transmission proof downgrades `PrecommitState` to `NotAttempted`; the proof is recorded at one transmission point by setting `RefMutationItem::attempted` immediately before `putIfAbsentControlled`, rather than enumerating refusal sites.

The controller's pre-attempt fence and deadline checks can reach the marked path without sending to the backend; when `attempts_sent == 0`, `unresolvedProvesNothingWasSent` clears `attempted` and reports `NoAttemptSent`.

The attempted-transmission mark is set before the first attempt and is not reset by controller retries or later wedge resolution; a process death between the mark and the send deliberately over-reports rather than silently losing the release signal.

`armApplyPending` must be called inside a `state_mutex` scope immediately before the PUT and read under `state_mutex`; mutex ordering then guarantees that a reader after the arm observes `ApplyPending` and refuses, while a reader before the arm observes `Clean` before the PUT exists.

The apply-pending marker synchronization in the part-write seam is a prerequisite for removing the lane-quiescence refusal; the redesign cannot ship if the refined TLA model does not pass its stale-cache gate and expressiveness requirements.

A relink confirm requires two independent defenses against a stripped mode parameter: `content_addressed_answer=proven` must be present because offers never emit the answer cookie, and `assertEOF` must reject a non-empty offer body.

The receiver promotes only when the confirm body is empty, `content_addressed_nonce` matches the fresh nonce, `content_addressed_answer` is exactly `proven`, and `content_addressed_identity` equals the held validator; any single failed condition is `Unknown`.

The lane-quiescence terms are safe to remove only after marker synchronization: a pending item is not durable, and each leader tenure's chunks close their own durable-but-unapplied window before the next chunk arms the marker.

The synchronized marker must be sufficient for a reader holding `state_mutex` never to observe `Clean` while a transaction is between its marker arm and install; this is an explicit requirement of the relink design even though the implementation belongs to the release-seam document.

S2 (`CaRelinkPromote::Unresolved`) always throws retry-later `NETWORK_ERROR` and never byte-fetches, because the earlier append may already have committed and a byte fetch could publish the part twice.

The core relink invariant is: adoption transfers liveness evidence, so the receiver may accept n blobs on one certificate of a committed binding, while the actor that removes that certificate must return per-blob evidence.

The relink TLA work must name `FreshCertifiedResponse`: the response acted on must have been produced by the sender for this request after T1, not replayed and not an offer mistaken for a confirm; the nonce and confirm-only answer plus `assertEOF` tests discharge that assumption.

The required apply-pending TLA refinement adds `sApplyPending` before `SenderDurable`, clears it atomically with the row update, requires `_sab_noapplypending` to find the stale-cache counterexample, and requires `_sab_stalecache` with the marker intact to pass; failure of the latter blocks implementation.

The relink model must express two mounts with equal `root_namespace` and different `disk_name`, with `_sab_barevalidator` and `_sab_nodiskqualification` both red, and must model a single leader tenure committing multiple durable transactions; unresolved promote remains the named assumption `UnresolvedPromoteNeverBytes` and is discharged by a direct test.
Stage-A `assert_no_leftovers` is narrowed only for the gated `unreachable:_manifests` family and counts/reports that residue; blob leaks, `unaccounted`, and `dangling` still fail independently.

The private relink vocabulary intentionally has no wildcard, comma-separated list, or weak-comparison grammar; every wire value is compared as one opaque token, and an `If-None-Match` or related standard conditional header selects nothing and certifies nothing.

A non-corruption exception from `classifyRefLogOccupant` leaves the lane `Wedged` with the exact attempt retained; because equal bytes are returned as `Ours` before the throwing decode, such an exception implies foreign bytes at a write-once key and cannot lose a durable own transaction.
If private candidate preparation throws before I/O, the lane remains `Wedged` and the runtime state is not mutated; decoding and applying target the private candidate rather than the runtime state.

The marker contract has two distinct obligations: `MarkerCoversDurableWindow` covers the entire durable-but-unapplied interval, while `MarkerSeenMatchesMarker` requires a reader acquiring after the arm to observe the armed value.

The relink safety theorem covers a landed `Unresolved` publication as committed even while the receiver remains in state S2; `rCommitted`, rather than only receiver state S3, is the theorem antecedent.
`Reason::RefusedPreAttempt` belongs to an `Unresolved` result, not to the `slotOccupy` exception path; the exception path never reaches the recheck block and does not set `reason`.
Before trusting a nonempty checkpoint base, recovery exact-reads and decodes the matching `_log`, rejects an `EpochSeal`, and then reads the same-id `_snap`; fsck applies the same exact-base check.
For identical backend objects, full, empty, partial, and reordered listings must reconstruct the same logical state with zero recovery LIST requests; forged listed snapshots are not observed.

Extracting `prepareRefChunk` must preserve backend request counts, fault and ambiguity semantics, the existing wedge protocol, allocation-free post-durable install regions, and post-durable fault seams; broad settlement rewrites are out of scope.
A stale namespace-file reader may return stale data or `NotFound`, but never data from a newer incarnation; a stale writer may target only its old incarnation and never write into the new one.

The confirm model proves custody-chain safety under the explicitly named assumption `CommittedEdgesAreGcVisible`; the sender certificate and GC contract are layered, with GC turning the certified binding into blob liveness.
No append begins outside `Ready`, and confirmation and snapshot publication are allowed only in `Ready`.
An empty `Builds` domain is semantically valid for `CaRefWriterCleanupCore`; an `ASSUME Builds # {}` must not be added merely to hide the defective TLC result.

The relink gate's three named assumptions are `CommittedEdgesAreGcVisible`, `UnresolvedPromoteNeverBytes`, and `FreshCertifiedResponse`; the first is discharged by v9 chain models, the second by relink spec §11 row 9 with an in-model sabotage, and the third by nonce and offer/confirm discrimination rows while replay generations remain transport-level.
A fresh catalog, life, and fence validation is still required immediately before every destructive delete even though deposited life identity provides the primary stale-pass isolation.
A `NamespaceLifeId` may originate only from catalog snapshot resolution; it must never be minted from a `RootNamespace`, LIST key, or path.

Current-life destructive cleanup must revalidate the exact life, catalog-entry token, and fence immediately before every per-key `deleteExact`; a token change before the first delete permits no delete, while a change between two deletes refuses the second.
Within one operation, multiple life resolutions must use the same `CasRefCatalog::Snapshot` and must not observe different catalog snapshots.
Fresh namespace-file resolution accepts only a `Live` catalog life and rejects `Creating`, `Removing`, or absent catalog rows without durable mutation.
A reader holding a life from before same-name rebirth can return only the old life's bytes or absence; it must never return successor-life bytes.
Delayed inline finalization cannot change the successor life's token or bytes; it writes only under the captured old life or fails with a typed stale-write exception.

An unresolved every-attempt writer grant may correspond to a durable precommit; failure queues an in-memory cleanup duty while the mount lives, `Adopted` resolution requires exact owner removal before retirement, and `Rejected` resolution proves that no owner exists.

CAS recovery uses the exact checkpoint frontier through `chooseRecoveryGrounding`; `hint_log_ids` is not used, and neither `CasRefProtocol.cpp` nor `CasRefLedger.cpp` enumerates the ref stream with `Backend::list`.

The writer cleanup seam enqueues an uncertain or durable precommit duty without retiring its build sequence; a sticky queue-failure bit pins the cleanup floor, and all six mutating `ref_ledger` forwards in `CasPool.cpp` pass through `mutateRefsAfterWriterCleanup`.
Verification verdicts distinguish `done`, `rejected`, `stale`, `open`, `doc-fact`, `unverifiable`, and `ephemeral`, and verdict evidence is pinned to the checked Git commit.
The CAS reliability story is based on TLA+/TLC model checking, corner-case testing, and multi-hour chaos-tested soak runs.
A `done` verdict means implemented at HEAD and requires `file:symbol` or test evidence, while an `open` verdict means the claim is still actual and absent at HEAD.

A `rejected` verdict requires a conscious decision pointer and reason, a `stale` verdict requires what HEAD contradicts, and an `unverifiable` verdict requires an explanation of why code cannot check the claim.
Verification is scoped to claims that enter new documentation, enter BACKLOG as `open`, or justify removal; `ephemeral` and `history` claims are not verified against code.
Stale-but-honest reads create a true historical cut whose errors cause retention or delay, while a fabricated cut from omission under a seal can authorize unrecoverable destruction.

One CAS pool is one trust domain: CityHash128 and XXH3 are not cryptographic and deduplication is cross-tenant within a pool; multi-tenant isolation requires cryptographic hashing or trust-domain-scoped deduplication.

The fsck phantom-dangling fix re-resolves every referencing ref at both HEAD-absent branches; a missing blob is `dangling` only if a current ref still names it, not when the ref was legitimately re-published or dropped after the initial walk.
The CaIncarnationCore publish gate must consult durable deleted-token history `deadTok[h]`, not only the in-flight `retired` set.
A tree ref may be published only when all direct children are present and non-condemned at publish time, enforcing bottom-up `TreeDepsOK` construction.
Equality of an empty `CatalogUniverse` and empty `FrontierProven` is not sufficient destructive authority; an empty universe keeps physical condemnation and deletion suppressed.

Neither the pool-global round nor the incarnation alone is sufficient: dropping the newborn self-floor violates `INV_NO_DANGLING`, while dropping incarnation from the fold cursor permits an ABA dangle.

`AckedOpsAreDurable` requires every acknowledged operation identity to be in `durable`; with byte comparison disabled, `WedgeRetryOccupied` can falsely acknowledge a second same-generation operation from the first operation's bytes.
A `Live` catalog row is safe only when its life's `_ckpt` exists; this protects against both an over-broad janitor and a fenced or token-stale creator installing late.
A stale predecessor proof must not delete a successor in `Removing`; exact deletion must match life id, lifecycle state, and the full-catalog token.
Every checkpoint CAS binds an exact sampled token, so an intervening checkpoint update invalidates it, while an already-issued request may still linearize after a fence move.
An absent expected-next id is not a safe frontier in a sparse id space because recovery cannot distinguish a gap from the end and can install state missing every record above the gap.
The relink theorem is conditional on complete `LIST` discovery in the shipped pre-v9 GC; the confirm protocol itself cannot repair a journal-discovery hole.
A direct numeric epoch transition `E -> E + 2` cannot authorize recovery, fold, or destruction because the missing `E + 1` seal violates `INV_NO_EPOCH_SKIP`.
No path may lose acknowledged data or delete an object still named by a committed reference; any current gap must be named, mechanized, executable as a test, and fixed before release.
TLA+ conventions require `_sab_*` and `_bug` sabotage configurations to produce counterexamples, while a `violation` from `_witness_*` means the negated reachability state is reachable.
The pre-fold plan is keyed only by opaque life id, and stale full-catalog token/value, stale cut ordering, absent-listed classification, and identity-blind deletion are each independently unsafe.

`Occupied` with an `EpochSeal` terminates a concurrent recovery walk, while an operation acknowledged after a lost write is forbidden unless byte comparison proves that operation's bytes were durably written.
The only persisted format version field is the header `v`; readers reject `v > G_BUILD` with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION` before reading the body.

Deterministic formats such as `cas_fold_seal` and `cas_run` use strict keys and pinned raw encoding; a `putDeterministicArtifact` conflict is resolved by re-encoding at the version of the existing object.
A persisted key prefixed with `!` is critical, and a reader that does not understand it fails closed.

Every positive scenario requires replica-oracle SQL agreement, `clickhouse-disks cas-fsck --detail` with `dangling = 0`, and `clickhouse-disks cas-gc-dryrun` candidates contained in the quiescent `cas-fsck` unreachable set.

During precommit-first publishing, a durable precommit may name a manifest while blob upload is still in progress, so mid-write `fsck` and dry-run results are not hard correctness verdicts; structural assertions belong at quiescent checkpoints.
S07 requires a manifest-limit failure to return `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, publish no live ref to the rejected manifest, and leave only bounded reclaimable staged debris.
S27 requires duplicate or unstable root-shard LIST pages to force safe rereads and treat ambiguous keys as changed, preserving correctness while exposing extra `CASRootGet` cost.

The allocation-fault scenario S42 treats a post-durable-install allocation failure as allowed to fail queries but not invariants: after quiescence and restart, `fsck` must report `dangling=0`, `unaccounted=0`, and `stale_edge=0`, with every acknowledged insert present.
The replacement test `ManifestCleanupDrainsEntireRoundWithNoSkips` asserts that a five-manifest owner removal deletes all five manifest bodies in the same GC round.

`ForceFreshMutable` reads bypass retained views for mutable per-part files, `FreshForWrite` reads current committed state for write sources, and `StrictValidate` validates remote presence and corruption immediately for fsck/debug paths.
If an underlying CAS mutation throws, cache state and the caller-visible cache generation remain unchanged.
Mutable per-part file reads use force-fresh resolution and must not trust a stale retained view.
Cache fill and strict validation surface missing or corrupt manifests as exceptions, and payload reads still fail when a referenced blob is missing.
`PartFolderView` is a memoized result of validated CAS reads, is neither a source of truth nor durable state, and is not write-path evidence unless fresh evidence was requested.
The cache does not retain negative ref lookups or empty namespace results because a newly published part must not remain invisible.
The `PartFolderView` cache must never retain a decoded manifest that failed validation.

Backend safety depends on exact-token conditional delete: a DELETE If-Match token with a wrong token MUST fail, not silently succeed; this is probed at startup and the disk fails closed if the backend does not enforce it. Promote's publish-gate obligations (MR-1/MR-2/MR-3) apply only to the non-tokened evidence/copy-forward dependency subset since EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE: MR-1 consults durable deleted-token history, not only a cached retired set; MR-2/F1 re-validates the dependency's current physical state (still present, still carrying the originally-observed token, not merely 'not condemned when first seen'); MR-3/F2 requires bottom-up tree publish so a manifest may publish only when every direct child is present and non-condemned at publish time. A tokened dependency gets zero promote-time re-validation against any of these.

`INV-2` (precommit-first / reachability-before-content): the build-root precommit must be published before any pool content GET/HEAD/PUT of the build's content; the full write ordering stages blobs into local temp files, then makes the edge-bearing manifest body durable via `stageManifest`, then lands the owner event via `precommitAdd`, and only then do blob uploads reach the pool. A writer dying mid-upload therefore leaves blobs whose edges already exist in a folded body, so there is no structural 'orphan blob' class — an object in `blobs/` with no edge-bearing body in history should be impossible and fsck may treat one as an anomaly.

The design rule that generalizes the LIST-trust resolution: any input feeding an irreversible action must be structurally unable to authorize it wrongly, it may only delay it. A stale-but-honest observation is a true cut from the past whose induced errors fall toward retention/latency and are closed forward by ordering and a final re-check at the destructive site; a fabricated cut (omission under a permanent seal) corresponds to no point in time and can authorize destruction. LIST is only used in roles that satisfy this (work bound, witness set, genesis hint); the trusted verbs (exact-key reads, conditional writes) carry everything else.

The CAS backend contract's `TOKEN ⟹ CONTENT` requirement (a repeated token implies unchanged bytes) is the one item that cannot be probed cheaply and is therefore a documented, unverified assumption on every backend, not enforced by the capability probe.

CAS's transient-vs-terminal exception classifier separates a READ-plane and a WRITE-plane per an audit of every throw site tree-wide: the READ plane is the only one with destructive reach and had exactly two sites, of 106 GC-ref throw sites tree-wide 27 were transient (19 `NETWORK_ERROR`, 5 `INVALID_STATE`, 3 `ABORTED`); a write-once `ABORTED`-on-write-once site (718 occurrences) was judged a real defect while the deposition/fence family was deliberately left `INVALID_STATE` because recoding it to `ABORTED` would regress by escaping a backoff exemption.

CAS's single true read-side correctness hole (labeled X1/R1, "missing read"): a ref-less/cross-node reader resolves ref to manifest to blob-location at plan time, discards the manifest, then performs a deferred, unpinned blob GET later; if the ref is dropped and GC completes condemn to pending to delete before that GET fires, a committed datum becomes unreadable mid-query (`NoSuchKey`). This is bounded to the write/GC plane being otherwise loss-free; the fix direction is an ephemeral reader pin folded into the GC mark/ack-floor union, or bounding query lifetime below the condemn-to-delete latency.

CAS's security perimeter is exactly the S3 bucket credential: there is no intra-pool authorization, identities are self-asserted and unsigned, and blobs are shared pool-wide by content hash with no namespace in the blob key. Combined with non-cryptographic CityHash128 content-addressing and reads that never re-verify payload-against-key, this enables SEC-1 (High) collision poisoning: because dedup is HEAD-first and blobs are pool-global, an attacker who can craft a `CityHash128` collision can pre-seed a poisoned blob under the victim's future hash so a victim in a different table/tenant later writing the benign content dedups to the poison and reads attacker bytes, with all CRC checks passing (latent in a single-trust-domain pool, real the moment a pool is multi-tenant).

SEC-8: provenance (`server_id`, timestamp, op, `build_id`) and the `CasEvent` sink give a useful audit trail, but everything is self-asserted and forgeable by a pool-write adversary, so it is good for debugging and honest-fault forensics but not an integrity/attribution control against a malicious insider.

SEC-9: blobs are plaintext table bytes; confidentiality relies entirely on S3 SSE + bucket policy + TLS, and content-addressing also makes content equality externally observable (same content maps to the same key), which deployments with confidential data across tenants in one pool should assume as an equality-leakage risk.

The full set of code sites sharing the renameParts -> Keeper-decision -> parts-commit slot audited for the part-durability-before-Keeper-commit fix is: `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart` (INSERT, the only dedup-token site and hence the only silent-loss path), `renameMergedTemporaryPart` (merges), `MutateFromLogEntryTask::finalize`, `fetchPart`, `executeLogEntry`, `executeReplaceRange`, `replacePartitionFromImpl`, `movePartitionToTable`, `renameAndCommitEmptyParts`, and `createEmptyPartInsteadOfLost`; non-INSERT paths hit the same window but only cause replicated-log-entry re-execution churn, not acknowledged data loss.

The ref-chain complete-cut design's generation-change safety was confirmed to have no durable double-apply path: if the old PUT wins, the successor adopts it; if the successor's seal wins, the old PUT is rejected; if the generation changes before the old write is even sent, the old send is refused outright.

The recommended fix for the CAS `fsck` seal-awareness gap requires a point read of the authority for every known namespace, traversal of the complete seal-descriptor history, exact-`GET` verification of every referenced seal, and treating missing/malformed/regressed/mismatched pointer-vs-seal state as fatal `unchecked`/corruption rather than clean.

The inequality `min_ack ≤ K−1` prevents an entry condemned in pass K from graduating in that same pass, so the two-round condemnation pipeline follows from the round arithmetic.

The queue's TLA+ posture treats a batch as a sequence of today's transitions committed atomically; any crash or conflict leaves a durable prefix, and the reachable durable states are a subset of those available from fast sequential `casPut` operations.
The TLA+ mount model adds `GcFence`, splits adopt into GET and CAS steps, permits late renewal after expiry, and checks `FENCE-COSTS-EPOCH` plus eventual remount liveness.

The corrected replay implementation deletes public `ApplyMode` and keeps poison-on-throw in a private `RefTableState::applyTxnInPlace` reachable only from `replay`.

The planned parallel commit snapshots parts into an index-addressable vector, preallocates outcome and exception slots, dispatches bounded worker loops, waits with `wait()` rather than `get()`, and performs rollback only after the inner runner scope drains.

All CAS event emission routes through one reentrancy-safe serialized dispatcher, and ledger events are emitted after releasing ledger locks; per-component event locks are rejected because they can deadlock with reentrant sinks.
The ref-lane fix must land before publish-confirm work, and all three post-durable sites must install state without allocation: chunk commit apply, wedge-resolution apply, and wedge construction.

A `Poisoned` marker is not sufficient protection before the no-throw install fix: without that fix, later transactions could still publish a snapshot hiding a durable missing transaction, so poison must either follow A1 or become a hard per-namespace fence.
A decommission path must not blindly bypass the mount-presence guard: minting epoch 1 over a live epoch-1 mount would recreate the forbidden same-pair twin and defeat live-member refusal.

The ref-lane fix makes the interval between durable ref-log publication and runtime installation allocation-free at all three post-durable install sites, enforced by `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` and reinforced with an apply-pending poison marker.

`confirmExactRef` must try-lock `state_mutex` while holding the ref queue mutex; failure to acquire it is treated as `Unknown` so confirmation never blocks pool-wide append admission behind recovery I/O.
Wedge retry is demand-driven: a permanently quiet wedged namespace retries on its next caller or an independently occurring remount, because the unresolved operation was never acknowledged.

The lease-blip fix is classified as a robustness fix: the induced timing kept the part `ACTIVE`, produced zero CA-log events and no `part_log` remediation row, while the residual double-blip risk remains named.

The recommended transient-classifier fix is to add `throwCasTransientUnavailable` beside `throwCasWriteRetryLater` in `Backend/CasRequestControl.cpp:190-201`, minting `NETWORK_ERROR` for `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1111`, `:1163`, and `CasMountRuntime.cpp:106`; this changes no upstream files.

The apply-marker lock belongs at each call site rather than inside `armApplyPending`, because `forceWedgeForTest` already calls it while holding `state_mutex`; the helper remains `noexcept`, allocation-free, and lock-free with a documented locking precondition.
Recovery must not fall back to `hint_log_ids.front()` or fabricate `life_epoch` with `value_or`.
Fsck's namespace and life universe must come from one validated catalog snapshot; backend listings may discover physical objects within that universe or report extra orphaned objects.
GC, ref cleanup, namespace cleanup, fsck, and decommission should consume one immutable `GcNamespacePlan` or one shared catalog snapshot and must not independently re-read catalog state.

The catalog's advantage over LIST is atomic completeness as of one object-version cut, not freshness; protocol closes staleness after the cut but cannot recover a namespace never named by an incomplete LIST.

Canonical life-qualified objects whose life is not the current catalog life are inert debris; malformed or unparseable keys remain anomalies; an absent or undecodable initialized Stage-B catalog stops creation, removal, and GC.

The LIST-derived fsck snapshot oracle was removed; `FsckClass::SnapshotOracleMismatch`, its report fields, its hard-findings row, and the corresponding `CommandFsck` failure path are absent from production code.
Verification agents receive claim and cluster JSON but not the source documents; evidence must come from code at HEAD rather than from the statement that a document says the claim.
A random five-percent adversarial audit rechecks `done` and `stale` verdicts because a false `done` can lose work and a false `stale` can lose knowledge.

A reachable state handled by code must not be guarded by `chassert`: the handler is the fail-closed behavior, and an assertion above it otherwise makes sanitizer/debug builds abort while release builds execute the handler.

When a function's returned aggregate element type, member count, or member order changes, every structured-binding call site such as `auto [a, b]` must be audited because C++17 can silently rebind fields without a compile error.

The mount model's honest `RemintEpoch` path over-approximates production because it omits the code precondition `serverRootSubtreeEmpty`; the model's honest `FenceCostsEpoch` counterexample is therefore conservative rather than proof that production reaches the same state.

The recovery-generation model identifies an operation by `<< actor, generation, op >>`; using only `<< actor, generation >>` aliases distinct same-generation operations and can hide an ack for bytes that were never written.

The ref-lane implementation replaced nested apply-marker and durable-floor encodings with `RefLaneState{Ready,Writing,Wedged,NeedsRecovery,Closed,Faulted}`; confirmation is `Ready`-only and terminal `Closed`/`Faulted` states are non-retriable.
CAS correctness claims require an executable counterexample when a rule is removed; a green check that cannot go red is not evidence.
CAS operations must fail closed under ambiguity: an operation that may have landed must not be treated as one that did not.

`blob_storage_log` records object writes and deletes but not LIST calls, so the observed evidence bounds timing without identifying whether the listing failure was a dropped page, a boundary error, or another store behavior.
A `ca-surgeon` safety argument must be re-derived when the storage shape being changed is within that argument's scope.
The cache is a memoized access layer over already-valid CAS operations, not a new CAS protocol component.

The cache design keeps public APIs small, keeps cache code outside CAS protocol logic where possible, makes mutation side effects local, preserves the call graph when disabled, and does not weaken CAS invariants or TLA+ assumptions.
`PartFolderView` must not call back into `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`, mutate `Cas::Store`, or perform object-store I/O.

In disabled mode, `getView` still resolves refs and reads manifests, writes still use `CachedPartFolderAccess`, and correctness and side effects remain identical, but the one-`GET` performance guarantee is absent.
The cache facade erases the affected view after a successful `updateMutableFiles`, `dropRef`, `promoteBuild`, or `dropNamespace` operation.
Cache insertion captures a local sequence before loading and publishes the view only when that sequence is unchanged, preventing a stale in-flight read from repopulating after a local write.
The cache mutex must not be held during `resolveRef`, `readManifest`, `HEAD`, `GET`, or decode, and single-flight must be scoped per `(namespace, ref)` or `ManifestId` rather than globally.

CAS blob content hashes use CityHash128 consistently with MergeTree file checksums, while tree or manifest identity also uses CityHash128 where other higher-level identities commonly use SipHash128; the review recommends documenting or revisiting that choice under the collision model.
A valid successor seal must remain the conclusive rejection when an old I/O result returns after a generation bump, and the superseded runtime must not acknowledge, install, or publish it
RunFile block and footer CRC32C should remain until RunRef.checksum is either verified as a full-run artifact hash before trust or removed or demoted before release

CAS fsck classifies canonical physical keys absent from the catalog at a post-listing observation cut as soft FsckClass::JanitorPending, with report fields namespace_janitor_pending, namespace_janitor_pending_bytes, and namespace_janitor_pending_lives; these fields are excluded from kFsckHardFindings.

CasFsck.cpp uses observe-then-cut classification: it buffers canonical candidates during the physical LIST, reads a fresh catalog cut after listing completes, and classifies candidates against that cut to protect concurrent namespace creation.

The two holey-LIST tests `OmittedRemoveRecordIsSkippedForever` and `OmittedActivationNeverPermitsDeletingALiveBlob` are retained because they cover skipped-transaction retention-leak and data-loss behavior independently of probe A.

The anomaly and carried-hold terms in `suppress_destructive` are structural defense-in-depth: in current in-fold paths they co-fire with frontier incompleteness and cannot be isolated by the existing test seams.
`RefPlan` has a private mandatory constructor, is non-assignable, exposes const views only, and has neither mutable `foldState` nor a destructive `releaseFoldStates` operation.

The sole ref-plan builder consumes an rvalue `RoundInput` and moves its scan and catalog cut into `RefPlan`; fold, the store-quality probe, DEFER accounting, frontier/publication, and healthy rebuild receive the bound plan only.
Raw `RoundInput` construction is private to `Gc` and the narrow named `tests::buildRefWalkPlanForTest` wrapper, preventing arbitrary scan/catalog pairs from bypassing the production binding boundary.

The authoritative `CaRefLaneCore` model composes the existing single six-state append lane with a bounded identity/cache submodel containing two runtime ids, two durable life ids, one non-authoritative name slot, one old handle, immutable identity records, per-runtime cache/durable markers, one delayed-invalidation target, and fence state.
An already-issued stale request may land only while its adopted proof remains current; the B-drained takeover trace is a helping barrier rather than atomic revocation of an independent catalog CAS.
The copy `const RefTableState before = state;` in `E3AdmitsPreviewLeavesStateByteIdentical` must remain an independent snapshot because `state` is mutated later for byte-identical comparison.

The TLA+ model collapses the real `armMountFence .. noteRemounted` interval into one atomic reclaim action because the op gate refuses durable admission while the state is not `Live` and older fence generations fail revalidation.

Canonical catalog-absent objects are inert debris that must never damage data; fsck therefore needs a grammar-discriminated `janitor_pending` class rather than treating all such debris as a hard corruption finding.

On existing non-CAS disks, immediate local-filesystem visibility and object-storage parts represented as independent files generally prevented the weak disk-transaction contract from causing direct data loss, but MergeTree still depended on implementation-specific visibility and early sub-part commits.

CAS design work treats a proof of correctness as requiring an executable, reproducible counterexample: a test must be able to fail. A relink proved only by a flat blob count is worthless because a byte fetch onto a content-addressed disk also dedups and produces the same flat count, so that test cannot distinguish the mechanism under test from a working fallback.

CAS's documented deployment rule from the security audit: never share a CAS pool across trust domains until SEC-1 (collision poisoning), SEC-2 (dedup existence oracle), and SEC-3 (no intra-pool authorization) are addressed; the single highest-leverage code fix common to both the Jepsen-style consistency audit and the security audit is a `writer_epoch`-fenced shard CAS precondition, which simultaneously closes SEC-7 (NTP/pause-amplifiable fencing) and the J1/J2/J3 split-brain class.
The B140 dangle fix requires both build-root protection and fail-closed commit; the model found that either mechanism alone is insufficient.

The holey-list sabotage configuration `_sab_holeylist` of `CaRelinkConfirmCore.tla` violated `ConfirmedRelinkNeverDangles` with one incomplete LIST page, proving that relink confirmation is safe only conditional on LIST completeness.

A namespace can leave the old walk silent when `cursor == RefTxnId{}`, `listing.logs` is empty, and `checkpoints.life_epochs` has no entry; the old code skipped `while (expected)` with no anomaly, hold, or warning, while the current `!grounding` arm emits a warning and records `CheckpointUnusable` or a hold.
The TXN-final phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, recovered from five faults and three restarts, reported `ABORTED-retried INSERT=0`, and drained the pool to 256 bytes.
The S38 late-PUT fence test passed 19 of 19 verdicts and the real object store returned HTTP 412 for a straggler's conditional create at a sealed id.
`CaB140DangleMerge` passed its empty-`Trees` configuration `m_empty_trees.cfg` as green.
`CaIncarnationCore_empty_hashes.cfg` passed as green with `Hashes = {}`.

In the observed list-incompleteness occurrence, ref-log objects `0x1430c`, `0x1430d`, and `0x1430e` were uploaded in strict ID order at 16:47:19.211480, 16:47:19.212340, and 16:47:19.213680 respectively.
The first walk returned ref-log object `0x1430e` after its upload, but did not return the two earlier objects `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` even though they had been durable for 1.3–2.2 ms at that point.
A measurement of 65,263 ref-log uploads found zero out-of-order uploads after partitioning by writer epoch.
For the observed disagreement, `ch2` deleted zero ref objects over all time, `ch1` deleted zero ref objects during 16:47:00–16:48:00, and `ch2` deleted zero ref objects during that interval.
Relaxing the condemned-token gate for non-pending entries was rejected because `SabotageAdoptRetiredToken` demonstrates that binding a listed token is unsafe.
Accepting a condemned token without resurrecting it is unsound because exact-token GC deletion can graduate and delete that incarnation, leaving the committed manifest dangling.

Skipping the occupancy `HEAD` on a dedup-cache hit is unsafe: the cached matching blob may have had zero in-degree and been fully deleted since caching, and after the proposed §5 change an absent `.meta` object would look like Clean, so only `HEAD` or a body GET can distinguish absence from a live blob.
A fallback is acceptable only when uncertainty concerns the mechanism; uncertainty about the source must abort and retry rather than silently taking another route to the same peer.
CAS code uses `LOGICAL_ERROR` only for genuine programming invariants and uses `CORRUPTED_DATA`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, or `ABORTED` for the corresponding existing CAS error classes.

The primary soak correctness oracle is all-replica agreement on `count() + sum(sipHash64(*))`, with an absolute Python-side prediction for deterministic `INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM numbers(N)` workloads.

The core invariants (INV-NO-LOSS, INV-NO-DANGLE, INV-NO-RETURN, INV-JOURNAL-COVERAGE, MonotoneGC) are model-checked by CaIncarnationCore.tla; mount-safety invariants (WriterEpochMonotoneUnique, SupersededWriterMakesNoMutation) are model-checked by a focused Phase-0 TLA+ model; INV-NO-DANGLING and INV-NO-ORPHAN-EDGE under D1 are model-checked by CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla (724,944 states, GREEN as of 2026-07-01).

Backend conformance table: AWS S3 (versioning off) uses ETag, fully conforming, validated live 2026-07-03, probe-gated at startup (DeleteObject If-Match GA'd Sep 2025). RustFS 1.0.0-beta.8 uses ETag, empirically verified 2026-06-11, leading open-source CI candidate, with known issue rustfs#3231 (overwrite-leak of objects above the store's inline threshold, e.g. 128 KiB, in unversioned buckets) that can produce metacache LIST storms and false 404s on HEAD -- the only source of GC fold clamps observed to date. Azure Blob uses ETag (write-sensitive), supported and probe-gated, with versioning/soft-delete required off. GCS uses generation, binding specified but implementation deferred, fail-closed until probed. MinIO OSS (archived 2026-02) has If-Match on DELETE silently ignored (confirmed 2026-06-11) -- fail-closed. Ceph RGW has no conditional delete documented -- fail-closed.

The archaeology report names concrete evidence-based test-coverage gaps (vol. 06 §5): the `SingleWriterSlot` background renew loop has zero direct test references (`MountLeaseKeeper` is exercised only via synchronous `renewOnce`, so the async renewal thread and its error-latch split-brain-safety path rest on review plus soak) — flagged High because the P3.1 S13 fence-of-blocked-lease wedge lived exactly in this machinery; `CasGcScheduler` thread pacing/heartbeat cadence is unit-untestable without sleeps and was verified by review only (the P3-B1 wedge was exactly here); async-insert retry row-loss (B139) is parked behind the soak default `async_insert=0` with no gtest; and several `IMetadataStorage` overrides (`createMetadataFile`, `truncateFile`, `chmod`, `setLastModified`, `setReadOnly`, `createDirectory*`) are never driven by any test, though mostly deliberate no-ops.
The reader implementation requires a TLA+ invariant that every object in a live reader pin's `replay(S, tail <= L)` closure is neither condemned nor pruned.

The owner-tombstone change requires tests proving that decommission leaves a present owner object with `retired_at_ms` set, that a competing `putOverwrite` makes the tail abort closed, and that a tombstoned same-UUID owner is rejected by `claimOwnerOrThrow` with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
A detector should flag a namespace whose current catalog life contributes no checkpoint or listed objects while a non-current life of the same name has listed objects.

The TXN-ONE-PIPELINE design's plan-time audits require a fault-injection regression verifying that process termination after a successful `Keeper` publication but before disk `commit` enters the existing missing-part fetch/lost-part path, and explicitly forbid introducing CA-specific recovery for this window.

The old `gc_clear_on_spare` behavior and the post-adoption clear modeled by `post_adoption_clear` must remain red in the TLA gate; the latter is specifically unsafe because adoption does not fence pre-CAS side effects.
The report's earlier claim that `renameParts` performed the CA publish before the Keeper multi is explicitly corrected as false; on CA `renameParts` is only a tmp-to-final overlay re-key.
The `lazy_load_tables` proxy is considered unsafe for upstream promotion because it weakens type identity and has roughly sixty unforwarded virtuals, including a silent-empty `backupData` path.
The CAS path stages every blob locally and then uploads `pending_blobs` in a serial loop while committing parts one at a time, so one thread orchestrates and waits on each PUT or HEAD in turn.
The dead-precommit skip was not the S42 cause because `dead_precommits_skipped` was zero on both nodes; the skipped `-1` path never fired.

The previous design treated immutable log PUT as durability even though semantic application depended on later in-memory installation, creating possibly durable-but-not-applied state after an ambiguous PUT.
The intermediate `B167` blob-watermark design had a livelock in which GC could re-condemn a build's fresh upload during the non-atomic upload-to-publish gap, preventing publication forever.

The B140 dangle was caused by `reuseBlob` (the adopt operation) transferring the blob hash but not the `cas_owner` protection, so an adopted blob's protection stayed bound to the retired byte-writer and GC reclaimed it under a still-in-flight adopter; `system.content_addressed_log` (B170) pinned the precise dangle event with its token and timing.

An aggressive test GC cadence exceeded the fixed iteration cap of 8 in `resolveAndResurrectGeneration`, producing `CORRUPTED_DATA` failures in ordinary insert/mutation tests; the soak surfaced 33 failures from this single root cause and the fix was a one-line cap change from 8 to 256.

A 2026-06-20 soak reported 1.6M `S3WriteRequestsErrors` and 94 `fsck dangling` after a chaos window; forensic analysis showed all 922,772 GC deletes had `indeg_at_recheck=0`, the errors were ~1.57M by-design `PreconditionFailed` (412) CAS contention on root-shard manifests, and the 94 dangling was a transient read-unavailability false-positive (429/503 load shedding) whose 180s settle budget was too short under write load.

`CaGcIndegRefoldCore.tla` isolated an in-degree-underflow hazard the large safety model could not express: the C++ accumulated blob in-degree as a non-idempotent integer delta stream, which could reach -1 (throwing `CORRUPTED_DATA`) when a completion-seal cursor persisted at the wrong position; the fix adopted an idempotent two-cursor presence-set merge, making the underflow structurally impossible, and the model was then removed because it described a design the code had abandoned.

An external author review of rev.6 confirmed 3 substantive findings: F1 seal-skip-on-empty-dead-region combined with a blind detector, F2 a sticky-boundary-bool causing over-seal plus a fail-open allowlist, and F3 the seal PUT held under `state_mutex` for up to 90s; all three were filed as a fix-round task.

`CasInstrumentedBackend`'s classifier still contains a dead `_watermark` classification branch and a stale comment (`CasStore.cpp:263`) claiming the watermark writes a `roots/<server-hex>/_watermark` slot; the standalone watermark object was retired when the watermark was folded into the mount-lease beat by the ack-floor merge (`FormatId::Watermark=7` is retired).

The stage-1 fix-verification pass found the writer-ledger memory regression guard incomplete: `LongTailReplaysUnderMemoryBound` exercises only the free `recoverRefTable`/`recoverRefTableDetailed` path, not `CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered`, so the ledger's own recovery loop could regress to whole-tail materialization while all existing bounds and the test-local control stay green; a later fix (commit 330d52e8c96) added a dedicated ledger-path test that verifies both an upper and lower peak bound.

Several GC-reclaim tests for abandoned precommits were deleted (not disabled) because reclaiming an abandoned precommit is now the writer's job on recovery (it appends the exact `owner_transition` removal), not GC's.

`gtest_cas_mount.cpp:101`'s comment "No mount has been written in Task 4" is stale and contradicts the same file's extensive mount writes; `gtest_ca_wiring.cpp`'s B188 predicate comment still references vestigial `/trees/` though the gate collects only `/blobs/`.

The final whole-branch review (base `d57a41f353d` to head `7771bb60c70`, 38 commits) found a Critical `partAccess` use-after-free (the same class task T9 meant to close but missed) plus a `gcHealth`-blocks-behind-round issue, fixed in `452d17af42f`.

The final whole-branch review found the S22 caller discarded `Committed`/`Conflict`/`Unresolved` outcomes (fixed `8068d8c5fe0`), the decommission owner-tombstone write was not resumable on an ambiguous outcome (fixed `bec89a9de95`), and `emu_token_state` had unbounded growth (fixed `08ea8d1200e`, closing the whole fix-wave and review cycle).

S13's quiesce-wedge (cluster died ~6 minutes into the quiescing-cluster phase) was attributed to the same lifecycle-lock class as the final-review Critical `partAccess` use-after-free; after the fix, a re-run with sidecar instrumentation passed 13/13 with quiesce completing cleanly in ~7.5 minutes.

An early draft of the relink/seam TLA+ model omitted the WedgeRetryCreated action entirely, making the wedge protocol's own happy path unreachable: CasRefLedger.h:784-801 documents that a bounded conditional-create retry either lands the exact same transaction bytes or conflicts, so without modelling that retry as a durability-producing event, WedgeResolveInstall's sApplyOwed guard could never be satisfied and every state downstream of a resolved wedge was missing from the state space.
The mount crash-recovery change does not modify `claimMount`, the owner anchor, the epoch counter, or the watermark, and it adds no user-facing configuration.
The no-paranoid-mode decision rejects retaining deleted checks behind a configuration flag; detection remains with ca-fsck, soak assertions, and system.content_addressed_log.

The source-layout refactor preserves behavior by forbidding mutex coverage or lock-order changes, construction/destruction-order changes, persisted-byte/key changes, log/event/metric changes, and mixing file moves with content edits in one commit.

Renaming `Store` to `Pool` and `Build` to `PartWriteTxn` changes only C++ identifiers and file names; the protocol vocabulary `build_seq`, `buildSeq`, `BuildPrefix`, upload stamps, and related build-sequence identifiers remains unchanged.

Each `RefTableState` experiment must pass the full gtest and property gates, record benchmark numbers and an explicit elegance judgment, and retain reverted experiment results in the comparison report.

The fetch-handoff design does not change GC folding, journal codec, snapshot format, sweeps, orphan protection, or anomaly suppression; every write remains in its owning domain and the ordinary INSERT/merge path is behaviorally unchanged.

The TLA phase summary is a pass only when every green configuration is green and every `_sab_*` configuration reports its expected violation; listing-trust audits record the exact action and premise for every model.
The conflicting-`life_epoch` behavior change is delayed until `_ckpt` is re-keyed, because different namespace lives could share the old key before incarnation separation.

`CaRefLaneCore`, `CaRelinkLaneComposition`, `CaRefCatalogCore`, and other listed models with fixed in-module universes have no applicable empty-entity-set configuration; fixed universes are intentional where the proof requires specific actors, rows, or namespace scenarios.

The shipped v12 gate intentionally reuses the name `SabotageStaleCache`: in `CaRelinkConfirmCore` it must be red because it drops v11 rule 3's pending and leader terms, while in `CaRelinkReofferCore` it selects the design predicate and must be green when the marker is intact.
`listedTok` in `CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla` models a LIST-observed live root-shard token as the value compared with persisted fold coverage to decide whether a shard body read can be skipped.

The historical `CaB140DangleMerge` fix requires journal trimming only up to the cursor inside the committed snapshot and atomic commitment of that cursor with the edges; either half alone can lose data.
A future persistent metadata cache would require separate model review because local manifest bytes could survive process restart outside the modeled object store.
The obscure naming pass leaves production classes `CasGc` and `CasRefCkpt` unchanged; the renames apply to metric and suite tokens rather than those class identifiers.

`fixture::fixtureLife` creates a deterministic namespace-derived identity rather than a fresh random life, `fixture::admitLive` creates a bare `Live` entry without `_ckpt`, and `fixture::writeRefLogRaw` writes ref-log bytes directly at the resolved fixture identity while bypassing the writer birth/append lane.
CascadeWriteBuffer is excluded from the CAS* suite set because its Cas prefix is accidental and unrelated to CAS tests.

The four token-diff model configurations `stage5_tokendiff`, `sab_skipchangedshard`, `sab_skipparksdeadprecommit`, and `fix_skipparksdeadprecommit` were retired because no production seam skips a manifest or owner-transition fold read based on a LIST-derived token match.
`Gc::newestFoldSealRef` uses listing absence as a virgin-by-enumeration verdict on the rebuild path, and this is documented as a named residual through `RebuildReport::virgin_by_enumeration`.

The exact retired identifiers are `namespaceIsRemoved`, `refCleanupMarkerKey`, `RefNsCleanupState`, `ns_cleanup_items`, `cleanup_markers`, `publishRemovedSnapshotNow`, and `runNamespaceCleanupPasses`.

The `RefTableState` closed-class optimization design lists three residual risks: E3's overlay-level transaction layer moves the strong-exception-safety guarantee into new code and needs an explicit test that state is byte-for-byte unchanged after a throwing transaction; E4's flat-vector base has different iterator-invalidation rules than the old node-based map, so the closed class's read API must not leak the old iterator-stability promises; and `cas-gc-rebuild` is a shared branch worked concurrently by another session, requiring commit discipline (verify `HEAD` after commit, one ninja at a time, never rebase/amend).

The heart conjunct of the Apalache inductive invariant, `InflightCurrentUnreferenced` (a delete message in flight for a still-current token implies no folded root edge and no unfolded add past the cursor), was proven irredundant by a negative control; dropping the `W-REVALIDATE` re-observation conjunct from `WPublish` produces a counterexample breaking `NoDangle`, machine-checking the F1 re-observation requirement.

A TLA+ model is deleted, not kept, once keeping it would assert a guarantee the shipped code no longer makes; false comfort (an unfaithful model implying a safety property the code does not actually provide) is treated as worse than having no proof at all.

dedupTrace independently traced the CAS write ordering in `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink`: the CAS commit (`renameParts`→`stageManifest`, line 976) strictly precedes the atomic Keeper dedup-token multi-op (line 985), so a failed CAS write leaves no dedup token behind; this refuted the initially-suspected "orphan-token" mechanism for the R3 data-loss regression, though the acked-then-lost data loss itself remained confirmed via a separate mechanism.

codex_r6_findings.md's 'Checks that held' section confirms: a ref-log body whose decoded sequence differs from its key is already rejected; under a true state-derived next ID a dying lane that sees a seal at T+1 cannot create T+2 and must retry T+1; seal-on-every-transition (including clean transitions) is stated correctly; the S42 removal-tail retention rule is safety-correct (its missing piece is bounded execution, finding 6); and REBUILD condemn-nothing fixes the round-5 asymmetric-LIST data-loss scenario (its missing piece is orphan-blob reclamation, finding 9).

`CasFormat`'s `G_BUILD=3` is the highest format generation the build understands (reader rule: `compatibility_version > G_BUILD` throws `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`); retired `FormatId`s are frozen and never reused: `Tree(2)`, `GcSnap(4)`, `RetiredSet(6, magic CART)`, `Watermark(7)`, `RootsRegistry(10)`, `CompletionSeal(15)`.

Regression-pin test files are named after the invariant or mechanism they protect (e.g. `CasGcDangle`, `CasGcUndercount`, `CasGcLeak`), not after raw bug numbers except `b140`/`b171`; the absence of a `bNNN`-named file does not mean that bug is uncovered.
Only two tests in the entire CA gtest suite are DISABLED, both in `gtest_cas_protocol_scenarios.cpp`, pinning obsolete tree-model subtree-adopt behavior.

Restricting a deposed GC leader's advisory meta to condemn-only (add-only, never clearing to Clean) makes the TLA+ witness model GREEN (935,815 distinct states), confirming that stray-Condemned effects are safe as the v3 spec claims and that the SOLE violation source was the stray-Clean `clearSparedMeta`; `FoldRound`'s identical clean-on-spare write is safe only because it is coupled to adoption (the pending row is dropped in the same atomic step), a coupling the deposed-leader case lacks.

The source-layout refactor's phase-5 rename sweep (`Store`→`Pool`, `Build`→`PartWriteTxn`) must use word-boundary-anchored seds rather than blanket `s/Store/.../` or `s/Build/.../`, because a blanket substitution would incorrectly hit `IMetadataStorage` and the protocol vocabulary `build_seq`/`BuildPrefix`, which must survive the rename unchanged.
Each non-trivial implementation task uses a fresh implementer followed by independent specification and code-quality review subagents.

The `gc_lock` in-process mutex was rejected because it blocked writers and limited GC to one process; exact-token deletion, attempt-scoped generations, and the lease provide split-brain safety instead.
Content-addressed immutable data uses binary encoding, mutable control and ref objects use protobuf, and the earlier JSON codec family was abandoned.

The CA IO-layer extension points are CA-agnostic virtual interfaces with fail-closed defaults, while the MergeTree integration remains leaky through repeated `isContentAddressed()` branches and a seam header located inside the CA directory.
The canonical incarnation model establishes exact-token deletion, fold-through-fence ordering, registry commit-time universe fencing, and evidence re-observation as load-bearing safety rules.

The shipped writer uses lazy manifest-body edge discovery with a missing-body clamp barrier rather than the model's inline closure at precommit; this preserves the safety conclusion through a different mechanism.

The `FrontierUnproven::NoCatalogEntry` and `AppendAboveFrozenTail` buckets were removed outright (not retained with a comment) once they became unfireable-by-construction, because a zero-only bucket cannot change the invariant `sum(buckets) == frontier_namespaces - frontier_proven`, and retaining a dead enumerator would falsely imply a live exit path to a reader.

The GC in-degree model replaced a bare integer refcount with a source-edge multiset (`+`/`-` deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)`); the fold computes net in-degree from the edge multiset, and the `BlobInDegreeMatchesActiveManifests` TLA+ invariant asserts the multiset exactly equals the active manifests referencing the blob, turning the `+`-not-yet-durable race into a pending-fold problem rather than a guard problem.

The attempt-scoped-generation fix moved all decision-bearing round artifacts, including `retired` and `outcomes`, under `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/…` rather than the narrower original proposal of attempt-scoping only the four `gc/gen/<gen>/…` write-once artifacts, because `retired` is a writer-facing publish-gate input that `RetireView::refresh` LISTs and writers consult on the commit path, so a stale retired set from a deposed leader under its own `(round, fence_seq)` could otherwise influence live writers.

The B167 watermark models established that `build_seq` must be allocated from a monotone counter, not merely a unique one: a non-monotone allocation lets the active-set floor (`min_active`) be pulled back below a finished build's sequence, re-protecting an already-condemned blob (a leak); this monotone-`build_seq` floor lemma survives in shipped code for precommit-ref reclaim (`Gc::prefixEligible` / the `BuildPrefix` watermark floor in `CasGc.cpp`), even though the blob-protection use case it was built for was replaced.

CAS treats a plan as a hypothesis about how to proceed, not an authority: plans have been wrong in every round (a field placement that silently rebound positional initialisers, a prescribed proof that proved nothing, a step whose own authorization forbade it), so the person executing a plan is expected to notice when it is wrong and say so rather than execute it as written.

Mid-way through the rev.7 disk-lifecycle plan the user ordered a scope cut to a FORGET-only v1: the natural-erasure proof stack (~1500-2000 lines) was excised entirely (erasure is asserted, never machine-proven), documented as spec rev.8 with a 10-item excision list; TLA+ Model 1 (natural-erasure proof) was dropped while Model 2 (lifecycle/FORGET) remained the gating model, and the excision itself removed a net 1095 lines with a clean adversarial review.

E1 (relaxed replay of RefTableState) shipped as KEEP: the un-materialized overlay makes per-transaction scratch copies O(overlay) instead of O(N), reducing replay cost by 22-25% and strengthening the case for E3.

E2 (owned-manifest index for RefTableState) shipped as KEEP achieving flat O(1) BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit (~712-726 ns), at the honest cost of ScratchCopy +13 ns and BM_ReplayHistory regressing to 50,082 ns/row because the index overlay grows along the never-materializing replay tail; E3 was tasked to recover it.

E3 shipped as the simplified variant with no undo journal: `TrustedHistory` apply-mode does in-place mutation with poison-on-throw (replay-only, poison provably contained at all 3 callers), while `Full` keeps the verbatim two-phase copy; this cut BM_ReplayHistory from 50,082 to 1,725.58 ns/row (-96.6%, ~29x) with writer benches flat.
E5 (mutate-in-place-when-uniquely-owned materialize) shipped as KEEP, cutting unique-owner materialize from O(N) to O(overlay) for both COW containers.

The reviewer's (Mikhail) final disposition of the review findings: most "findings" and comments were judged not real or by-design, with a small set treated as genuine and prioritized: (1) GCR-1 rebuild mount-lease interlock — real, add the interlock; (2) `Build::promote` overwrite leak — the most concrete storage leak, fix by failing closed or repointing; (3) lost-ACK idempotency (W-N1/W-N2/J5) — reconcile by reading post-state instead of blindly replaying; (4) J1/J2/J3 writer-lease-is-not-a-fencing-token — add a SIGSTOP/SIGCONT test first, then re-check `mayMutate` immediately before the shard CAS as a short-term mitigation, `writer_epoch`-in-precondition as the longer-term fix; (5) G-N1 persistent clamp — keep fail-closed but add observability/operator escape. RPL-3 was judged safe in practice because the sender cannot remove a part until it receives an ack, which the receiver gives only after a successful write.

Reviewer disposition: the security finding labeled "SEC-2 - no intra-pool authz" in the reviewer's reply (matching the audit's SEC-3, no intra-pool authorization) is accepted as by-design: all bucket-credential holders share the same trust boundary. RPL-2 (ZK/CAS ref divergence on partial commit) is judged not a CAS-specific issue but general ReplicatedMergeTree partial-commit behavior that the project already knows how to resolve (via detached-parts handling). RPL-4 (`to_detached` relink disabled, always streams bytes) is accepted as a possible real performance issue to recheck, believed to use the same mechanics as a normal fetch. RPL-5 (no dedicated CAS integration tests for quorum/SYNC REPLICA/cloneReplica) is accepted as coverage debt comparable to other ClickHouse features, mitigated by all stateless tests passing successfully against a CAS-backed server.

The follow-up triage's "Close As No-Action / By Design" bucket: G-N3 (spurious ABORTED on lost-ACK round CAS) is a false positive because the next GC round reads the already-committed `gc/state`; cross-shard serializability findings (fractured read, read skew, phantoms) are accepted as by-design; and RPL-2 (ZK/CAS ref divergence) should follow ReplicatedMergeTree's existing detached-part/recovery semantics rather than invent CAS-only cross-registry transactionality.

The Stage B strategic review's concentration proposal, in dependency order: (1) a `FencedCatalogWriter` primitive constructed once per mount from `(admitted_generation, check_fence_or_throw)` that owns `casUpdate`/`casAdmitEntry`/`publishCkpt` dispatch and re-checks the fence inside every CAS attempt, replacing the two threaded fence parameters at every call site; (2) collapse namespace-life resolution to three named entry points — `lifeIfCataloged` (read), `resolveNamespaceLife` (the sole writer-mint path after the R12 fix), `liveUniverse` (GC/fsck/sweep/decommission) — retiring `resolveLifeOrSentinel`; (3) make removal ordering (prune GC-held state before entry delete) the load-bearing invariant so incarnation-scoped cursor re-keying and half the coexistence tests become unnecessary.

Lesson recorded from the deposed-leader stray-Clean investigation: a formal model that is safer than the code hides real bugs. The original `CaRetiredInRun` TLA gate did not model the deposed leader and stayed green; a first attempted fix made the model advisory-add-only and also went green, but this was a false-green that masked the code's actual behavior (`clearSparedMeta` really does clear-to-Clean pre-CAS) until the BLOCKED verdict and a not-weaken-invariants discipline caught the discrepancy.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's top identified risk (R1) is that an extraction changes lock discipline: the publish lane's correctness depends on the two-phase carve happening under one continuous lock hold and the install region not allocating; the mitigation is to extract only pure functions called from the same place under the same lock (so discipline is unchanged by construction) and to gate on a soak run, not just gtests.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R2 risk is `Pool` facade churn, since B6 touches the class everything depends on; the mitigation is to do that extraction last and keep `Pool` as a delegating facade so call sites are untouched.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R3 risk is that `docs/superpowers/cas/11-walkthrough.md` cites roughly 200 file:line references that workstream B invalidates; the mitigation is to refresh the walkthrough as the final step of workstream B, before carving, since it is the document reviewers read first.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R4 risk is that workstream A3 may be reshaped in upstream review after it has already landed in the fork; the mitigation is to keep A3's fork commits identical to what is proposed upstream and treat upstream feedback as a follow-up to both.
