The D1 implementation plan replaces `gc/registry` discovery with `LIST(cas/refs/)` and reclaims empty ref-shard objects so `dropNamespace` no longer leaks a monotone registry and empty shard objects.

The D1 design collapses the prior fence coordinates into two orthogonal coordinates: immutable shard `incarnation` for identity and birth ordering, plus pool-global GC `round` for the writer retire-view floor.

D1 makes `LIST(cas/refs/)` the discovery authority, retains ambiguity detection across pages as a fail-closed condition, and removes `gc/registry`, `RootsRegistry`, `rootsRegistryKey`, `ensureRegistered`, the registry-fence sub-step, and the `_registry` cursor branch.

`dropNamespace` appends an explicit tombstone as the last journal event after ref removals, and GC deletes the shard only when it is empty, tombstoned, and folded past a completed fence using `deleteExact(rootShardKey(ns, shard), token)`.
After registry removal, GC fences only discovered shards from `LIST(cas/refs/)`; an absent shard is not minted or fenced, and create ordering is supplied by the precommit gate.

The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC protocol documentation to cover lease/election, rounds, orphan and ref removal, shard reclaim, incarnation, registry removal, attempt-scoped generations, TLA+ references, and S3 budget links.
The ack-floor GC redesign replaces O(universe) per-round fence and recheck phases with a merged per-server heartbeat, a current retired list, and a one-pass three-cursor merge.

The current retired-list design adds `RetiredEntry::condemn_round`, adds `GcState::retired_refs`, uses `cas_gc_state` version 4, rejects v3 fail-closed, and has `RetireView::refresh` GET `gc/state` followed by each referenced retired-list object without LIST.

The planned one-pass ack-floor round computes the heartbeat floor before discovery, folds and merges deltas, deletes graduated entries by exact token, writes retired-list objects, and then performs one `gc/state` CAS; `fence` and `recheck` are removed.
The redesigned regular GC round targets O(delta) plus O(servers) S3 requests; its only universe-proportional operation is the existing LIST sweep, which costs O(universe/1000) LIST requests.

The retired list is one current sorted candidate set referenced by `gc/state.retired_refs`; per-round retired sets keyed by `retiredKey(...)` and the multi-round `RetireView` fetch protocol are removed.

`gc/state` removes `fence_version`, adds current retired-list references and checksums, and is updated with one CAS per pass containing the round, generation adoption, retired references, and coverage.
`fence_round` is no longer bumped every round; it remains only as the birth floor stamped at root-shard creation for THM-NO-RETURN newborn ordering.
Graduation is two-phase: a pass marks fresh graduates with `delete_pending = true` and keeps them published, while `deleteExact` runs only for entries already pending in the previous published list.
Snapshot-run streaming scope includes T2 streaming reads and T0 reference-parent runs for empty-delta shards; T1 delta-runs are deferred to a subsequent specification.

Implemented retention skips at generation granularity and advances `snap_pruned_through` over every visited generation; when a reference moves off a skipped generation, hand-off deletes the whole `gc/gen/<g>/` prefix rather than one run, preventing leaks of the rest of that generation's artifacts.

The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration over batches of at most `rebuild_edge_budget` edges, feeding the previous attempt's runs back as `prior_runs`; this provides O(budget) memory without new spill/merge classes.
GC trim uses `mutateShard` as a `WholeShard` queue item, so trim rewrites no longer race writers even though trim still flushes alone.

If any fold pass records a clamp anomaly, destruction is suppressed: no graduations or redeletes occur, pending entries carry `UNCHANGED`, condemn/spare continue, and deletes resume on the first clamp-free pass; the pass emits a warning and increments `CasGcClampSuppressedPasses`.
GC Lever A skips the expensive in-degree snapshot rebuild on rounds with no destructive decision; Lever B, an incremental point-updatable in-degree store, remains out of scope.

The DEFER decision is true exactly when changed-shard count is below `fold_threshold`, no destructive decision is due, and `rounds_since_last_fold` is below `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`; otherwise the round FOLDs.
Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for a renewal is conservative for the GC floor because it can only lower `min_ack` and delay graduation; lease expiry is the failure that must be avoided.

The phase-4 GC optimization skips unchanged namespaces so an idle round approaches O(servers) reads and a small-delta round costs O(delta), with a mandatory TLA+ proof that owner-removal events are never skipped.

The dangling-precommit fix uses a fold-side, watermark-keyed force-Read: `ShardCoverage` records the minimal live precommit binding, and `computeDiscoverDecisions` overrides `Skip` when that precommit is provably dead.

The resurrect-reupload fix keys blob condemnation on `(hash, current token)` instead of only on the hash, and re-condemns a current token when a touched hash has net in-degree zero and a prior retired token differs.
Build::abandon retires build_seq after its precommit-removal CAS, while alive is set false early.
Graduation is re-keyed from condemn_round < min_ack to condemn_round < current_round, with min_ack removed from the GC fold interface.
After v3, the retired list is GC-private: writers make condemned decisions through per-hash `.meta` point reads and do not read `RetiredSet`.

Retired-in-snapshot preserves settlement semantics including condemn, carry, round-paced graduation, `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, the pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters.

The two-cursor merge settles a pending row by exact-token redelete at d = 0, spares any row at d > 0, graduates a nonpending row when `condemn_round < current_round`, and otherwise carries it unchanged.
In-place journal trimming was replaced by cleanup of `_log` and superseded `_snap` objects only when both durable cursor coverage and observed snapshot coverage exist.
CAS listing and exact-delete handling is intended to share a callback-based `forEachListedKey` iterator and a `classifyDeleteOutcome` classifier across GC, fsck, and orphan-manifest cleanup.

`GcState::fence_seq` is write-only vestigial state because GC outcome and retire keys use `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`; its proto field is removed and field number 3/name `fence_seq` are reserved.
`ShardCoverage::folded_cursor` and `ShardCoverage::incarnation` have no production readers and are removed from the fold-seal format while the `ShardIncarnation` type itself is retained.

GC fold body reads should size each fresh `ReadBufferFromS3` from the known listed/meta body size plus small slack, capped at the current default; the expected effect is approximately 99% less fold-buffer churn with no behavior change.

Manifest debris must be drained before deleting the victim mount slot because deleting the mount body removes `floorForNamespace` watermark authority and would make the debris ineligible forever; the decommission command is the epoch authority and can sweep old-epoch prefixes.
The rev.6 GC-defense audit treats zero S3 requests spent fighting a foreign writer on hot paths as the compliance principle; incidental checks and CAS-linearized commits are compliant by definition.
A new GC leader starts lease observation afresh, delaying fencing by one round without weakening safety because fencing is a liveness and cleanup mechanism.
The rev.6 GC-defense audit keeps the `gc/state` CAS, orphan-sweep prior-epoch gate, and fold-lag machinery because they are GC or intra-node mechanisms rather than foreign-writer defenses.
The recommended root-cause fix for the fetch-by-relink residual is a liveness re-check at the GC pre-CAS `deleteExact` site rather than restoring blanket promote-time HEAD and `loadMeta` probes.
Reader retention is implemented as incremental removal deferral rather than refolding the entire pinned closure each GC round.
Fetch-by-relink handoff pins and reader snapshot pins share only the GC retention-overlay primitive and are independently shippable features.
Any future §5 revival must keep spare tombstones uncleared until a writer resurrects the blob with a fresh token.

CAS runs use sorted NDJSON with no blocks, footer, or `seek`; `RunFileReader::seek`, `inDegreeInGeneration`, and `SourceEdgeKeyCodec::seekPrefix` are deleted because production consumers read runs sequentially, accepting approximately twice the bytes with re-binarizing `cas_run` as the localized fallback.
`cas_gc_outcomes` is not deterministic: it uses idempotent `putIfAbsent`, and replay adopts an existing durable object after decoding rather than treating byte inequality as a correctness failure.
Only `RunKind::SourceEdge` is live for standalone `cas_run`; `BlobDelta` and `TargetShardDelta` are dead, while `ManifestEntries` remains only for the embedded part-manifest stream.
The production fold uses a hand-written two-cursor merge of the prior run stream and scattered deltas; no k-way line-based merger is introduced.
The superseded v1 protocol proposed a build-owned pin at `gc/fetch-pins/<receiver_srid>/<build_id>` containing the fetched part's blob-ref closure, created by the sender before releasing its part.

Review finding №2 is by design at the harm level: unconditional `resurrectStaged` is safe because content-addressed payloads are byte-identical, promote dependencies are tokenless-on-ref, and fresh tags defeat stale exact-token deletes.

`CasDecommission.ManifestDebrisPhaseFailuresWarnAndContinue` should inject `S3_ERROR`, not `LOGICAL_ERROR`, because `sweepNamespace` catches `Exception` without inspecting the error code and the test models unavailable backend protection-view access rather than an invalid invariant.
The sound S31 completeness check compares `previewDeletes` with the same-instant `fsck.pending_gc` and delete-pending classes, not cumulative `deleted_total`; no product-code change is required.
The GC scheduler exits at its next wake on `Vanished`, on published `vanished_intent`, and on `IdentityLost`; it does not join from a callback.
The skipped-transaction detector must detect the effect that a fold cursor advanced past a ref-log transaction that was never applied, rather than assume that the cause was a hole in a `LIST` page.
Probe A compares the two existing full enumerations of `cas/refs/` instead of performing another scan, so it adds a set comparison and no backend I/O.

`GcRoundLogRecord` uses a fresh `round_id` for every round attempt and stamps it on Start, Phase, and Finish rows; `round` is unsuitable because it is zero on Start, unavailable on non-leader rounds, and known only after a folding CAS.

The fix must not assume holes are page-shaped or trust a particular store, must retain Probe A and its `HEAD` verdict, and should close Probe A's two blind spots with the authoritative chain rather than widen its witness rule.

For each ref log, GC performs one GET of the log body because the transaction must be read; for each edge it performs one HEAD and one GET of the manifest body because the reducer needs the blob list for both `-1` and `+1` edges.
Per-log GETs and per-edge manifest GETs are independent fetches; their application order matters, but fetching can be parallelized subject to the existing pool concurrency limit.

A GC invocation performs a catalog-only pre-fold drain after acquiring its lease and before defer, stream enumeration, the fold catalog cut, folding, or successor-seal adoption; it deletes only complete observed `Removing` rows whose matching adopted life row has cleanup evidence and no durable hold.

Namespace removal deletes lifecycle metadata only; it has no `suppress_destructive` input and performs no physical deletion, leaving `_ckpt`, stream objects, `_files`, and other dead-life objects to the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor.

The bounded-walk fix freezes each round's work set at the round-start LIST tail: if `tail_listed > cursor`, exact-walk only through `tail_listed`; if equal, skip the namespace; if below, skip and count the stale listing, with no new persistent state.
A namespace reaching its frozen LIST tail is not counted as frontier-proven; quiet-namespace probes remain responsible for proving the frontier and detecting persistently hidden new records.

The destructive GC round remains sequential in this series: it adds no `MultiDelete`, batch-delete API, parallel delete fan-out, or delete-side concurrency, so the soak establishes a per-operation baseline for a later optimization round.

Probe A is deleted because catalog-authoritative discovery and LIST-independent recovery make its second full stream LIST irrelevant to correctness; B1/B2 accounting and the mount-time capability probe remain.
The Stage-A sampled store-quality detector was intended to suppress only its response: a nonzero `CasGcRefScanDisagreements` does not abort, hold, or gate a round whose ref intake reads exact keys.
Task 15 bounded rounds are the load-bearing GC scalability fix: making every round terminate restores cadence semantics for downstream work keyed on round completion.
The C1 frontier fix removes both probing and durable holds for an uncataloged namespace because all probe and hold operations are reachable only inside the catalog-resolved loop.
A `RemovalReady` namespace is excluded from GC walking and cursor creation, making cursor absence monotone while the catalog row remains present.

Canonical cursors for namespaces absent from the catalog are retired metadata and should be omitted from the next seal, while the condition is counted and logged rather than used for pool-wide suppression.

Writer cleanup duties own precommit-owner settlement and the active-build-floor pin, not physical body deletion; settlement order is exact `OwnerTransition` append or conclusive absence, then `retireBuildSeq`, then duty removal, with failures retaining the duty for retry.

Physical unreachable bodies from `Rejected`, `Uncertain`, and `Durable` attempts remain GC/orphan-sweep-owned; the writer path never exact-deletes a body, and missing attribution suppresses destructive fallback.
Enabling production destruction may change only the source of `frontier_complete` from hard-wired false to catalog-proven true; changing any other suppressor term is a protocol error.
T6 cannot enable destruction until the frontier-attribution verdict is `BENIGN-TRANSIENT` with convergence evidence or a real-gap fix has landed and reproduced a complete frontier.
The ref/GC subsystem has the highest documentation drift because Stage B landed on 2026-08-03 after the walkthrough, so current code takes precedence over the walkthrough for those pages.
The LIST anomaly had a correct tail; the lie was omission of predecessors below the returned frontier rather than tail under-reporting.
The CAS GC trust chain is catalog cut, `_ckpt` acknowledged frontier, exact `GET` records, and conditional-write fences; LIST is only a hint for work bounds, witness sets, and genesis.

CAS GC optimization must retain arithmetic middle intake everywhere, frontier probes for held or logless namespaces, and `tail < cursor` quality detection; only `tail == cursor` can prove a trusted frontier under a bucket passport.

Trusted-LIST frontier mode may skip the exact `GET cursor+1` probe only for a per-backend certified store whose LIST is known to include keys completed before the LIST began; the mode must remain opt-in and fail closed to probe-always.

A backend-independent parallel exact-key walk can fan out namespace probes and `cursor+1..tail` record GETs over a bounded pool without changing the trust model, while fold application remains ordered or deterministic.

The safe response to a GC post-CAS cleanup error is to retain leaked bodies for the orphan-manifest sweep rather than fail the already-committed decision; cleanup errors after `gc/state` CAS are data-safe but can redden the round.
Expedited or GDPR deletion is intended to confirm that no live ref remains under the GC lock and then bypass the normal two-phase graduation delay without changing the layout.
A naive GC fold budget is unsafe: omitted `+1` edges must suppress deletion rather than permit it, so bounded rounds require durable progress state.

The chosen interim response to the LIST-hole hypothesis was mechanism-agnostic detection: compare two ref-prefix enumerations before advancing a cursor and compare intended-to-fold records with actually applied records; the permanent journal-chain fix remains required before release.
GC read parallelism is safe because tables fold independently and log reads can be prefetched while prior logs are applied; the ordering constraint applies to folding, not fetching.

The concurrent-leader GC fix stores every per-round artifact, including `retired` and `outcomes`, under `gc/gen/<gen>/attempt/<a>/...`, where `<a>` is the folding leader's lease sequence; a lease-guarded adopt CAS publishes `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`, and readers resolve only that adopted pair.

GC cadence should be driven by per-shard journal pressure (event count, body size, or age), not changed-shard count, because one hot shard can accumulate thousands of mutations while still counting as one changed shard.

The resurrect-reupload fix makes `closeBlob` HEAD the current token when a prior retired entry reaches zero in-degree and condemns the current token if it differs from the retired token, matching `CaIncarnationCore`'s `GRetire` behavior.

To reclaim abandoned precommits on parked shards, `Gc::computeDiscoverDecisions` force-reads a token-stable shard when its sealed minimal live precommit is dead according to the mount watermark, allowing `reclaimAbandonedPrecommit` to emit the owner removal.

The GC-wedge fix protects pending removals of every owner kind: in `activeManifestKeys`, any removal with `transition_version > sealedFoldCursor` keeps its `old_binding` manifest body active until the removal `-1` is sealed; the sweep also emits a manifest-delete audit event.
The B140 dangle fix requires both `TrimGated`, which limits journal trimming to the committed fold cursor, and `CursorInSnap`, which atomically commits the fold cursor with the snap edges.
A DEFER invocation may inspect one bounded namespace-janitor page under suppression, but it must retain a valid cursor so the next authorized fold retries that page.
The root-local part-manifest design retired the `listedTok` token-diff discovery skip: a LIST match may not authorize skipping a manifest or owner-transition fold read.
The GC round DEFER mechanism bounds consecutive deferrals with `MaxDefer`; once the bound is reached, `GBegin` and weak fairness drive `GFold` so `unfolded` eventually returns to `{}`.
`Indeg` is read from the sealed `folded` snapshot only; a delta added after the fold cut remains in `unfolded` and is protected by the pending-delta guard rather than by the in-degree check.

FOLD and DEFER are mutually exclusive in an idle round: `DeferRound` is enabled only when `~GraduationDue` and its deferral condition hold, while `GBegin` is enabled for graduation or an exhausted honest defer budget.

The CAS worklog's observed S42 stale-edge defect occurs when a precommit's `+1` edges fold into in-degree, allocation then aborts, and the orphan-manifest sweep deletes the now-unowned manifest without decrementing those folded edges.
Catalog deletion does not require physical emptiness: `_ckpt`, stream, `_snap`, and `_files` residue may remain for the perpetual janitor or a family-specific sweep.
The ref-delta intake has no quiet or expected-next 404 frontier: every catalog target must resolve through its exact CTE.
Under the amended v9 intake, `LIST` is a zero-trust hint; fold progress advances arithmetically and destructive work requires a per-namespace frontier proof.
`GFold` and `GSettle` are separate steps, so a `+1` durable after a round's fold cut is invisible to that round's settlement.
GC must not trust LIST completeness, independently of whether the object store is RustFS or AWS S3.

Run-file streaming is complete: `RunFileReader` uses ranged reads through `CasObjectStorageBackend::get` and `getStream`, and the whole-run `full` member was removed; delta-runs and compaction remain desirable follow-up work.
The setting `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` was removed entirely because bounding the one-shot manifest cleanup phase converts a bounded burst into a permanent leak.
A retained view may delay detection of `INV-NO-DANGLE` after a live manifest body is physically deleted, so fsck and corruption probes must bypass retained views or use strict validation.
The candidate `RoundContext` must preserve the GC invariant that round state is threaded and never re-read; adding a re-read convenience would be unsafe.

Stage A must not be certified or deployed as a standalone deletion-capable stage unless it has the authoritative catalog universe or all destructive work remains globally suppressed until Stage B is installed
Every destructive GC phase, including handoff_reclaim, must receive suppression state before execution and have a zero-delete test when the hold is active or the frontier is incomplete
With only per-key deleteExact available, catalog-token and fence credentials must be revalidated immediately before each delete rather than once per multi-key batch
The late-plus-one delete-site guard needs a test-only sabotage or fault seam that bypasses the final in-degree read, records an isolated RED test, and then restores the guard for GREEN
The production UniversePolicy default must remain non-authoritative until a dedicated enablement task after Stage B Tasks 5 and 6, preferably Task 7, are green
The frontier test belongs in gtest_cas_universe_from_catalog.cpp, while the sole Stage-B edit of gtest_cas_list_liar_end_to_end.cpp belongs to Task 7b
The unversioned GcHeartbeat is acceptable only as disposable advisory state; if it affects cross-version safety it must be converted to protobuf with CasHeader
If GcHeartbeat remains fixed binary, it must be documented as disposable advisory state with exact-length validation and permission for future readers to ignore or recreate it
Orphan-manifest deletion for live namespaces must be disabled unless a persisted owner-grant ref id or fenced quiescent reconstruction proves the cut
Catalog admission must reserve each entry's worst-case Removing and fold-seal representation so capacity can never refuse the transition needed to remove an admitted entry.
Every unsettled writer cleanup duty must be persisted before the build is retired, with a defined adopter, exact-delete completion, and retirement transaction.
Catalog admission must reject creation unless the encoded catalog plus worst-case fold cursor and removal reservations fit within both the catalog cap and the 256 MiB fold-seal cap.

Orphan-manifest nomination must exact-GET and decode M, submit neutral current-count touches without B2 or unmatched-removal accounting, adopt them through the fold seal/gc/state CAS, and exact-delete M only afterward.

Catalog admission must enforce the additive reservation predicate fold_fixed + Σ reserve_cursor(entry) + Σ reserve_removing_cleanup(entry) + Σ reserve_hold(entry) <= fold_seal_cap in addition to encoded_catalog(post).size <= catalog_cap.

Classification-4 wire fields require exact bounded names and values, duplicate-field rejection, and a byte-exact worst-case reservation including escaped namespace text, framing, newline, and trailer growth.
Arithmetic exact-key intake is the intended mechanism for closing LIST omissions; the former Probe A seam was deleted rather than retained as a sampled store-quality detector.
Parallel GC fetching should be bounded by the number of in-flight manifest bodies and should leave application strictly ordered while fetching log and manifest bodies ahead of use.
A proposed manifest cache is keyed by `ManifestId`, scoped to one fold round, bounded in bytes, and dropped at round end; avoiding one redundant edge avoids both its HEAD and GET trips.

Blob in-degree is derived from a folded set of source-edge deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)` rather than stored as a mutable counter; set semantics can delay reclamation but cannot accelerate deletion.

The ack-floor GC round replaces fence and recheck phases with a three-cursor streaming merge and one `gc/state` CAS; graduation requires `condemn_round < min_ack` and two-phase `delete_pending` handling.
All decision-bearing GC artifacts, including `retired` and `outcomes`, are under `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/`, and only the adopted attempt is reader-visible.

The useful manifest-body cache scope is one GC round: an op-scoped or transaction-scoped cache saves nothing, while a round-scoped cache can avoid cross-transaction re-reads; the HEAD-before-GET pair remains vetoed from change.
GC, orphan sweep, and fsck should share a structured deletion outcome vocabulary: deleted, missing, token mismatch, unsupported, and failed.

Retired entries can ride the source-edge snapshot as condemned-sentinel rows, reducing the GC merge from three cursors to two; a separate incremental LSM snapshot is an independent later optimization.
GC streams the three-cursor merge but accumulates the round's `std::vector<BlobDelta>` in memory, so a large mass-drop delta can cause an OOM and repeated lack of progress for that shard.

The later GCR-1 re-triage concluded that `rebuildBaseline` computes the mount-lease ack-floor and installs `gc/state` with a fail-closed CAS, so floor-gated graduation protects post-snapshot writer objects without refusing rebuild while writers are mounted.
The P3-B1 fix invokes an `on_lease_acquired` hook immediately after `acquireOrRenewLease`, sets `i_am_leader`, and pulses the heartbeat before folding begins.

sweepManifestCursorPage is test-only code: it was moved to src/Disks/tests/cas_sweep_test_support.h as sweepManifestCursorPageForTest, and no production translation unit calls it because exact-token deletion without source-edge retirement or gc/state adoption would recreate the accounting hole.
T5 removes `Gc::sampleRefListQuality` and its `ref_list_probe` call, so a regular GC round no longer performs a second full ref-prefix LIST for store-quality sampling.
`UniversePolicy::kDefault` is `Authoritative`; the destructive gate requires an authoritative universe, `frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces`.

After the destruction flip, the dropped-pool-member integration test expects janitor residue to drain to `janitor_pending == 0`, while checking `lifeless_keys=0` on every poll and retaining final `dangling=0` and `unaccounted=0` checks.
`cas_gc_maintenance_state` has no janitor invocation, `GcState`, fold, catalog, DEFER, or round-publication coupling.
Lifecycle physical cleanup is not part of the pre-fold drain: `suppress_destructive` does not govern it, and the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor plus orphan-manifest sweep own physical debris.
No janitor state is stored in `gc/state` or a fold seal, and there is no lifecycle-specific cleanup attempt.
GC must not advance a cursor over records whose enumeration completeness it cannot prove from authoritative data rather than assuming a listing is complete.
The in-degree reducer is intentionally not changed: a set cannot cancel an element it never received, and materializing an unmatched negative edge would create false deletion.

The eager-unlink helper `isEagerContentAddressedUnlink` and six per-method `remove*` eager branches are replaced by subclass dispatch, with durable deletion represented as a staged intent materialized at commit.

The current GC implementation (Gc class, CasGc.h) is a leader-paced ack-floor redesign (spec 2026-07-02): one pass per round consisting of a heartbeat ack floor over MountLease.observed_gc_round, a three-cursor merge fold, two-phase condemn/graduation deletion, and a single gc/state CAS; the older fence_round/recheck terminology survives only as fossil comments/variable names.

Task A7 serializes the manual `SYSTEM ... GC` round against the background GC loop using a dedicated gc_round_mutex rather than the scheduler's existing `mutex`, because loop() deliberately releases `mutex` before running a round so that stop() and heartbeatLoop() are not blocked; holding `mutex` across a long fold would freeze the GC heartbeat and stall shutdown.

GC baseline rebuild is deliberately over-protective rather than under-protective: a build alive across journal trim has no journal evidence, so its manifests look unowned; the rebuild includes edges for every unowned manifest that is not provably build-dead, over-protecting rather than risking under-count. An unowned manifest that later dies with no journal evidence leaks its blob's edges for one bounded rebuild-to-rebuild window, `fsck`-visible as `unaccounted` — preferred to violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY`.

A destructive GC gate based only on `proven == total` accepts an empty universe vacuously because `0 == 0`; the fix adds an explicit nonempty-authority predicate so the gate cannot be satisfied by having nothing to prove.

`cas-gc-rebuild`'s security verdict: it cannot delete live data directly (deletions still flow through the normal round's ack-floor plus two-phase plus exact-token path), and a crafted owner state that makes rebuild under-count requires full owner-plane write access, which already implies total pool compromise (SEC-3) — the trimmed-history guard closes the naive truncation path. Residual risks: FORCE only skips the healthy-pool check (operational risk, not a safety bypass); rebuild does a full-universe discover-and-fold (O(all shards + all journals)), an expensive pool-wide sweep an attacker with SYSTEM access could trigger repeatedly (shares the SEC-4 decode/fold exhaustion surface); and a concurrent GC leader's round CAS and rebuild's `gc/state` install can contend, so rebuild must be verified to respect GC leadership or a split-baseline is possible.

D7: the SQL `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` verb and the offline `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` command are NOT duplication — both call the same `Gc::rebuildBaseline` core through two deliberately inverse-gated surfaces (live/writable vs offline/read-only), and this dual surface should be kept as-is.

There are two independent sharding axes in GC that are deliberately different and easy to confuse: `blobShard` (blob-hash high64 % gc_shards, for in-degree work) versus `Store::shardOf` (CityHash64(ref_name) % root_shards, for the owner journal). There are also two independent lease/watermark concepts: the GC lease inside `gc/state`, versus the mount lease / build watermark at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`; `computeHeartbeatFloor` fences only the latter, never the GC lease.

The RemovalReady state costs less wire-format surface than a life-keyed-cursor alternative: cursor identity appears in eight files spanning the wire grammar, every builder/parser, REBUILD, fsck, and the sweep's coverage lookup, versus one enum value, one codec branch, one transition, and the five predicate sites for RemovalReady. Life-keyed cursors also create a new corner case (a reborn name's fresh-life cursor coexists with a dead-life cursor nothing prunes), so they only relocate the retirement-tracking problem rather than avoiding it.

The Stage B strategic review's invariant rulings: weaken byte-exact fold-seal capacity reservation to a generous over-covering bound (count times a conservative constant, hard namespace cap ~10^4) instead of exact worst-case arithmetic; cut the `Creating`-forbids-publication write-path check as a separate production-path obligation since `resolveNamespaceLife` already loops until `Live` and is the sole life source; cut incarnation-scoped fold cursor re-keying once prune-before-entry-delete is the pinned invariant; weaken the `_ckpt` conflict-is-corruption join to a semantic-max merge (corruption only on genuinely incomparable fields).

Under strict removal ordering, the worst cases "two cleanup rows for one namespace" and "a cleanup row with no catalog entry" become unconstructible (both require rebirth before the first removal retired); the worst-case capacity test should be replaced by an anomaly check that fires if GC ever observes an entry-less cleanup row.

Probe A is reported-not-gated: a soak can go GREEN with confirmed enumeration holes (`nonzero_in=28/88 reads`) because folding aborts and nothing is deleted, which is defensible while the product fails closed, but is flagged as a decision that should be made deliberate now that the holes are confirmed rather than suspected.

The ack-floor GC redesign drops `process_epoch` as a separate merged-heartbeat field because the writable path already sets `process_epoch = writer_epoch` (`CasStore.cpp:157`) and the sweep consumes `writer_epoch` unchanged, so a distinct field would be redundant.

The ack-floor design renamed the sabotage control `SabotageDeleteAtFloor` to `SabotageIgnoreAckFloor` because an `r < min_ack` vs `r ≤ min_ack` off-by-one is provably still safe under the publish-order invariant, so the load-bearing control is "ignores the floor entirely", not the exact boundary.

An optional pre-pass refresh for the promote copy-forward tokenless-blob race fix (spec §3) was deliberately deferred rather than implemented: it is a fast-path-only optimization, not required for correctness, so it was left unscheduled rather than turned into a task.
Per-round LIST hunting for deposed-leader GC debris had already been removed; stale generations are now reclaimed by ordinary retention pruning with zero extra hot-path requests.
The three observed ref-log keys were deleted at 16:53:59 after folding aborted and a later complete enumeration reclaimed them; this occurrence produced no leak.

Before the redesign, 100,000 tables with 8 root shards each required approximately 800,000 CAS-PUTs and 1,600,000 GETs per GC round because the fence and recheck traversed the entire root-shard universe.

The redesigned steady-state round budget is one LIST sweep plus O(servers) heartbeat GETs, O(D) changed-shard GETs, O(window) manifest GETs, O(gc_shards) run GET/PUTs, candidate HEADs, graduated DELETEs, O(D) coverage PUTs, and one `gc/state` CAS, with no O(universe) GET/PUT phase.

Before T2, a snapshot run was materialized three times—by `CasObjectStorageBackend::get`, `RunFileReader::full`, and `readPriorEdges`—for peak memory of approximately 3 × O(active edges) per GC shard; the target example estimated about 24 GB RAM for one fold.

Before T0, every pass rewrote every GC-shard snapshot run even for an empty delta, causing an idle pool to pay two snapshot sizes per round; at the target scale and 5-minute rounds this was estimated as terabytes per day of churn.
Opening a snapshot run in streaming mode uses a HEAD, a ranged tail GET for the footer, and a body `getStream`; resident run memory is O(block) while the wire bytes are unchanged.
With T0, an idle round that has no changes touches zero snapshot-run objects and consists of the LIST sweep, heartbeats, and one `gc/state` CAS.
Idle GC over a static 20M-row, 400-part pool used about 1,362 `CasGcGet`, 643 `CasBlobHead`, and 457 `CasRootGet` operations per round, roughly 2,500 S3 operations per round despite no changes.

The observed GC round duration grew from 87 ms at 400 parts to 92.6 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at 100,000 parts, demonstrating O(ref-universe/object-count) scaling; fsck also becomes O(objects) and timed out at 100,000 parts.
Partitioned inserts in S11 require O(partitions) CAS commits, taking about 10 seconds for a 256-partition insert; deferred GC during 64 delete rounds allowed orphaned parts to outpace disk capacity.

`Gc::fold` performs a streaming two-cursor merge over the entire prior generation's source-edge run, reading the whole prior generation and writing a whole new consolidated run even when one edge or no edge changed.
The resurrect-replaced repair adds one HEAD only for a touched condemned transition; quiescent graduation through `settleRetiredBelow` takes no additional HEAD.
The codecs-v3 phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, equal oracle counts on both replicas, recovered from four faults and two restarts, and drained the pool from about 3 GB to 102 MB.
The measured ref-intake cost is `logs + 2 × edges` round trips at approximately 0.9 ms per trip, making the phase request-bound rather than CPU-bound.
In the measured intake, 7,565 edge reads were re-reads across 4,573 distinct manifests, or 39.6%; all observed re-reads were cross-transaction and none were intra-transaction.

The ref-intake loop is serial: approximately 1.9 million requests at 0.9 ms each imply about 1710 seconds, close to the observed 1830-second maximum and consistent with nearly all phase time being serial request latency.
If the approximately 1710-second serial fetch floor were parallelized N-way, the ideal fetch component would be about 213.75 seconds at N=8 and 106.875 seconds at N=16, before merge cost.

The ref-chain design adds about two serial S3 round trips per committed chunk for `_ckpt`, one conditional PUT per touched namespace per epoch transition during recovery, and one catalog GET per fold round after the hot LIST.
The dominant T15 GC cost was `defer_decision`: 5,096.39 seconds, 79.11% of GC time, including full LISTs of about 177,000 keys even when `changed_shards` was zero.
The empty `CaGcDestructiveGateCore` universe configuration was green, with `CatalogUniverse = FrontierProven = {}` and physical actions suppressed despite the two sets being equal.
`CaGcAckFloorCore_empty_blobs.cfg` and `CaGcAckFloorZombie_empty_blobs.cfg` both passed as green with empty `Blobs` sets.
`CaGcLeaseCore_empty_actors.cfg` passed as green with `Actors = {}`.

`CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore_empty_namespaces.cfg` passed as green with `Namespaces = {}` despite the model having configurable entity sets for writers, leaders, blobs, manifest instances, refs, builds, paths, build prefixes, and shards.
`CaGcRoundDeferCore_empty_blobs.cfg` passed as green with `Blobs = {}`.
`CaRetiredInRun_empty_blobs.cfg` and `CaRetiredInRunFoldAbortWitness_empty_blobs.cfg` both passed as green with empty `Blobs` sets.
Across 65,263 ref-log uploads in the affected namespace, partitioned by epoch, zero uploads were out of order.

The GC cadence tradeoff is approximately `A/interval + B·interval`, where `A` is per-fold universe work and `B` is writer amplification from journal growth; the proposed optimal interval scales as `sqrt(U) / r` for blob universe `U` and hottest-shard mutation rate `r`.

GC folds remain O(ref-universe) for large deltas: measured duration grew from about 87 ms at 400 parts to 93 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at about 100,000 parts, even though correctness held with `dangling=0`.
The merged `m_merged` configuration was green with `TrimGated = TRUE` and `CursorInSnap = TRUE`, while `m_both_buggy`, `m_cursorskip`, and `m_trimonly` violated `INV_NO_LOSS` under the same bounds.

Streaming GC run reads use true ranged reads and `getStream`; opening a run costs three requests (`head`, tail `get`, and body `getStream`), or four when a large footer is present, and each `seek` costs one ranged GET per block.

The C2 soak comparison recorded 112,518 skipped entries and 110,218 permanently unreachable objects with a cleanup cap of 5000, while disabling the cap drained 223,714 objects with zero unreachable objects.

The `system.cas_gc_log` counters `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, and `entries_redeleted` represent the three retired-cursor pipeline stages: newly condemned, floor-passed and republished `delete_pending`, and executed exact-token blob deletes.
In that fold window, 2,991 manifests carried both an add and a remove edge, and `CasManifestGet == CasRefEmittedEdges`, demonstrating that no manifest-body cache existed.

The outstanding reconciliation debt recorded 56 already-leaked blobs that incremental rounds could never reclaim because their in-degree was pinned above zero; only rebuilding in-degree state could reclaim them.
Before generation retention (B174) was added, a 12h soak measured `gc/` bookkeeping at 82% of pool storage (2822 retained generations, roughly 3.7 MiB/shard/generation), dwarfing actual data 8:1.
GC observability gained per-phase timing during Stage B, which immediately found the fold seal being read five times per round where the design intended two.

The measured GET-cost formula for a folding GC round is exact: total `S3GetObject` = ref-log body GETs + manifest body GETs, i.e. `1 + edges_per_log`, which climbs from 1.54 to 3.73 as backlog grows; round trips equal `logs + edges` at a flat roughly 0.5 ms per round trip across a 140x request range, and a measured 416-round `Success` sample cost roughly $0.007 in total S3 charges.

GC's `fold_ref_intake` is linear in the ref-log backlog at 256 logs/s sustained; the flat cost is per S3 request (~0.92 ms), decomposing as one GET per log body plus one per emitted manifest edge, so round trips equal `logs + 2*edges`, and edges-per-log climbs from 1.54 to 3.73 as backlog grows.

39.6% of GC intake manifest fetches are re-reads (7,565 edges over 4,573 distinct manifests): intra-transaction redundancy is exactly zero, and all of it is cross-transaction (2,991 manifests carry both an add and a remove edge in the window, so the same body is read once when the ref is published and again when it is dropped), making a round-scoped body cache — not an op- or transaction-scoped one — the effective lever.

Probe B's throw wedges GC until an operator runs the rebuild; on a pre-release soak stand this cost a disk-budget blowout, with the last observed run reclaiming 124 GB at one checkpoint once the wedge was cleared, which motivates the open question of whether the first N occurrences should suppress-and-continue with a counter, escalating to a throw only on recurrence.

A sweep-only defense that makes `activeManifestKeys` judge precommits dead was deferred because it would delete the manifest body without releasing the precommit's pinned blob edges; the fold-side fix is required.

Removal completion performs no namespace-owned physical LIST, physical delete, physical-empty proof, or second deletion window; `_ckpt`, stream, and namespace-file residue is leak-only janitor work, while orphan manifests remain the orphan sweep's work.
Queueing an exact removal is not a valid fix for the unmatched-minus-one leak because `RefTableState` throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` when the binding is absent, turning the leak into a permanent wedge.

`DeleteObjects` cannot replace token-conditional `deleteExact` because bulk delete has no per-object precondition and could delete a replaced incarnation; parallel individual conditional deletes preserve exactness.

A cap on manifest cleanup was rejected because it converted a bounded burst into a permanent leak; measured cap=5000 left 112,518 entries skipped, while disabling the cap drained 223,714 entries in-round.

Moving pre-CAS redeletes to execute only after round commit (to avoid idempotent re-execution on an aborted round) was rejected: the pre-CAS placement is a deliberate Task-9 ack-floor decision justified by durable state and safe at any leader staleness, re-execution is idempotent via exact-token deletes, and the P3-B1 heartbeat fix already removes the amplification that made aborts frequent; revisit only if a post-fix soak still shows re-execution churn.

Accepting a condemned tokened blob without resurrecting it is UNSOUND and rejected in the promote/resurrect design, because the condemn→delete pipeline is exact-token two-phase and an accepted-but-condemned token can graduate to delete, dangling the manifest; only a fresh incarnation via uploadFromSource is safe.

Strict ref-key parsing that accepts only _log, _snap, and _cleanup will abort a fold round when _ckpt appears under cas/refs/<ns>/.
`CasRefCatalog` has no entry-deletion API in the documented state, so a catalog entry survives unconditionally rather than through a partially completed multi-step removal path.
The fence-race `/Replacement` fixture's successor `_ckpt` is life-scoped: the predecessor `_ckpt` at incarnation 177 cannot satisfy a successor at incarnation 178.

An uncaught `CORRUPTED_DATA` from `resolveByExactGet` or `putIfAbsentControlled` in `flushRefBatch` can leave `leader_active` set and waiters blocked indefinitely; the remaining queue must be completed with the exception and notified.
`Build::promote` overwrites `refs[R]` without emitting a committed-to-committed repoint event, so the previously committed manifest and its uniquely owned blobs remain pinned forever.
A crash or exception after `republishRef` promotes the destination ref but before it drops the source ref causes a retry to mint a fresh manifest and leak the first committed destination manifest.
After a lost-ACK `dropRef` CAS, replaying the closure can throw `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` even though the ref removal already committed; conditional-write conflicts should reconcile the post-state instead.
A lost-ACK publish or promote can replay its closure and append a duplicate journal event, producing journal bloat even though set-based GC keeps blob in-degree semantically correct.

E5's in-place-materialize fast path was unreachable from production: `flushRefBatch`'s trial-validation copy `working` stayed alive to function scope, pinning a second shared_ptr reference to the live base across the post-PUT install so `materializeCommitted()` always saw `use_count()==2` and took the O(N) copy path; fixed by releasing `working` before id allocation so the live base is uniquely owned at the install point.

A race existed where the relaxed `use_count()` load in the in-place-materialize fast path could race a cross-thread shared_ptr release: `trySnapshotPublishOnce`'s `candidate_state` (a shared-base copy) was destroyed at function return outside the lock. Fixed by resetting `candidate_state` under `state_mutex` immediately after `snapshotOf`, covering every exit path.

A retry path that treats a vanished CAS catalog object as an empty catalog is a silent-default-substitution defect: on retry after a vanish, it would replace every namespace's catalog with a single mutation's output via create-if-absent; the in-tree analogue `PoolMeta::admitOrValidate` already fails closed on exactly that observation and was cited as the pattern to follow.

`Build::promote` can overwrite an existing committed ref (`refs[dst]=T_a`) with a new manifest (`T_b`) without releasing `T_a`, permanently orphaning (leaking) the old manifest and its blobs; this is the most concrete confirmed storage leak from the review. Fix: `Build::promote` must, when `refs[R]` already names another manifest, either emit a proper committed-to-committed repoint or fail closed with an exception; also move `Build::abandon`'s `retireBuildSeq` call after the removal mutation.

Risk register #5 (Medium, confirmed): `moveDirectory`'s RENAME TABLE path (`:980-1006`) is non-atomic across namespaces; a mid-loop throw can leave the table split across two namespaces (documented as re-drivable), producing an operator-visible split state until manual re-drive. Suggested action: track as a known limitation, consider a durable move journal pre-release.

`RefCowMap::find` builds a non-mergeable iterator for overlay-only keys by using `base->find(key)` instead of the sibling base branch's `lower_bound`; with base={A,D} and overlay-only B, `find("B")` then `++` hits a state bitwise equal to `end()` and silently skips D. Not reachable through current point-dereference-only callers, but the fix (`lower_bound`) is a strict improvement, identical when the key is shadowed.
Per-table refs use an append-only log plus periodic snapshot, and CasRefStateMachine computes RefTableState = replay(snapshot, tail) for writers, recovery, GC intake, and fsck.
The all-tree part-files design stores txn_version.txt, metadata_version.txt, and uuid.txt as ordinary entries in the part manifest rather than a separate ref sidecar.
`mutable_files` such as `txn_version.txt` are inlined into the root shard's `RootRef` protobuf and add zero S3 operations.
After the all-tree part-files migration, `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, and `metadata_version.txt` are ordinary manifest entries and no longer populate `RootRef.mutable_files`.
`FREEZE` creates per-part shadow refs under `shadow/<name>/…`; unchanged parts share blobs by hash and the refs act as GC reachability roots.
A fresh pool mints its own owner and epoch, while imported manifests cannot collide with new ones because `ManifestId` includes the namespace.
The only mutable CAS data is ref state binding a part name to a manifest id; blobs, part manifests, and their metadata are write-once objects.
A precommit may name only a manifest minted by the transaction or the ref's current committed manifest; granting fresh ownership to a foreign manifest id is rejected to prevent ABA reuse.
Publishing over an existing ref binding throws; an intentional repoint must use `republishRef`.
The append-mode `writeFile` path is safe only under the single-appender invariant: it freezes the carried prefix when opened and its CAS loop re-reads the token but not the base content.
A `ManifestRef` has at most one owner in a table, in either the `Committed` or `Precommit` slot.
The former `RefSidecar` and mutable-per-part-file classification are deleted; `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, and `metadata_version.txt` are ordinary manifest entries.
A part manifest contains `ref`, `root_namespace_id`, `payload_digest`, and strictly path-sorted `entries`; `payload_digest` is integrity/debug metadata rather than a key or GC edge.
A manifest id is `ManifestRef = {writer_epoch, build_sequence, manifest_ordinal}` and is not a content hash or random value.
Ref transaction ids are per-namespace contiguous pairs `(writer_epoch, ref_sequence)` rendered as fixed-width hexadecimal fields; `applyRefLogTxn` rejects a non-successor id with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The ref lane has no append-to-object or CAS-swapped mutable pointer: ref logs and snapshots are immutable objects created with conditional creates, and only GC deletes ref objects.
Under D1, `listNamespaces` is derived from a LIST of `cas/refs/` and is unioned with `roots/` for namespaces containing only verbatim files.

Rebuild edge reconstruction replays committed owner state and live precommit bindings, validates every committed `PartManifest` with `refMatchesBody` and `manifestNamespaceMatches`, and refuses the whole rebuild on a missing or invalid committed manifest body.

The queue leader increments `root.shard_version` after every closure in queue order rather than once per flush, so each promise receives its own post-bump transition version and one `casPut` may carry multiple ordered events.
A create-if-absent mutation with `token == nullopt` flushes alone using its `birth_incarnation` and `birth_floor_provider`, preserving the existing birth-stamping behavior.
The new `ShardCoverage` fields are `has_live_precommit`, `min_live_precommit_writer_epoch`, and `min_live_precommit_build_sequence`, and they round-trip through the fold-seal codec.

`ShardCoverage` stores the lexicographically minimal `{writer_epoch, build_sequence}` among live precommit bindings, stamps it on every Read visit, and carries it through Skip and durable fold-seal restart.
`ManifestPut` records `object_kind = Manifest`, the owning namespace, `manifestRefDebugString(id.ref)`, the body token, and reason `stageManifest: part-manifest body written`.

`PrecommitRemoved` records `object_kind = Root`, the target namespace and ref, `manifestRefDebugString(precommit_manifest)`, and reason `abandon: precommit binding removed`; GC-side removals remain `PrecommitReclaim` events.
Decoded `PartManifest::entries` must be strictly ascending by `path`; binary search and all index-free folder-view queries rely on this invariant.

`Store::readManifestShared` has the same mandatory `HEAD`, fail-closed `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` and `CORRUPTED_DATA` behavior, and manifest-cache insertion semantics as `readManifest`, but returns the cached `std::shared_ptr<const PartManifest>` without a per-call copy.
`resolveRef(allow_stale=true)` is bounded by `shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` and locally write-coherent because committed shard mutations erase the shard decode-cache entry and bump `shard_write_seq`.
`decodePartManifest` rejects `path <= prev_path`; the encoder already emits sorted entries, and the strict ordering guarantee is what makes `PartFolderView` index-free.

The byte-weighted manifest decode cache remains keyed by `(ManifestId, Token)`; a token mismatch causes a fresh `GET` and decode, a failed decode is not cached, and the mandatory manifest `HEAD` remains.
A same-manifest re-promote is allowed and must be idempotent; the guard compares the existing manifest_ref with the manifest_ref being promoted rather than rejecting every already-committed ref.
republishRef compares only the source and destination PartManifest entries and drops the source ref without staging a new manifest when the entries match.
Build::promote proceeds when the target ref is absent or already names the same manifest_ref, and throws ABORTED when it names a different committed manifest_ref.
republishRef determines idempotency from PartManifest::entries, not ManifestId, because a re-drive mints a new manifest ID for the same content.
PartManifest::entries are canonical path-sorted vectors, so element-wise vector equality is stable for comparing source and destination content.
When the destination ref is absent, republishRef retains the normal stageManifest → precommitAdd → promote → dropRef sequence.

The obsolete ref handoff transfers a contiguous writer-log prefix into the GC generation through the existing single `gc/state` CAS; before that CAS the prefix is authoritative, and after it the GC fold is authoritative.

`dropNamespace` is represented as one constant-size `remove_namespace` transaction that atomically clears committed and precommit bindings and changes the incarnation to `Removed`; it does not serialize the owner list.
A writer-log object can be removed only when the adopted fold seal names a valid `RefBaseSet` whose namespace row has the same incarnation and `folded_seq >= log_record.seq`.
Every writer-log key and GC ref-fold entry contains the namespace incarnation, so an older incarnation cannot cover or consume a newer incarnation's sequence numbers.
`remove_namespace` changes `Live` to `Removed` and clears every owner binding in one replay transition; no later mutation is valid for that incarnation.

A warm-cache isolated ref mutation creates one `_log` object and performs zero ref-state reads, while a compatible batch of `B` mutations shares one `putIfAbsent`; uncertain writes are resolved by an exact-key `GET`.
The same `WriterId` identifies build ownership, the prefix of each `ManifestRef`, and a namespace incarnation; `birth_gc_round` remains separate and orders a new namespace incarnation relative to GC.
`ManifestRef` is `{writer_id, manifest_ordinal}` with ordinal range 1 through 999999, and canonical manifest paths include `cas/manifests/<namespace>/<writer_id>/<000001>.proto`.
All archive namespaces end in `@cas@`, and `shadowNamespace` must preserve that suffix.

A `RefLogTxn` contains `header`, `namespace`, `namespace_incarnation`, `seq`, and repeated `RefOp ops`; supported operations are `namespace_birth`, `owner_transition`, `set_payload`, `clear_precommits_before`, and `remove_namespace`.

A transaction containing `namespace_birth` and its optional first owner transition runs alone; `clear_precommits_before` and `remove_namespace` also run alone, and a batch never crosses its encoded-size or operation-count limit.

`namespace_birth` is operation zero of sequence one, creates `Live` state for the physical incarnation key, normally includes the first precommit add, and has `birth_gc_round` no greater than the current decoded `gc/state.round`.
A promote operation requires `Live` state, the exact old precommit, a committed binding naming the same `ManifestRef`, and a complete initial `RootRef` payload.
A committed ref removal requires the exact committed binding and removes its `RootRef` payload.
A payload update requires a live committed ref still naming `expected_manifest_ref`; it replaces the complete mutable payload and changes no reachability edge.

Applying `remove_namespace` clears committed refs, precommits, and payloads, changes state to `Removed`, and makes a second durable remove record corruption; API idempotency returns success after observing `Removed`.
A successful append leaves no dirty ref-state memory because the log is authoritative; complete namespace views may be evicted immediately, and eviction never writes storage.

The common write path validates under the namespace lock, writes one inline key or deterministic batch transaction with `putIfAbsent`, resolves an uncertain precondition failure by reading the same key, and applies the transition to memory only after the log is authoritative.
A namespace recreation at the same archive path is allowed only after the old namespace-file prefix is empty, uses a strictly greater `NamespaceIncarnation`, and starts again at sequence one.

Ref-base row keys are `NamespaceMeta`, `Committed`, or `Precommit` tuples beginning with `LogPrefix(ns) = canonical_namespace_bytes(ns) || "/_log/"`; memcomparable encoding preserves canonical object-key `LIST` order, including prefix-related namespaces.

GC processes namespaces in canonical tuple-key order, selects at most one complete transaction prefix per namespace per generation, and never returns to a namespace after emitting its output; any suffix remains in `_log` for a later generation.

A writer mutation exists exactly when a durable operation exists in its `_log` object; one `_log` object may contain a bounded flat-combined batch, and its key plus body are the complete operation encoding.
Only the mounted writer allocates namespace log sequence numbers; GC never appends to the writer log.
Every owner add, move, payload update, removal, and namespace removal is a writer-log operation; GC only replays those operations.
The existing GC generation CAS co-adopts reachability runs, the fold seal, and the exact `RefBaseSet`; there is no independent ref adoption state.
An append that exceeds the namespace tail or decoded-row bound fails before object creation and retains the current sequence.
Mixed manifests store one `BlobRef ref` per `ManifestEntry`; the entry payload is `placement u8, algo u8, digest <lenFor(algo)> raw BE bytes, blob_size u64, inline_len u32, inline`.
The per-manifest `blob_hash_len` header is removed in mixed-algorithm pools, and an unknown entry algorithm fails decoding with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

For a table snapshot `S_X`, recovery computes `TableState = Replay(S_X.state, tail(X))`, where `tail(X)` contains every valid log transaction with identifier greater than `X`; without a snapshot, recovery starts from the empty state and `namespace_birth`.
A snapshot reuses the `RefTxnId` of its last included log, producing one shared ordered timeline where `log X == snapshot X` and later logs have greater identifiers.
`RefTxnId` is distinct from `build_sequence` and `build_id`; a build may create multiple ref transactions and transactions may contain operations from multiple builds.
A `Removed` snapshot contains no committed refs or precommits, and a later `namespace_birth` with a greater `RefTxnId` recreates the namespace on the same timeline.
Promotion removes an exact precommit and creates the committed binding to the same manifest in one transaction, installing the complete initial mutable payload without an ownerless interval.
`remove_namespace` is the final operation in its transaction, follows exact owner transitions for every committed ref and precommit, requires empty owner sets, and records its own `remove_txn_id`.
At most one ref-log PUT per table may have an unresolved result; a later same-table PUT cannot start until the earlier result is resolved.
Warm table mutations perform no ref `LIST`, snapshot GET, `gc/state` read, HEAD, or compare-and-swap; they append one deterministic log object and update cached state.
Failed precommit cleanup is persisted by the writer before build retirement; GC does not detect or remove dead precommits by itself.

Owner transitions emit direct manifest-edge events: owner addition is `+1`, removal is `-1`, same-manifest promotion is neutral, replacement emits old `-1` and new `+1`, and mutable-payload updates emit no edge.

The ref protocol stores per-table append-only `_log/<txn-id>` objects and writer-published `_snap/<id>.proto` snapshots; `GC` folds per-table cursors and manifest-edge deltas from one global `LIST`, cleans covered objects, and never reconstructs table state.

Ref transaction IDs contain nonzero `writer_epoch` and `ref_sequence`; `renderRefTxnId` renders canonical IDs as `0000000000000007-000000000000008e`, and `parseRefTxnId` accepts only the canonical form.
Ref log operations are exactly `NamespaceBirth`, `OwnerTransition`, `SetPayload`, and `RemoveNamespace`; owner bindings distinguish `Committed` and `Precommit` owners.
Ref table snapshots have `Live` or `Removed` lifecycle, optional `remove_txn_id`, committed rows sorted by `ref_name`, and precommits sorted by `(ref_name, mref)`.
Ref snapshot encoding requires committed and precommit inputs to be sorted and rejects unsorted or duplicate rows; a `Removed` snapshot must have zero rows and a `remove_txn_id`.

A ref append lane obtains `ref_sequence` from a store-wide counter, permits at most one unresolved PUT per table, blocks that table's lane while unresolved, and applies observed durable state to the cache before unwedging.

The ref batching queue creates one compatible `RefLogTxn`, validates requests with per-request undo against cached state, gives invalid requests their own exceptions, runs birth and removal alone, and limits each batch to one operation per ref name.

Snapshot publication is background and off-lane, uses `snapshot_log_count_threshold`, `snapshot_log_bytes_threshold`, mount-time triggers, and `snapshot_min_log_age_ms`, and resolves uncertain publication by exact-key byte comparison.

`dropNamespace` emits one transaction naming every owner followed by `remove_namespace`, applies it in memory, rejects further operations, and publishes a constant-size `Removed` snapshot after durability.
Recreating a removed namespace requires the exact `_cleanup` marker found during recovery and continues the existing transaction-ID timeline.

When `flushRefBatch` catches a `CORRUPTED_DATA` exception, it must complete pending and carved survivor requests with that exception, reset `rt->leader_active`, notify `rt->cv`, keep the wedge on corruption, and rethrow.

The ref-model rev.6 oracle is `WStateRev6 == FoldIds(EmptyState, writtenEver \ droppedEver)`, and the strict `NoDivergentFold` invariant requires every completed reader under `Rev6MountRule` to reconstruct that oracle.
The rev.6 snapshot codec stores optional `RefTableSnapshot::sealed_from`, uses format version 2, rejects version 1 fail-closed, and throws when `sealed_from` is greater than `snapshot_id`.

On an unclean epoch boundary, recovery publishes a seal with `seal_id = RefTxnId{liveWriterEpoch() - 1, UINT64_MAX}`, `snapshot_id = seal_id`, and `sealed_from = greatest listed txn id` before marking the ref table recovered; a failed seal PUT throws and leaves recovery fail-closed.

The recovery seal is skipped when the boundary is clean, the live writer epoch is below 2, the dead-epoch region is empty, the table is already sealed through the boundary, or the recovered lifecycle is not `Live`.

The publish trigger uses `tail_count_since_snapshot` or `tail_bytes_since_snapshot` above configured thresholds and no longer requires entries to age; `snapshot_min_log_age_ms`, `TailLogEntry`, `tail_since_snapshot`, `snapshot_base_state`, and `CasRefLatePredecessorObserved` are removed.

A late `_log` with id `L` satisfying `sealed_from < L <= newest_snapshot_id` is reported with a warning and one `RefLateLogDetected` event, never GET-revived, and left for ordinary covered-log cleanup.
At an unclean mount, recovery LIST and replay are followed by an immediate snapshot PUT seal before the mount opens writable.
The recovery seal ID is `RefTxnId(my_epoch - 1, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)`, which covers every late log from every dead epoch below `my_epoch`.

Snapshot publication copies the live state once at a transaction boundary when the count threshold exceeds `snapshot_log_count_threshold` or the bytes threshold fires, then encodes and PUTs asynchronously.
A lane refuses to allocate new IDs past an unresolved PUT in release builds and uses `chassert` for the same wedge invariant in debug builds.
A standalone committed-file removal without a directory drop publishes one repoint containing the manifest without the removed entry.
A repoint publishes the new manifest closure before backend observation and atomically moves ownership onto the same ref key; the old manifest is reclaimed by normal GC.
A byte-equal repoint is a zero-mutation no-op with no audit event.
The repoint primitive serializes concurrent repoints through the per-table single-writer ref lane and promote CAS.
For a ref key `K`, `repointRef` maps to `WRepoint(mOld, mNew, ref=K, w)`: one journal event in one namespace carries `old=Bind(mOld)` and `new=Bind(mNew)` under the same ref.

`Build::promote` accepts a trailing `bool allow_repoint = false`; when it is true and the committed ref names a different manifest, it emits one committed-transition RefOp from the current `ManifestRef` to the new `id.ref` and emits `CasEventType::RefRepoint`.

`repointRef(const PartRefKey &, std::vector<Cas::ManifestEntry>, Cas::ProvenanceOp)` returns false and performs zero pool mutations or events when the candidate manifest is byte-equal to the committed manifest; otherwise it publishes with `allow_repoint=true`, increments `ProfileEvents::CasRefRepoint`, logs the ref and entry count at warning level, and erases the cached folder view on success.

After the mutable-file deletion sweep, resolved refs contain `manifest_id`, `manifest_size`, and `published_at_ms`, while the access API is `publishEntries(dst, entries, op, allow_repoint)` and no production code retains mutable-file fields or predicates.
The CAS refsnaplog migration covers `cas_ref_log` objects at `_log/<txn_id>` and `cas_ref_snap` objects at `_snap/<snapshot_id>`, moving both from binary codecs to the phase-1 text file shape.
A `cas_ref_log` object represents exactly one committed `RefLogTxn`, containing one namespace, one transaction ID, and that transaction's vector of `RefOp` entries.
The recovery seal is an ordinary `RefTableSnapshot` published at synthetic `snapshot_id = {my_epoch-1, UINT64_MAX}` with `sealed_from` set to the greatest applied reference transaction ID.
`sealed_from` is an optional `RefTxnId` whose absence and presence must remain distinguishable in the snapshot wire format; it is not represented by a sentinel value.
Every `RefTxnId` field in refsnaplog text, including the synthetic seal sequence `UINT64_MAX`, is serialized as a decimal string rather than a JSON number.
Snapshot committed rows are strictly ascending by `ref_name`, precommits are strictly ascending by `(ref_name, manifest_ref)`, and every precommit has `kind == Precommit`.
`cas_part_manifest` becomes a `PayloadHybrid` object consisting of a header line, descriptor meta line, sorted JSON entry records, a {"n":count} trailer, and a raw payload zone for inline bytes.
Blob manifest entries carry `ha`, `h`, and `sz`; inline entries carry `il` and no blob reference; entry records are sorted by canonical path without duplicates.

A failed repoint of an existing ref must not drop that ref during compensation: `publishStaging` returns false for the repoint path, so the ref is absent from `created_refs` and is not rolled back as newly created.
After `cas_ref_snap` switched to zstd-framed text, appending garbage to a zstd frame causes one-shot decompression to fail with `Src size is incorrect`.

The corrected seal-conflict test constructs a valid foreign seal with the same namespace and seal id `(2, MAX)`, `sealed_from = (2,1)`, and three committed rows, then proves adoption with `listRefs().size() == 3`.

The plan's Atomic-layout `route()` contract folds `moving/<part>/<file>` into the live table namespace with ref `<part>` and file `<file>`, while a bare `<table>/moving` container has an empty ref and file.

`RefCowMap` copies share the immutable base and copy only the overlay, keyed reads check overlay before base, point writes modify overlay, ordered iteration merges both sorted ranges, and `materialize()` folds the overlay into a fresh base once per flush.

The planned `RefCowMap` API is a read-only-iterator, `std::map<String, RefCommittedRow>`-compatible subset covering keyed lookup, ordered iteration, size/empty, emplace, insert-or-assign, erase, equality, and materialization.
`RefCowMap::size()` and `empty()` are O(1) because `net_delta` tracks overlay inserts and tombstones relative to the immutable base size.
`RefCowMap::materialize()` merges overlay values and tombstones into a new immutable base, then clears the overlay and resets `net_delta`.

Changing `RefTableState::committed` to `RefCowMap` leaves keyed-read and ordered-iteration consumers compatible; `CasRefProtocol.cpp::applySetPayload` is the exceptional site that must be rewritten for read-only iterators.
`RefCowMap` preserves canonical snapshot ordering by bytewise `ref_name`, so the codec boundary remains `std::vector<RefCommittedRow>` and snapshot bytes remain unchanged.

`CasRefLedger::flushRefBatch` must call `rt->state.committed.materialize()` immediately after installing `final_txn` under the existing `state_mutex`, so later trial copies stay proportional to the current flush.
Hot ref-table paths are keyed lookups, while `snapshotOf`, `listRefs`, and `dropNamespace` are the cold paths that require full scans.
Ordered iteration is load-bearing because `snapshotOf` and removal-transaction construction require bytewise-sorted iteration by `ref_name`; an unordered overlay is insufficient.
`RefCowMap` keyed access checks overlay entries first, treats tombstones as misses, writes only to overlay, and performs sorted two-range merge iteration for cold full scans.
`RefCowMap::materialize()` is O(n) once per flush and restores `base + empty overlay`, so ordinary keyed reads between flushes access the base without merge overhead.

The ordered-identifier and snapshot negative tests treat source-edge ID zero, out-of-order source-edge records, zero `RefTxnId` components, and `sealed_from` greater than `snapshot_id` as invalid states.
`OwnerObject` gains `std::optional<uint64_t> retired_at_ms`, serialized under the key `"rt"`; the field is absent for an owner that has never been retired.

The two budget-relevant ref-ledger encodings are pure sums of independent per-row or per-op byte contributions plus O(1) framing: snapshot rows depend only on their own fields, and hypothetical removal operations depend only on owner kind, ref name, and manifest reference.
The counters are pure functions of `(committed, precommits)`, so copying a `RefTableState` carries consistent totals without additional synchronization or scans.
The only row-population paths for `RefTableState` are `stateFromSnapshot` and `applyOpInPlace`; these are therefore the only paths that seed or maintain the body-byte counters.

The size helpers `committedRowEncodedSize`, `precommitRowEncodedSize`, `snapshotFramingSize`, `removalOpEncodedSize`, and `removalFramingSize` calculate sizes by using the same encoder fragments as the full formats, avoiding hand-written escaping or length arithmetic.

Counter maintenance covers add precommit, remove precommit, remove committed, promote, and set payload; `set_payload` changes only `snapshot_body_bytes` because the ref name and manifest reference used by removal encoding do not change.
The incremental `admits()` change does not alter the ref wire format or persisted data and needs no compatibility scaffolding because CAS is pre-release.
The incremental-budget implementation maintains `snapshot_body_bytes` and `removal_body_bytes` at five row-mutation sites in `applyOpInPlace` and seeds them once in `stateFromSnapshot`.
The incremental-budget size helpers are factored from the existing snapshot and log encoders so per-row and framing sizes remain byte-identical to full encoding by construction.
The incremental-budget change must preserve the snapshot and removal transaction wire formats and requires no `NativeFormat` specification update.

Each CAS ref-table recovery retry starts from a fresh `LIST`, and the recovery steps are idempotent because the seal uses a conditional `PUT` with a deterministic `seal_id` and resolves an already-landed identical seal as `Committed`.
`recovery_in_progress` already serializes same-table concurrent callers across the recovery window, so extending the retry loop does not change the recovery concurrency invariant.

After encapsulation, `RefTableState` keeps lifecycle, transaction, committed-map, precommit, and byte-counter storage private; external code reads through accessors and mutates state only through protocol entry points such as `applyRefLogTxn`, `replay`, `stateFromSnapshot`, and `admits`.

`submitBatch` enqueues ordinary per-item mutation records atomically but waits for all of the submitting group's items; concurrent items may join its flushes and existing same-ref and `WholeShard` carve rules remain unchanged.

When adding the next item's operations would exceed `ref_txn_max_ops`, the item and later unvalidated items are returned to the head of `pending` in order; the current flush proceeds without an exception.
`dropRefIfMatches` must perform its read-and-remove condition inside one `appendRefOps` builder, returning true only when the current committed binding equals the expected manifest.

The ref-ledger carve is two-phase: a throwing plan scans `pending` and reserves all capacity without mutation, then a no-throw publish under the same `ref_queue_mutex` pops selected items and moves them into `owned_items`.
The validation loop reserves `final_ops` and `survivors` before applying an item to `working`, and publishes `working` only after all accumulation operations that may throw have completed.

Each ref-ledger chunk is a complete commit boundary: it allocates a real transaction id, encodes and PUTs the chunk, applies it to `rt->state`, updates tail counters and metrics, completes that chunk's survivors, wakes waiters, and schedules snapshot publication before reseeding the next chunk from live state.

An item with more than `ref_txn_max_ops` operations fails alone, while removal-class items are exempt from the op cap only when their built operations contain `RemoveNamespace`; `WholeShard` scope alone is not the discriminator.
Streaming ref recovery applies decoded transactions one at a time into a private candidate `RefTableState` and never mutates live `rt.state` until complete recovery is ready.

Recovery publication installs every `RecoveryResult` field atomically under `state_mutex`, sets `recovered` last, and notifies waiters only after state, cleanup markers, snapshot identity, tail accounting, budgets, stale-precommit state, and recovery-seal facts are complete.

For chunk commit, the candidate is built by copying live state and applying the complete chunk with the real transaction id before PUT; after a committed PUT, the candidate is moved into `rt->state` under `state_mutex` and `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE`, then materialized outside the deny region.

The apply-pending marker transitions `Clean → ApplyPending` before a durable PUT, returns to `Clean` after successful apply or proven non-durability, and becomes terminal `Poisoned` when apply throws after durability; only fresh recovery clears `Poisoned`.

`precommitAdd` may take an unowned `ManifestId` only from the transaction that freshly staged it; already-committed idempotence remains a read-only no-op, making exact `ManifestRef` equality an ABA barrier.

An unresolved relink abort leaves the ref lane wedged until exact-GET resolution or remount; a landed abort PUT is applied before unwedging, while a never-landing PUT causes retry-later behavior and fail-long over-protection.

The stage-1 `RefReplayBuilder` owns a private candidate, applies decoded transactions in place, discards it on failure, and returns a complete `RecoveryResult`; vanished objects re-list, while decode or apply corruption fails fast.

`RefTableState::swap(RefTableState & other) noexcept` is the sanctioned post-durable installation operation, and member-wise swaps keep destruction of the old state outside the allocation-denied install region.

Wedge resolution is a post-durable install: it must install the decoded transaction exactly once by noexcept swap, clear the wedge in the deny region, and swallow a later `materializeCommitted` failure so the same transaction is not re-applied.
`precommitAdd` may introduce an unowned `ManifestId` only when the same transaction freshly staged it, except that the idempotent already-committed-to-this-exact-ref path remains legal.

`confirmExactRef` answers whether `ref_name` in a namespace still names exactly `manifest_ref` in the writer's committed view, performs zero object-store I/O, and returns `Unknown` for cold, evicted, or recovering tables instead of recovering them.

`NoAttemptSent` means both pre-attempt gates rejected before `backend->putIfAbsent`; therefore `commitRefChunk` must not install a wedge, while a fence lost after an attempt (`FenceLostMidWay`) must still wedge.

CAS removal classification and chunking share the same op-inspection discriminator: production `RemoveNamespace` is `WholeShard`-scoped and singleton-carved, while normal chunks split before exceeding the operation cap.
Recovery rejects raw or compressed ref-log bodies over the configured cap with `CORRUPTED_DATA`; corruption is not classified as transient and is rethrown instead of triggering a relist.
Current-build `set_published_at` ref-log encode, decode, and apply preserve the same ref name, expected manifest, and timestamp.

The final recovery memory guards use decoded transaction footprints and require both an upper bound near one transaction and a lower bound at least as large as the largest actual transaction, including an independent ledger recovery test.
`sealed_from` is paired with `newest_snapshot_id`: recovery seals install both values, while later ordinary or removed snapshots adopt a null `sealed_from` and clear the predecessor seal binding.

Ref transaction identifiers are allowed to have safe gaps: an append refused before any network attempt can leave a gap, so a missing id in an otherwise ordered sequence is not by itself evidence of incomplete enumeration.

Within each `(namespace, epoch)`, durable ref ids are dense from 1 through the greatest applied sequence, and the next id is `greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1`; the pool-wide `next_ref_sequence` allocator is removed.

Under the every-attempt rule, an id is freed only when nothing was sent or every sent attempt has its own conclusive rejection; a definite rejection after an ambiguous attempt keeps the namespace lane wedged.
