When the caller does not provide a transaction, `src/Storages/MergeTree/DataPartStorageOnDiskBase.cpp:514` creates a whole-part transaction for cloning, and `metadata_version.txt` is written inside that transaction at line 553.
Projection build, merge, and mutation call sites can always invoke `beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction`; the storage decides whether it owns the transaction.
`createHardLink` must stage the hardlink eagerly so `loadProjections` during the same finalization can see a carried-forward projection.
`DiskObjectStorage::supportsHardLinks` returns true for CAS to enable mutation, lightweight `DELETE`, and data-`ALTER` capability checks without selecting a per-file autocommit path.

`DataPartStorageOnDiskBase::freeze` wraps the whole clone in an owned transaction and writes `metadata_version.txt` inside it, preserving whole-part atomicity from many files to one manifest and one ref.
Projection tasks may call `commitTransaction` unconditionally because a borrowed CAS projection rides the parent transaction and its `commitTransaction` is a no-op.

For `ContentAddressed` disks, `checkAlterPartitionIsPossible` allows `DROP`, `ATTACH`, `REPLACE`, `MOVE`, `FETCH`, `FREEZE`, `UNFREEZE`, and `FORGET`, and rejects other partition commands fail-closed.

`MergeTreeDeduplicationLog::load` treats a missing `logs_dir` as normal for both Plain and `ContentAddressed` storage and still creates `current_writer`, because neither storage materializes empty directories.

`StorageMergeTree::supportTransaction` accepts a disk that reports `supportsTransactionalMutableFiles()` even when the disk does not support append, allowing CAS to persist per-part MVCC `txn_version.txt` in its per-ref sidecar.

Per-part write-time files uuid.txt, txn_version.txt, and metadata_version.txt are ordinary PartManifest entries, not a separate mutable sidecar; a single-file change on an already-committed part resolves through a committed-ref repoint that carries every unchanged entry forward and republishes one manifest, and a byte-identical rewrite is a zero-pool-mutation no-op (repointRef).

A SQL DROP PART/DROP PARTITION is modeled as removal supersession: an additive commit creates a real part ref, a removal creates an empty covering tombstone ref promoted from MergeTreeData::dropPartImpl's local Outdated empty covering part into a persisted, Active, covering ref using the existing ActiveDataPartSet/getActiveContainingPart covering machinery. This persisted part ref is distinct from the D1 shard-object tombstone, which is a journal marker letting GC reclaim an empty shard object.

DROP PART has a documented weak guarantee under a mid-range race with a concurrent merge: the merge may produce a real covering part carrying the data, so DROP PART can end up merged into a bigger part instead of deleting it (ReplicatedMergeTreeLogEntryData::getVirtualPartNames returns {} for DROP_PART). The persisted tombstone for a mid-range single part is therefore conditional/reconciled, not unconditional: if a real covering part wins the race, the tombstone must not strand or double-cover.

FREEZE must materialize real bytes into the local shadow/ directory and cannot be reference-only, because shadow/'s documented contract is filesystem-readable hardlinks consumed by external backup pipelines; freeze/freezeRemote/clonePart are independent IDataPartStorage virtuals not built on createHardLinkFrom. A self-describing snapshots/<name> ref-set may exist as an additional in-pool reachability root for restore-by-reference but does not replace byte materialization.

Since the all-tree part-files migration, filling in the creation CSN on COMMIT and locking/unlocking the removal TID on an already-committed part are ordinary committed-ref standalone writes through `repointRef`, not a special mutable-only case: every OTHER committed manifest entry is carried forward and a byte-identical rewrite resolves through `repointRef`'s byte-equal check with zero pool mutations.

An uncommitted INSERT inside an open transaction still publishes a CAS ref whose blobs stay GC-reachable via a `WriteSession` pin until the ref lands; the part is logically invisible via its `txn_version.txt` creation CSN. ROLLBACK removes the ref, after which the blobs become GC-eligible.

A transactional merge/mutation spanning multiple parts is keyed by a per-part staging map, `parts: (namespace, ref) -> PartStaging`, rather than a single `(table_uuid, part_name)`; a deferred rename (`tmp_merge_X -> X`) moves the staging entry to the destination key and merges it with any destination entry a deferred-window `txn_version.txt` write already created. `commit` takes the `gc_lock` once and iterates `parts`, applying the whole-part publish or the mutable-only branch per entry.

A transactional multi-part commit is not filesystem-atomic on CAS: MVCC visibility is gated by the per-part CSN/TID in `txn_version.txt`, not by disk-op atomicity, so CAS may publish parts one at a time; a crash mid-commit leaves some refs published and some not, and orphan refs are GC-reclaimed exactly as any uncommitted-then-abandoned build (B122).

CAS refuses BACKUP via temporary hard links for Ordinary (non-UUID) databases with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, while Atomic databases back up normally; partition commands are refused outside an explicit allowlist (DROP_PARTITION, DROP_DETACHED_PARTITION, FORGET_PARTITION, ATTACH_PARTITION, REPLACE_PARTITION, MOVE_PARTITION, FETCH_PARTITION, FREEZE_*, UNFREEZE_*); `supportsChmod`/`supportsStat` are false and `getHardlinkCount` returns 0; bucket versioning must not be enabled and is probed and refused; and `<readonly>1</readonly>` disks take no mount claim, run no probe, no writes, and no GC.

S06/S07 (10000/20000-column wide parts) confirmed the manifest encode/decode works correctly at scale: a 10000-column wide part commits under the manifest hard cap with no LIMIT_EXCEEDED needed, and the 1M-entry manifest cap is unreachable at any SQL-feasible column count (three orders of magnitude below 20000).

The removal driver resumes entry deletion idempotently on the owning writer's next mount after a stop in the `Removing`-without-`_ckpt` window; it never re-creates `_ckpt`, and the dead-root branch belongs to the decommission path instead.

`namespaceIsRemoved` gates its recreate-flip on the `_cleanup` marker and `dropNamespace` publishes a constant-size `Removed` snapshot; both reader-side predicates must be re-derived from catalog state (`Removing`, then entry-absent) before the `_cleanup` marker class can be deleted.
The writer no longer synchronizes a retired view or writer-side ack floor; it point-reads an add-only freshness meta at promote and copy-forward.
The planned registry-free newborn protocol creates a precommit-state shard fenced to the current `gcRound`, and gates `promote` on the shard's own `fence_round` rather than a registry fence.

A first publish into a new namespace uses the existing precommit machinery: the ref-shard becomes a precommit-state object, its `+1` is protected by the fold barrier, and there is no separate `pending-newborns` object.

Phase 2 makes `CachedPartFolderAccess` the owner of freshness policy and terminal committed-ref primitives while `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` retains path semantics and transactions retain staging orchestration.
Write-through erases are cache hygiene rather than a correctness dependency; `dropRefBestEffort` erases even when its underlying drop fails because durable ref state is then unknown.

The two-level write API puts terminal committed-ref primitives and `republishRef` in the facade, while `publishEntries` replaces the near-duplicate publish body of `adoptPartFromManifest` and transaction staging remains in the transaction.
Writer cleanup removes stale precommit ownership, and weak fairness of successor maintenance is expected to eventually clean pending stale ownership.
Dead-precommit removal moved from GC to the writer, which appends exact `owner_transition` removals; GC reclaims the resulting blobs through ordinary edge cancellation.

The borrowed-projection transaction rule removes six duplicated `if (!isContentAddressed()) begin/commitTransaction()` guards from merge and mutate paths; the two sites that decide whether a projection borrows the parent transaction remain unchanged.
Pool-member decommission performs full srid erasure of namespaces, manifest debris, staging, roots objects, and the slot, while subsequent normal GC rounds reclaim the now-unreferenced blob bytes.
On atomic-write storages, `VersionMetadataOnDisk` writes version information with one `writeFile` instead of a temporary file plus rename.

The freeze `metadata_version_written_by_freeze` special case is removed because an identical post-clone rewrite is absorbed by the byte-equal repoint no-op, while a differing rewrite may legally repoint.
`Pool/CasBlobUploader` moves byte-delivery execution out of `CasBuild`, while admit/adopt/resurrect decisions and dependency-set recording remain on the transaction class.
The proposed MOVE-to-CA fix is a CAS-aware `clonePart` path that stages the whole part in one `ContentAddressedTransaction`; the generic per-file cross-disk copy path is insufficient.
Whole-part atomicity sites such as `freeze`, restore-from-backup, and B58 projection commits remain single-`commit` transactions because this design deliberately introduces no `precommit` phase.

Verbatim table-level and mountpoint files are treated as an immediate autocommit class: writes are durable on finalize and deletes or moves remain durable at call time, avoiding a second timeline for those files.

The MOVE-to-CA design was reframed as one whole-part `ContentAddressedTransaction` threaded through the move, plus a layer-1 parser fix so the final part identity is used instead of `moving`; the earlier claim that a transactional copy would lack full build semantics was rejected.

Review finding №12's call-time mutation of durable refs is by design: `renameParts` is the commit point and rollback compensates with new operations over committed disk state, but `removeDirectory` must discard staged entries when removing a part before commit.
The generic fix closes every part disk-storage transaction in `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` after deferred renames, with no CA-specific code change.

The intended protocol is prepare durable and compensable storage before the Keeper decision, then apply visibility with a cheap finalize or compensate on abort; `renameParts` is the existing lock-free prepare slot.

The agreed fix model closes the disk transaction at `renameParts`; a later parts-transaction commit has nothing left to do on disk, while rollback performs compensation as a new operation over committed state.

For CA part moves, the crash-atomic design uses a transient `moving/<part>` reference prefix: `clonePart` commits under the moving reference and the mover later repoints it to the final reference, so startup cleanup can reclaim an orphaned moving reference.

The production INSERT topology commits one `ContentAddressedTransaction` per part, so cross-part batching must occur at the `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` seam rather than inside `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit`.

The phased engine uses one precommit ledger batch, one flattened cross-part upload wave, and one promote ledger batch; a 500-part INSERT is expected to reduce about 1026 serial ref-log PUTs to about two.

A plain INSERT performs one `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit()` per part with `parts.size() == 1`, so inner-loop parallelism cannot improve INSERT; cross-part concurrency must be introduced above the disk transaction.

The approved inner-loop design dispatches each part's unchanged `stageManifest → precommitAdd → uploadPendingBlobs → promote` sequence to bounded workers, preserving per-part ordering while overlapping parts.

The CAS commit pool must use bounded worker-loop callbacks or a dedicated pool sized by `cas_commit_concurrency`; scheduling one task per part on a shared 100-thread pool would not enforce the bound and could starve unrelated users.

The initial multi-commit design used `commitTransactions` as a transaction-centric seam: generic implementations loop sequentially, while `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` groups same-disk transactions without leaking `isContentAddressed` checks into generic MergeTree code.
`PreparedPartWrite` makes the receiver's durable `+1` and deferred promote an owned state: callers must explicitly `promote` or `abort`, because destruction of the handle alone is not cleanup.

Move assignment for `PreparedPartWrite` is deleted because overwriting a handle that still owes a terminal action may require a fallible `abandon`, which move assignment cannot report without dropping cleanup ownership.

The part-write release seam is relink-independent: any `PartWriteTxn` may leave a staged precommit whose release is unproven, and the accounting is intentionally not attributed to relink or another consumer.

`~PartWriteTxn`, rather than `~PreparedPartWrite`, owns the final release word because `prepareEntries` can fail before constructing a handle; the transaction destructor therefore covers both handle and no-handle staging exits.

`Poisoned` is not equivalent to a wedge: it means a durable transaction may be missing from the cached view, so it continues to block snapshot publication and triggers re-recovery; making `ApplyPending` debug-only is a follow-up, not part of Stage B.

The `RemovalReady` protocol is adopted as a transient catalog state between `Removing` and entry deletion: it is entered only after the terminal record has folded and the life-scoped cleanup item is durably `Completed`.

The final recommendation is to keep `NamespaceLifeId` and incarnation-qualified ref and namespace-file keys, avoid permanent `Retired` history and extra retirement markers, and delete a catalog entry only after terminal fold, cleanup/cursor retirement, and exact `_ckpt` deletion ordering is complete.

The incarnation is retained because temporary refusal alone cannot make omitted old physical objects safe for eventual same-name reuse; the generation makes old ref objects and namespace files structurally inert.

The `RemovalReady` state machine is `Creating -> Live -> Removing -> RemovalReady -> absent`; `RemovalReady` means no writer publication, recovery, ref fold, or new cursor is permitted, and only exact removal of the row is legal.

Physical `_files` debris is outside namespace rebirth gating; incomplete `LIST` may defer reclamation and leak bytes, but cannot expose an old file through a new life or prevent the new life from being admitted.

`Build::abandon` must call `retireBuildSeq` only after the precommit-removal `mutateShard`, so the build becomes watermark-dead only after its removal is durable; this ordering mirrors `Build::promote`.

The tokenless DETACH/freeze adopt path can race GC condemnation because `copyForwardFromCondemned` runs once before the CAS closure; the proposed fix is a bounded copy-forward and re-HEAD loop outside the closure, analogous to tokened resurrection.
SQL DROP PART or DROP PARTITION is represented by a covering tombstone ref in the CAS model, distinct from the D1 shard-object tombstone.
FREEZE uses one ref per frozen part rather than a shared container to avoid shared-`detached` read-modify-write and B66a torn-read hazards under concurrent freeze.

Catalog-only pre-fold erasure of a proved `Removing` lifecycle row is independent of the later physical destructive gate and must not be suppressed by unrelated later-round anomalies or carried holds.
Content-addressed storage requires a real transaction commit point, so `RegisterDiskObjectStorage.cpp` sets `needs_real_transaction=true` for CAS.

The consistency review recommends using `TemporaryFileOnDisk` for CAS spill cleanup and considering `WriteBuffer`'s idempotent `finalize`/`cancel` state machine for the duplicated write-sink lifetime state.

CAS should keep the logical part format Full; it changes physical representation and publication protocol, not the independent MergeTree files such as checksums.txt, columns, marks, projections, and metadata.
A candidate DataPartStorageContentAddressed would carry typed CAS root namespace, ref, and optional projection-relative prefix, while file operations add only the part-relative file name.
Build-root reachability and fail-closed commit are both required to prevent the `B140` dangle; either mechanism alone still has a counterexample.
The `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` order is precommit with durable closure, then adopt/observe, then promote; under this order promote-time revalidation of tokened leaves is redundant.

The `TXN-ONE-PIPELINE` design gives `IDiskTransaction::precommit` an explicit two-phase contract: CA precommit performs manifest publish through promote, CA commit materializes durable intent, and one `dispatch` funnel replaces the CA subclass.
The T6 retirement fence is correct: slot retirement is forbidden while any entry owned by the root remains, so the proposed exemption for just-transitioned `Removing` rows was rejected.

Projection sub-parts must use the parent part's whole-part transaction; commit `24f89d7ce78` routed merge/mutate projection sub-parts through that parent transaction, and commit `73b03c9a1e4` encapsulated the rule in borrowed projection storage.
`DataPartStorage` owns the rule for whether a projection storage opens its own transaction or borrows the parent transaction, so call sites do not need storage-specific transaction branches.
A logical clone of a part should be one operation represented by one disk transaction rather than independent autocommit file operations, especially for object-storage-like disks.

CAS cannot use early sub-part commits as a read-back mechanism because publishing a sub-part before its parent would expose a partial part; the sub-part must borrow the parent transaction and read staged files through its overlay.

CAS unlink operations were eagerly staged in memory and program order to fix the `01603` column-TTL ordering inversion; under the two-domain invariant, unlink dispatch remains eager while the durable delete is materialized as an intent at commit.

When `supportsAtomicFileWrites` is true, `VersionMetadataOnDisk` writes `txn_version.txt` directly instead of using a temporary file and `replaceFile`, because the storage itself provides atomic publication.

`DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction` are no-ops when `has_shared_transaction` is true, centralizing the rule that CA projections ride the parent whole-part transaction.
`getProjectionPartBuilder` sets `use_parent_transaction = !is_temp_projection || isContentAddressed()` so a CAS temporary projection sub-part shares the parent whole-part transaction.

`MergeTask` uses a `projection_uses_parent_transaction` flag and unconditional projection `beginTransaction`/`commitTransaction` calls so CAS projection sub-parts share the parent whole-part transaction.

Since Task 5's `supportsAtomicFileWrites` capability, `VersionMetadataOnDisk::storeInfoToDataPartStorage` writes `txn_version.txt` as a single atomic `writeFile` with no `.tmp` file and no `replaceFile` call; `ContentAddressedTransaction::moveFile`'s legacy mutable-per-part-file destination routing is dead code in production for CA, still present pending a later mechanical sweep but unreached by any current write path.

The optional age-based trickle warmer pushes blobs of hot parts older than a threshold `A` into the pool ahead of any snapshot, on the reasoning that a part surviving the young-merge window will likely reach the cold tier eventually; with the warmer on, consolidation degrades into publishing metadata only, and TTL moves become nearly free.

`kMutablePerPartFiles` was renamed to `kPerRefPartFiles` (with per-file rationale documented): `txn_version.txt` is genuinely mutable in-place (MVCC rewrites it after part publication) and stays a per-ref mutable sidecar; `uuid.txt` and `metadata_version.txt` are not mutated in-place under the single-owner-manifest model and were reclassified as ordinary immutable part files inside the manifest rather than sidecars, since the old dual-part-ref-sharing-one-manifest rationale for excluding them no longer applies once CAS stages a fresh `ManifestId` per ref.

The alleged abandoned copy-forward orphan exists only in a raw `putOverwrite` shape; in the real `republishRef` flow, `stageManifest` and `precommitAdd` precede promote, and the watermark plus fresh-token lifecycle self-heals a writer that dies after the copy-forward PUT.
The 56 retained blobs were traced to four `tmp-fetch_*` refs published and dropped within one 43 ms window; their `+1` was folded about three minutes after the drop and no `-1` was recorded.
Normal `Atomic` recreation creates a fresh table UUID and therefore a fresh namespace; it does not wait for the prior namespace to be removed.
Commit `6c495863667` introduced `rename_in_transaction` for lock-free part renames in `ReplicatedMergeTree`, and commit `3675c27fe9e` required explicit part renames in a transaction.

Scenario S37 passed 22 of 23 verdicts; all non-MOVE multi-disk legs passed, including policy placement, insert-time `max_data_part_size` routing, truthful `disk_name`, restart re-attach, and mixed-disk merge, while only cross-disk `clonePart` to CA failed.

Moving CA disk commit from `Transaction::commit` to `renameParts` moves S3 publish I/O off the `data_parts` lock without changing total I/O volume; the accepted cost is redo work when a later external decision rejects the part.

Publishing a cloned CA part directly under the final `<part>` reference before the mover swaps it is rejected because the final directory already exists and a crash can leave a committed final reference that moving-reference cleanup cannot reclaim.
Setting `alive = false` in `PartWriteTxn::promote` was rejected because existing promote-adjacent paths and the transaction destructor rely on current `abandon` no-op or soft-fail behavior.

Nested sub-manifests per projection (each projection its own sub-PartManifest plus a projections footer) were rejected as a format/version change requiring a recursive resolver for identity projections never use, since projections are always read as children and rebuilt on merge (YAGNI). A separate projections/ ref namespace lifecycle-linked to the parent was also rejected as a second namespace plus GC coupling for no benefit.

Task A5's detached-part-path fix anchors the reserved `detached` directory component left-to-right (first match), not the right-to-left scan the original spec sketched, because a right-to-left scan would incorrectly anchor on the inner part-dir-shaped component first.
A thread-local "active slot" design for the part-folder cache was rejected as unnecessary v1 complexity with no measurable benefit over a bounded shared map lookup.

The part-write crash-point table enumerates nine distinct crash windows (C1-C9) and their cleanup owner: C1 staging leaves local temp files (cleaned unconditionally) or S3 staging objects (cleaned only by the mount's own next-mount staging sweep, never on abort); C2 post-stageManifest-pre-precommitAdd leaves an unreferenced manifest cleaned by best-effort delete or the orphan sweep backstop; C3 an Unresolved precommitAdd leaves a possibly-live binding whose body is never writer-deleted; C4 between precommitAdd and promote has no resume path (INV-10) and is removed by abandon or a fenced successor's stale-precommit sweep; C5 mid blob fan-out leaves already-uploaded blobs as GC-reclaimable debris with nothing merged; C6 an Unresolved promote append leaves `CommitState::Uncertain`, mapped by the relink layer to "retry the whole fetch"; C7 a later part throwing after earlier parts published triggers precise rollback of only the refs this call created; C8 a destroyed uncommitted transaction has its destructor abandon every open build (INV-19); C9 a namespace dropped mid-build sets one atomic flag so every further op fails closed at `requireAlive`. Every row leaks at worst; no row loses data or dangles.

Free carry-forward on mutation (re-referencing unchanged column blobs without recompute) applies only to Wide parts, whose default remote-disk threshold is 1 GiB; Compact parts are a single blob and are always fully rewritten on mutation.
S36 is commissioned to test `ALTER TABLE ... MOVE PART|PARTITION TO DISK/VOLUME` in both local-to-CA and CA-to-local directions, including no dangling refs and round-trip deduplication.
The removal design must retain a negative test proving that cleanup failure or `_files` residue does not gate lifecycle completion, even when the bounded pass performs a best-effort `_files` listing.

The proposed spike should centralize DataPartStorageOnDiskFull construction, add a skeletal DataPartStorageContentAddressed for CA disks, implement one typed committed read and transactional write, test temporary-to-final rename and projection transaction sharing, and compare typed and path-derived routes.
The `B92` adopt path must populate the correct `tree_size` instead of leaving it at zero.

`ReadBufferFromFileView` must rebase position accounting from the implementation's real post-operation state and restore buffer swaps on exceptions; otherwise range reads can drift or retain swapped buffers.
Before the cache-over-CA fix, a `<type>cache</type>` disk over CA failed closed at `IDisk::startup` with code 48 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because the generic cache metadata wrapper hid the CA write path.
A cache disk over a content-addressed disk originally failed at startup because MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage did not forward isContentAddressed or the content-addressed transaction surface.

The 02941 projection failure was caused by `tryGetInFlightFileSize` and `tryGetInFlightStorageObjects` returning `blob_size` for an Inline entry, even though manifest decoding leaves Inline `blob_size` at zero and stores the real size in `inline_bytes`.

Review finding №16 is real: `ReadPipeline::tryBuildReaderExecutor` does not fall back for `file_view`, so a CA read can expose the `CHCA` envelope header and shift offsets when `use_reader_executor=1` and `remote_filesystem_read_method='read'`.

A five-hour CA soak failed when transient RustFS I/O saturation caused a CAS recovery-seal `NETWORK_ERROR`, after which `AsyncLoader` permanently cached the `ATTACH TABLE` failure without an automatic retry.
The CAS review triage confirmed that `ReaderExecutor` could bypass the `file_view` payload window and return wrong results; task T7 fixed the fallback condition in commit `aaf61086527`.

Generic `AsyncLoader` marks a failed async table-load job as terminal and later accesses rethrow the cached exception; `DETACH TABLE` can hit a catch-22 because table resolution waits for the failed job before reaching `eraseAsyncLoadState`.

A dense chaos-fault burst during CAS table-startup recovery caused the recovery seal PUT to exhaust its request envelope, after which `AsyncLoader` cached the table's `load table` job as `FAILED` and every later table touch rethrew the cached exception until a full server restart.

`DETACH TABLE` cannot clear a failed asynchronous table-load state because table resolution waits on the failed load before reaching `DatabaseOrdinary::detachTableUnlocked`, where `eraseAsyncLoadState` is called.

A transient backend failure during `AsyncLoader`-driven table or disk startup can permanently strand the table as `FAILED`; `DETACH` and `ATTACH` do not retry it, and only a server restart recovers it.

`DiskObjectStorage::prepareRead` downcasts to concrete `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`, bypassing the `IContentAddressedExchange` decorator seam and forcing generic cache wrappers to be bypassed for CA disks.
An unloaded lazy `MergeTree` can contribute no data to a backup because `StorageProxy` inherits the no-op default `IStorage::backupData`, which backup collection calls directly.
A lazy `MergeTree` exposed through `StorageProxy` currently reports false for `isMergeTree` and `supportsTTL` because those virtuals are not forwarded.
`StorageProxy` inherits `supportsOptimizationToSubcolumns`, so it can report support even when a nested engine such as `IStorageCluster` explicitly opts out.
The missing `StorageProxy::onActionLockRemove` forwarding is part of the `START` half of the action-lock incident because callers invoke it on the proxy.
`MergeTreeData` part loading enumerates through `iterateDirectory`; a benign-absent result on a not-live disk can silently attach an empty table over intact data.

A non-claiming reader has exactly one identified wrong-answer class: a superseded GC generation can disappear mid-scan, causing `openSourceEdgeRun` to throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` on a healthy pool; this is independent of mount ownership.
`ensureRefTableRecovered` and `resolveNamespaceLife` can mint a `Live` catalog entry and durable `_ckpt` from a read path, so `existsFile` on a never-born namespace can perform durable writes.

`existsFile` on a never-born namespace can mint a catalog entry and publish `_ckpt` from a read path, multiplying writes to the pool-wide catalog; `dropNamespace`, `listRefs`, and `resolveRef` were also identified as recover-and-mint paths.
The B117 fix stops `ReadBufferFromS3`'s outer retry loop after `KILL QUERY` by checking `CurrentThread::get().isQueryCanceled()`.
`CasObjectStorageBackend::get` and `getStream` can return bytes from one object version with the size and identity token obtained by an earlier `HEAD` from another version.
With `use_reader_executor=1`, CAS reads can expose the envelope header and use incorrect offsets because `ReadPipeline` rejects unsupported cache/decryption stages but not `file_view`.
Concurrent readers and writers of the same `detached/<part>` ref on local storage can observe a half-written object; S3 does not have this torn-read class because PUT completion is atomic.
`Store::resolveRef` hardcodes `.manifest_size = 0`, causing `PartFolderView::weight()` to undercount the manifest body because its weight is `bytes + manifest_size`.

`PartPathParser` duplicates the `store/<uuid[:3]>/<uuid>` fanout, detached and shadow names, mutable per-part file names, and part-name grammar instead of deriving them from canonical ClickHouse sources; its grammar misses the `patch-` prefix and format-version awareness.
A non-Atomic table named detached cannot always be distinguished from the reserved detached-parts directory when only the path string remains.

The committed read pipeline discards the resolved manifest and ref after planning a deferred blob GET, so dropping the ref and completing GC can make the later GET fail with `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` during a long read.
`readManifest` caches bytes fetched at GET token `Tg` under the preceding HEAD token `Th`, rather than under the token of the object whose bytes were decoded.

`ReadBufferFromFileView` could leave `file_offset_of_buffer_end` inconsistent when its inner buffer reset its working buffer during `setReadUntilPosition`, making `getPosition` incorrect and allowing seek or mark logic to reread an old decompressed block.
The outer retry loop in `ReadBufferFromS3::processException` could continue retrying transient errors after `KILL QUERY` even though the SDK retry strategy stopped on query cancellation.

The CAS read path re-parses the full part path on every IMetadataStorage call (existsFile/getFileSize/getStorageObjects/... each independently run parsePartFilePath plus route with ~10-15 small allocations), versus 1-2 allocations for non-CAS metadata backends; getView's cache-hit path additionally takes the per-table state_mutex and per-disk explain_mutex (a test/log-only decision journal) on every file-open plus two cacheKey() heap allocations, causing real serialization on wide-table/high-concurrency CAS SELECTs. Proposed fix: resolve the route once per file-open (memoize per raw path) and make the explain journal opt-in behind a setting, disabled by default.

The B115 `ReadBufferFromFileView` position-corruption bug was latent (not yet triggered) in `PackedFilesReader`, the only other in-tree consumer of `ReadBufferFromFileView`, because its current caller (`loadStatisticsPacked`) uses a sequential, non-seekable `CompressedReadBuffer` that never calls `setReadUntilPosition`; the fix is in place there too and the report flags this as upstream-relevant.

A coalesced shard read (single-flight read coalescing) has no deadline (F-N1): if the leader's GET hangs, all coalesced follower readers block indefinitely (a reader convoy) — a real liveness finding distinct from any correctness issue.

`DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::prepareRead` captures a raw `transaction.get()` pointer into a lambda, relying only on a prose comment asserting synchronous consumption "on this branch"; a future cache or async read stage could silently turn this into a dangling capture.
A live ref resolving to an absent manifest or blob raises FILE_DOESNT_EXIST rather than producing a silent empty read.
CachedPartFolderAccess is a bounded validate-on-hit cache of immutable PartFolderView snapshots and uses single-flight cold builds.
DiskObjectStorage::prepareRead serves inline or mutable bytes from memory and uses the standard object-storage read pipeline plus a bounded FileView stage for blob payload windows.
Snapshot-run consumers use streaming reads with fixed linear-scan requests of `head`, tail `get`, and forward-only `getStream`, retaining only the footer index and one block.
`getStream` is permitted only for write-once objects such as runs and seals; mutable objects remain on `get`.
