The public ClickHouse tree has no table-level durable part-registry interface such as IPartRegistry, IDataPartsStorage, or IPartCatalog.
CAS table refs represent the filesystem-like physical inventory, not the richer MergeTreeData active-parts registry or Keeper's expected per-replica part set.

For `Layout::parseNamespaceFileKey`, a key carrying `/_files/` is only a necessary trigger for namespace-file parsing, not sufficient proof that it is a real namespace file, because `Layout::mountpointObjectKey` does not enforce the `_files` reservation.

Raw object-storage paths are not a meaningful CAS filesystem interface: logical navigation from a part/ref to tree entries and blob content requires decoding manifests and trees; introspection must provide decoded views.

The fixture identity derivation is byte-for-byte equivalent to `NamespaceLifeId::stageATransition`: it uses `sipHash128` over the namespace string bytes, maps a zero hash to `1`, and calls `NamespaceLifeId::fromCatalogEntry(ns, incarnation)`; existing fixture keys therefore remain unchanged.
The persisted CasFoldSealFormat fields named gen and the gtest_cas_fold_seal_format.cpp golden value ,"gen":"7" remain unchanged because they are part of the persisted format.

The shared isCleanRelativeNamespaceFileName predicate is used by both Layout::namespaceFileKey and Layout::parseNamespaceFileKey, eliminating the prior parser asymmetry in which the parser accepted nonempty dirty names that the writer rejected.

The persisted fold-seal serialization key `gen` remains unchanged in `Formats/CasFoldSealFormat.cpp` and its golden test; `gc/gen/*` is likewise a persisted object-key path, not a renameable user-facing abbreviation.
The janitor model captures physical ids from LIST results and deletes by captured physical id rather than re-deriving a logical namespace name.
The janitor reclaims `_files` and `_ckpt` debris without reconstructing a namespace name or consulting `_path`.
The final S38 and S43 checks accept exactly one direct canonical lowercase 32-hex child below `cas/ns/stream/`; zero, multiple, malformed, uppercase, and nested children fail closed.

The negative `/_cleanup/` tests assert that removal, logical absence, same-name rebirth, and same-writer-epoch rebirth do not write a marker; the legacy namespace-bearing `_cleanup` test asserts that the generation-5 key is outside the final grammar.

`StaleReaderAfterSameNameRebirthNeverSeesSuccessorBytes` keeps the original storage/runtime alive across exact catalog removal and same-name rebirth; a stale disk read may return only predecessor bytes or absence, never successor bytes.

`DelayedInlineFinalizeCannotChangeSuccessorTokenOrBytes` requires an inline write opened under life 1 to finalize under life 1; life 2's backend token and bytes remain unchanged, with the typed stale-write exception also acceptable.

`IMetadataStorage` exposes in-flight read-your-writes methods, `isContentAddressed`, `supportsAtomicFileWrites`, and `supportsTransactionalMutableFiles`; the last capability indicates that per-part MVCC `txn_version.txt` can be persisted through a per-ref sidecar.
`IDisk` exposes `isContentAddressed` and `supportsAtomicFileWrites` capability predicates.
`DataPartStorageOnDiskBase` forwards `isContentAddressed` and `supportsAtomicFileWrites` to its disk.
`IDataPartStorage` exposes `isContentAddressed` and `supportsAtomicFileWrites` capability predicates.

CAS discovery LISTs use fixed prefixes: `cas/ns/stream/`, `cas/ns/`, `cas/manifests/`, `blobs/` (deliberately without the algorithm segment so one recursive LIST covers every hash algorithm), `roots/`, and `gc/server-roots/`. The `staging/` prefix is a top-level sibling that no GC LIST ever touches — it is reclaimed only by its own server's next mount.

`listDirectory`/`existsDirectory` branch by path shape in a fixed, load-bearing order — shadow, atomic-shard-dir, table-uuid, part-file, table-subdir, generic mirrored LIST — because `store/<u3>` and non-Atomic `data/<db>` would otherwise collide, so `isAtomicShardDir` must be consulted before `parseTableUuid`.

Every CAS key family is rooted at `POOL = pool_prefix`: blob body `POOL/blobs/<algo>/<S>/<hex>` (self-describing, `<S>`=first 2 hex chars); blob meta `POOL/blobs/<algo>/<S>/<hex>.meta`; part manifest `POOL/cas/manifests/<ns>/<epoch-hex>-<seq-hex>/<NNNNNN>.proto`; ref log txn `POOL/cas/refs/<ns>/_log/<render>`; ref snapshot `POOL/cas/refs/<ns>/_snap/<render>.proto`; ref cleanup marker `POOL/cas/refs/<ns>/_cleanup/<render>`; verbatim namespace file `POOL/roots/<ns>/_files/<name>`; plain mountpoint object `POOL/roots/<key>`; pool meta `POOL/_pool_meta`; GC state/heartbeat `POOL/gc/state`, `POOL/gc/hb`; GC generation artifacts `POOL/gc/gen/<gen>/attempt/<a>/...`; server-root control `POOL/gc/server-roots/<srid>/{owner,epoch,mount}`; opt-in staging `POOL/staging/<mount_id>/...` (a distinct top-level sibling GC never LISTs).

`blobsPrefix()` deliberately stays `POOL/blobs/` with no algo segment so a single recursive LIST returns every algo; strict key parsers (`parseBlobKey`, `parseManifestKey`, `parseRefObjectKey`) return `std::nullopt` (never throw) for foreign/malformed keys, treating them as debris rather than corruption.

`CasPoolMeta` (`_pool_meta`) is a pure protobuf `PoolMetaProto` holding `pool_id`, `root_shards`, `blob_header_len`, `min_reader_generation`, and a sorted append-only `algos_used[]`; invariants are `root_shards >= 1` and `blob_header_len` 8-aligned in `[96, 16384]`; admitting a new hash algorithm raises `min_reader_generation` to `G_BUILD` in the same CAS.
Phase 2 pluggable-hash `sha256` blobs are stored under the key shape `blobs/sha256/<shard>/<64-hex>`, distinct from the default 128-bit hash's `blobs/<aa>/<H>` layout.
S3-native staging is opt-in and streams to staging before a capability-probed conditional server-side-copy promote, with fail-closed fallback to local scratch.

The retired-in-snapshot plan makes each per-shard source-edge run carry condemned state at the existing zero-sentinel key, adds a per-shard `CondemnedSummary` to the fold seal, and removes `RetiredSet`, `CART`, `retiredKey`, and `GcState::retired_refs`.
`GcState::retired_refs` is removed and its protobuf field number is reserved; `GcState` retains round, fence, shard, snapshot, manifest-sweep, and lease fields without retired-object references.
A CAS pool may contain blobs under several hash algorithms without migration or rehashing; old blobs retain their original algorithm and new writes use the configured algorithm.
Settlement uses source-edge key schema 3 with key bytes `algo(u8) ++ digest[blobHashLenFor(algo)] ++ source_id(16 BE)`, producing 33-byte keys for 16-byte algorithms and 49-byte keys for SHA-256.
S3-native staging is opt-in per disk and off by default; large blobs stream to `POOL/staging/<mount_id>/<rnd>.tmp`, then promote to the content key by write-once conditional server-side copy.
`Layout::blobKey`, `Layout::blobMetaKey`, and `Layout::parseBlobKey` are defined in a dedicated `CasLayout.cpp` because including `CasBlobRef.h` from `CasLayout.h` would create an include cycle.

The pre-release CAS format cleanup removes the scalar `root_shards` from `PoolConfig`/`PoolMeta`, removes its proto field, and reserves proto field number 3 and name `root_shards`; the live `FoldResult::root_shards` vector is unrelated and must remain.

The `_precommits` namespace model and `isPrecommitNamespace` are dead because production ref keys use `_log/`, `_snap/`, and `_cleanup/`; their format modeling is removed without compatibility scaffolding.

The pure-visit pagination loops in `CasRefIntake.cpp` and `CasServerRoot.cpp` are candidates for a shared `forEachListedKey` helper, but adding stop-on-true or page-boundary control would require an interface design before migrating `deletePrefixWholesale` and namespace-cleanup passes.
All per-part files are designed to become ordinary manifest tree entries, making the per-ref mutable-file set empty.

The identity micro-header merge places `RootNamespace`, `Token`, `BlobDigest`, `BlobRef`, `ManifestId`, and `RefTxnId` in `CasTypes.h`, while codec and hex helpers remain in the separate `CasCodecUtil.h` file.
`CasPlainObjects` is stateless over `Backend &` and `const Layout &`, and `CasStore` retains the external API through thin delegates.
On the Atomic layout, `moving` already occupies the parser's part-directory position, so the L1 fix adds a `route()` case rather than changing `findPartDirComponent` for that layout.

The preferred S36/S37 fix is to keep placement-check payloads below `ROUTE_THRESHOLD_BYTES` at every scale by increasing part count rather than per-part bytes; raising `max_data_part_size_bytes` is less preferred because it weakens S37's deliberate 4 MiB routing test.

`_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and transaction-addressed, grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup; moving it to `state/` would require a second hot LIST or a simultaneous recovery-and-cleanup redesign.

The catalog entry's incarnation is the opaque physical `life_id` shared by the ref layer and namespace files; the logical `RootNamespace` remains in catalog entries and in-memory `NamespaceLifeId` values but is absent from life-owned object keys.

`_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and sequence-addressed, is grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup, and avoids a second hot LIST; the stream/state split is by access pattern, not ownership.

The CAS path boundary uses an `@cas@` archive suffix on the table directory, never as a standalone segment; a node is immutable exactly when it is content-addressed, and `@cas@` marks the content-addressed/verbatim boundary.
A projection is represented by nested `<proj>.proj/<file>` keys inside the parent part's single `PartManifest`; nested sub-manifests and a separate `projections/` ref namespace were rejected.
Removing the namespace registry requires two independent coordinates: a never-reused per-`(ns,shard)` incarnation for identity and the pool-global GC round as the newborn shard's self-fence.
The namespace registry can be deleted without an ephemeral `pending-newborns` fallback because the newborn self-floor plus per-round LIST fencing preserves `INV_NO_DANGLING`.
The D1 shard-incarnation and registry-removal work deleted `gc/registry`, stamps `ShardIncarnation` in `CasRootShardCodec.h`, and discovers the universe with `LIST`-based `discoverUniverse`.

`openObject` rejects a compressed body under a raw-compression policy, but passes a non-zstd body through verbatim under an `Always` policy as an intentional uncompressed-repair path; in normal operation `Always` objects are read through `.zst`-suffixed keys.
The candidate codec substrate may centralize version checks and named `UInt128` wire helpers, but must not unify or change the three existing on-disk byte orders.

The consistency review recommends using `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION` or `UNKNOWN_FORMAT` for future CAS on-disk versions, keeping `CORRUPTED_DATA` for malformed data and reserving `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for unsupported operations.

The embedded CARN stream in PartManifest should be retained only if PartManifest gains a real streaming reader or shares typed CARN validation; otherwise CAPT should become fully self-contained custom binary or protobuf

RunFile is justified for large sorted streams requiring bounded-memory merge, ranged seek, and replay or adoption of write-once run objects, but is less compelling for small embedded sections materialized whole
Typed CARN helpers should include openManifestEntriesRun, openBlobTargetRun, and openPartManifestCleanupRun and validate RunKind, key_schema, codec, and block-size invariants
Every self-describing CAS object in v2 begins with one universal 8-byte little-endian CasPreamble containing magic, writer_version, and compatibility_version
The shared v2 helpers encodeFramedProto and decodeFramedProto own framing, compression, magic, compatibility, and parse boilerplate; per-object codecs only map fields and validate invariants
v2 drops PartManifest.payload_digest because body_crc32c subsumes its guard role and the field was neither a key nor verified during reads
v3 makes every metadata byte human-readable with head, zstdcat, jq, less, and diff; raw blob payload remains the only non-metadata binary region
On mutable objects, additive JSON fields are designed to be safe-to-lose because an old-build read-modify-write can omit them until the pool floor rises
DataPartStorageContentAddressed addresses only part identity -> manifest entries and files; it does not replace table identity -> durable set of physical parts.

GC uses a hot `cas/refs/` path for listed reference metadata and a cold `cas/manifests/` path for cursor-paged manifest bodies; discovery is `GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/` with cost proportional to reference shards.
All part files, including previously mutable files, are content-addressed; committed-part repoint and an MVCC atomic-write short-circuit handle updates.

`DiskObjectStorageCache::wrapWithCache` must reuse the CAS metadata storage instead of a generic cache-passthrough wrapper because the generic wrapper hides `isContentAddressed` and concrete CAS types used by read and write paths.

`DiskObjectStorage::wrapWithCache` reuses the CA metadata storage directly instead of wrapping it in the generic `MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage`, because the generic wrapper would hide `isContentAddressed()` and the concrete types the CA read/write paths `dynamic_cast` to, forcing the write path into `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; only the object storage is cached, control-plane traffic bypasses the cache via the CA storage's own raw object-storage pointer.

The current `PartPathParser` behavior favors parsing real detached directories into the table namespace, so an exotic non-Atomic identifier named `detached` can be misparsed and `parseTableUuid` can return `nullopt` for its bare table directory.
The codecs-v3 audit concluded that all 15 live persisted CAS objects have text codecs under `Core/Formats/`, no `.proto` files remain, and both binary codecs were deleted.

With `root_shards=8` and a 96 KiB trim cap, observed shard bodies still reached 588 KB because the tail above the sealed cursor is round-cadence-bound; one key accumulated 8,471 leaked RustFS directories in 30 minutes.
A `ca_stress` Wide part wrote about 26.8 files but generated about 5.8 blob-body writes and one manifest write because small files were inlined into the manifest.
The v2 target reduces the format structure from five families plus one exception to three families plus explicit raw passthrough and reduces version gates to one name pair at one pre-parse position
v3 targets three families plus explicit raw passthrough, zero unversioned objects, one version field gated on line 1, and removal of protobuf and code generation from the subsystem
The multidisk placement policies used by S36 and S37 set `max_data_part_size_bytes` to `4194304` bytes (4 MiB) on their hot volumes.
S37 is commissioned to test multi-disk policies containing local and CA disks, including mixed-disk merges and atomic restart recovery during policy moves.

Unversioned RustFS overwrites of objects larger than 128 KiB leak the previous data directory; scanner reclamation found zero files after more than two hours, and LIST operations timed out around 600,000 files.

The clamped-shard incident was caused by RustFS false 404s on `HEAD` during a `rustfs#3231` metacache storm; the false 404s produced clamps, and clamp suppression prevented graduation over unfolded events until the storm ended.

The refined F2 root cause is RustFS issue `rustfs#3231`: overwriting objects larger than 128 KiB in an unversioned bucket leaks prior data directories, and metacache walks then time out and produce LIST storms and 503s.
Local or NFS multi-server pools can start with per-process conditional-operation emulation that violates CAS and GC invariants, because the implementation logs an INFO message and continues.
Unknown GCS bucket-versioning state fails open: inability to determine versioning only logs and continues, although enabled versioning archives generations and prevents GC from reclaiming storage.
RustFS failed the LIST-consistency passport by omitting keys that had been durable for 19 seconds, so conservative probe-always behavior remains the default.
A RustFS ref-log enumeration omitted durable predecessor keys `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` while returning later `0x1430e`; exact-key `GET` and `HEAD` still reported the omitted objects present.
Bucket versioning and versioning-suspended mode are rejected for the CA prefix because delete markers break the one-live-object model.
GC discovery requires strong LIST consistency: an object PUT before the LIST boundary must appear in the discovery result.
A generation-token store forces single-part conditional uploads and rejects versioned GCS buckets because exact-token delete would archive rather than reclaim the old generation.
CA requires server-enforced conditional PUT, COPY, and DELETE semantics, a write-time incarnation token, bucket versioning off, and strong LIST consistency.
The RustFS CA stateless job is required because MinIO OSS lacks the enforced conditional deletes needed by the incarnation pool's fail-closed probe.
CAS backup requires bucket versioning to be off; versioning-suspended buckets are rejected as well.

The backend must provide read-after-write visibility, conditional create via `putIfAbsent`, conditional overwrite via `casPut` or `putOverwrite`, exact-token deletion via `deleteExact`, no versioning or delete markers, and token-to-content stability.
The backend capability probe runs at every writable mount and refuses an object store that does not enforce the CAS conditions.
The D1 plan treats read-your-writes enumeration from `LIST(cas/refs/)` as load-bearing; a backend without that consistency is unsupported and must fail closed.
D1 requires strongly consistent LIST with read-your-writes enumeration; S3 is stated to provide it, while an unsupported backend must be documented and fail closed rather than use a silent fallback.
A generation-dialect GCS bucket with object versioning enabled is rejected with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because token-exact DELETE archives a noncurrent generation instead of reclaiming storage.

`isBucketVersioningEnabled` returns `std::nullopt` when the bucket versioning status is unknown or not applicable; the CAS probe fails closed when a generation-dialect storage explicitly reports versioning enabled.
A GCS versioned bucket is rejected even though per-operation conditional checks may pass, because versioning turns token-exact deletion into archival and silently prevents storage reclamation.

AWS S3 conforms to the CAS backend requirements: capability probing observes honest 412 responses for wrong-token conditional operations, two-phase reclaim deletes objects physically, and fsck remains clean through more than 28 GC rounds.
The GCS S3-compatible endpoint silently ignores `If-None-Match`, `If-Match` overwrite, and `If-Match` delete preconditions; notably, a wrong-ETag DELETE can delete the object.
A strongly consistent meta GET is a pool requirement because the writer must not adopt a body whose current incarnation has already been condemned.
The one-GET meta-adopt path requires a backend with strong read-after-write consistency; the plan identifies S3 since 2020 and RustFS as satisfying that requirement.

The required read-after-write visibility contract applies to both ref-log `LIST` and canonical ordering: a backend without visibility or ordering cannot enable the format and may not substitute an unbounded in-memory sort.
The supported platform wording for CAS object storage is: AWS and GCP work, Azure probably works, and other S3-compatible stores require atomic or conditional operations such as `If-None-Match`.

Predecessor omission below a correct LIST tail is legal on contract-compliant S3 for writes concurrent with a paginated enumeration because S3 provides no snapshot contract for keys landing during the walk.
Tail under-reporting of a completed write is illegal on a compliant store under the read-after-write clause and is the only LIST property a per-backend trust mode may rely on.
The fail-close default for LIST trust is probe-always, and RustFS currently fails the proposed passport by measurement.
The CAS capability probe requires an object store that enforces conditional operations, including wrong-token DELETE returning 412; the suite therefore uses RustFS `1.0.0-beta.8`, not MinIO.
The local or NFS backend is not safe for racy multi-writer put-if-absent use because it lacks the atomicity guarantees provided by S3 conditional PUTs.
The LIST-consistency probe in `Cas::Probe` is load-bearing before LIST-derived discovery can be trusted on a store, because S3 LIST may omit a just-PUT key.
The root-local part-manifest model assumes backend LIST consistency for shard discovery; the implementation must confirm strongly consistent LIST semantics per backend.

The pointer CAS design is supported by RustFS/AWS and S3-compatible GCS plus EmulatedSingleProcess, but Azure or non-S3 native object storage is not an admitted writable CAS backend under the current single-attempt retry profile
The CAS ref design relies on exact-GET and token-CAS backend semantics; a backend that violates those primitives is outside the admissible pool contract and must fail its capability probe.

If a backend advertises `supportsListTokens`, every listed item should provide a token compatible with `deleteExact` and matching `head`; otherwise the capability must distinguish no tokens from head-only tokens.

S3-native staging's real conditional-write/server-side-copy promote path is exercised only via RustFS in CI and integration tests, because MinIO OSS lacks the enforced conditional deletes the capability probe requires; the in-process gtest only covers the local-staging path.

Review finding №15 leaves shared local-pool startup behavior as a design decision because single-server ownership cannot be proved inside the process, and changing INFO to WARNING would break default CA-over-local tests.
Review finding №17 leaves unknown GCS bucket versioning as an explicit-WARNING tradeoff: confirmed `Enabled` fails, but an unverifiable check proceeds to avoid overly aggressive mount refusal.
A CAS bucket passport can be operator attestation per bucket, continuous verification with auto-revocation, or both; trust is a runtime property of a bucket rather than a backend type string.
The fix must tolerate an object store that returns inconsistent `LIST` results; RustFS demonstrated inconsistency and AWS S3 was untested at the time of the debt record.
Live GCS probes found that the S3-compatible surface silently ignores `If-None-Match` and `If-Match` on PUT and DELETE, so the CAS capability probe refuses that mode with exit 48.
GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 over the GCS XML endpoint enforced the full 12/12 conditional probe battery, showing that the CAS incompatibility is a signing-dialect problem rather than an API-migration problem.
With versioning disabled, CAS cannot use S3 CRR/SRR, AWS Backup for S3, S3 Object Lock, or Azure soft-delete and blob-versioning facilities that require versioning.
Garage was rejected as a CAS backend because it silently ignores conditional operations such as `If-None-Match`, while RustFS passed the conditional-write battery.

The CI RustFS setup required a downloaded arch-aware beta.9 binary because `start_rustfs` expected `ci/tmp/rustfs`; beta.9 passed the conditional-operation probes where a second `If-None-Match: *` PUT and a wrong-etag DELETE return 412.
A CA disk without an explicit scratch path creates `<data-path>/disks/<name>/cas_scratch/` at startup, and the parent `disks/` directory must be writable by the server user.

On generation-token backends, `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` defaults to 1 GiB and conditional writes larger than that are rejected with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; the limit is irrelevant to ETag-based AWS S3 backends.
The D1 design treats LIST consistency as load-bearing and requires RustFS and `InMemoryBackend` semantics to be confirmed; an unsupported backend must remain fail-closed.
Azure real-store GC validation remained the last leg of the real-S3 reclaim release gate after AWS and GCS validation.
Current integration tests use MinIO, but the production gate requires RustFS coverage because production S3-compatible backends enforce conditional PUT.
The shard-incarnation model assumes discovery equals present shards and therefore assumes strongly consistent backend LIST semantics.

A mount-time `Cas::Probe` should write a known key set, enumerate it, and refuse LIST-derived discovery on a backend that cannot return the set; the existing `list_consistency_hammer.py` is not this capability probe.
The CA integration harness uses RustFS rather than MinIO because the CAS tests require conditional-PUT semantics that MinIO did not enforce in the observed setup.
The factory configuration key gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes maps to the member gc_max_conditional_put_bytes_, dropping the s and making the member name misleading.
The metadata factory silently overrode the intended 32 `root_shards` with a default of 8; changing the factory default to 32 was verified live with shard indexes up to 27.
The equal 30-second S3 request timeout and mount lease TTL provide no operational timeout margin for protocol-significant writes.
Review finding №22 is real: `gc_interval_sec=0` causes back-to-back GC rounds, while `gc_shards=0` makes `gc/state` unreadable and can trigger modulo-by-zero, permanently wedging GC.

Review finding №31 is real: an explicit `staging_backend=s3` can silently fall back to local staging after a failed conditional-copy probe, unexpectedly consuming local disk and hiding a configuration mismatch.
The CAS review triage confirmed that zero-valued `gc_interval_sec` or `gc_shards` could cause a spin or permanent wedge; task T4 added bounds validation in commit `4fdbb3eaf11`.
`gc_interval_sec=0` can spin the scheduler and `gc_shards=0` can persist unreadable `gcs=0` state because bounds are not validated before opening the pool.
The new metadata storage can be selected directly with `metadata_type=content_addressed` without an `allow_experimental_*` gate.
Explicit `staging_backend=s3` can silently fall back to local staging after conditional-copy capability probing fails, hiding configuration errors and unexpectedly consuming local disk.
The capacity contract must use independent predicates encoded_catalog <= catalog_object_cap and fold_fixed_bytes + sum(reservation) <= fold_object_cap, accepting equality and refusing cap plus one

Risk register #11 (Medium, confirmed): a config-key/member naming trap exists where `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` is stored in a member named `gc_max_conditional_put_bytes_` (reads as garbage-collection, `MetadataStorageFactory.cpp:291` vs `.h:286`), and `root_shards` has a constructor default of 8 (`.h:73`) vs a factory default of 32 (`:251`) — a creation-time-only constant, so this is a real unit-vs-production divergence risk. Suggested action: rename the member; align the defaults.

For `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`, the ctor default for `root_shards_` is 8 while the factory's config default is 32; a pool minted via the ctor default (e.g. in a unit test bypassing the factory) is stuck at fanout 8 because `root_shards` is creation-time-only.
server_root_id must be a clean relative path without .., and two ClickHouse nodes must not share one server_root_id in the same pool.
server_root_id is required in the content-addressed disk configuration and is validated by Cas::validateServerRootId.
The `system.content_addressed_log` audit is enabled by default by the `<content_addressed_log>` configuration section and costs no rows or construction when no CAS disk is configured.
The `gc_shards` setting is fixed at pool creation and must be at least 1; it is not the same as the first-two-hex-digit S3 key sharding.
The `server_root_id` setting is required, immutable, and validated without sanitizing fallback; it roots `gc/server-roots/<srid>/`, `roots/<srid>/`, `cas/manifests/<srid>/`, and `staging/<srid>/`.

A generation-dialect CAS conditional write uses a single-part upload with the new `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` cap, defaulting to 1 GiB; a conditional write larger than the cap throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and names the future Compose path and setting.

The new write settings for generation stores are `s3_force_single_part_upload` (default `false`) and `s3_single_part_upload_max_bytes_override` (default `0`, disabled); setting the former makes `WriteBufferFromS3` refuse multipart creation.
`http_client = gcs_hmac` forces `ApiMode::GCS` even when credentials are present, because the SDK-side GCS accommodations must remain active for GOOG4 requests.

The generation-binding implementation's `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` cap buffers conditional single-PUT bodies in RAM; larger conditional writes fail rather than silently taking the multipart path.
`PoolMeta.algos_used` is a canonically sorted, append-only set of every algorithm ever admitted to the pool; once an algorithm is admitted, subsequent opens with it need no flag.
The write algorithm is node-local `PoolConfig`/`Store` state and is not persisted as a single pool-wide value, because live nodes may intentionally write with different already-admitted algorithms.
The disk setting `blob_hash` accepts `cityhash128`, `xxh3-128`, or `sha256`; unknown values fail with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and Phase 1 rejects `sha256` with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` until Phase 2.
A writer publishes a snapshot when log count or log bytes exceed thresholds, or after mount recovery exceeds a threshold; publication is off the mutation hot path and never blocks appends.
The default `cas_staging_backend=local` path is byte-for-byte the existing `scratchPath()` path; it performs no capability probe and takes no S3 staging branch.
The unclean-handover wait must satisfy `unclean handover wait >= all client timeouts + materialization_grace_ms`.
The GC configuration factory must reject `gc_interval_sec=0` and `gc_shards=0` before pool open, and `encodeGcState` must raise a runtime exception rather than rely on a release-inert `chassert`.
`lazy_load_tables` does not apply to views, materialized views, dictionaries, `TimeSeries`, table functions, or `FORCE_RESTORE` mode.

An explicit `use_fake_transaction=true` on a `content_addressed` disk silently selects per-file autocommit and removes the atomic manifest/ref commit point, so registration should reject it with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.

The refactored `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` constructor takes the object-storage pointer, key-compatibility prefix, server UUID, disk name, global context, and `const ContentAddressedSettings &`, with positional header defaults removed.
The per-write S3 override is `std::optional<bool> s3_check_objects_after_upload_override`; CAS sets it to `false`, and the override has the same polarity as `s3_check_objects_after_upload`.
The force-claim surface is `<force_owner_claim>true</force_owner_claim>` as a per-disk setting, defaulting to false and carried into `Cas::PoolConfig::force_owner_claim`.
`write_grace_ms` accepts any `UInt64` without additional validation; it flows from `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` through `PoolConfig::mountConfig()` into `MountConfig` and `CasMountRuntime`.
The CAS server setting names are `cas_blob_upload_pool_size` and `cas_condemned_upload_memory_bytes`.
The dead legacy disk-config keys `content_addressed_allow_shared_pool` and `content_addressed_gc_grace_sec` are not read and are removed from the skip-list and every configuration that sets them.
Per-disk CAS settings such as `scratch_path`, `gc_enabled`, and `server_root_id` remain unprefixed because they are scoped by their disk block.
The accepted metadata storage type spelling is `cas`, and `system.disks.metadata_type` renders it as `CAS`.
The CAS system log configuration sections are `<cas_log>` and `<cas_gc_log>`, corresponding to the tables `system.cas_log` and `system.cas_gc_log`.
The per-disk CAS settings are `deduplication_cache_bytes`, `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes`, and `gc_snapshot_generations_to_keep`.
The known-present blob cache is a bounded cost hint: reducing `deduplication_cache_bytes` may lower `CASBlobDeduplicationCacheHit` but must not change correctness.
All 10 CAS ParamSets belong in AltinityJobConfigs.cas_functional_tests_jobs rather than JobConfigs.functional_tests_jobs
