ci/jobs/functional_tests.py selects jobs using the --options parameter string rather than job objects
The capacity tests must separately accept equality and refuse cap plus one for encoded catalog size and fold_fixed_bytes plus reservation sum, while keeping the other predicate slack
Each capacity predicate needs its own equality-acceptance and cap-plus-one refusal tests that assert which named predicate failed
The persisted gc_shards value in cas_pool_meta is authoritative; a node reopening with a different local PoolConfig::gc_shards must use the persisted value

Format compatibility should guarantee that a new reader can read old object versions, while attempting to read an unknown newer version should fail safely; the proposed `max_content_adressable_pool_format` selects the write-version bundle while headers identify the read version.
The CAS privilege rows exposed by SHOW PRIVILEGES are byte-identical to the rows in 01271_show_privileges.reference:161-167, including tabs.

The canonical metadata storage type is cas: metadataTypeFromString accepts cas, registration uses registerMetadataStorageType("cas", …), and unknown content_addressed fails with UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG rather than acting as an alias.

CAS test-job options resolve through `--cas-storage` and `--cas-s3-storage`; the former `--content-addressed-storage` and `--content-addressed-s3-storage` options are not accepted by `tests/clickhouse-test` or `tests/config/install.sh`.

The legacy settings `<content_addressed_allow_shared_pool>` and `<content_addressed_gc_grace_sec>` were removed from CAS integration configs because unrecognized keys reach `impl->set` and raise an exception after Task 3 removed them from `non_cas_keys`.

The CAS storage settings in `ContentAddressedSettings::loadFromConfig` are direct children of the disk element: the loader calls `config.keys(config_prefix, ...)` and reads `config_prefix + "." + key`, so a nested `<content_addressed>` settings block is not part of the configuration contract.
The documented CAS configuration example uses only keys registered in `LIST_OF_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_SETTINGS`; the checked example contained no unregistered CAS setting names.

The current CAS metadata type is `cas`; the old `content_addressed` value, old config filename `content_addressed_*.xml`, and old stateless prefixes `content_addressed` and `ca_gc` are retired in favor of `cas_*`.
`MetadataStorageType::ContentAddressed` is registered as the `content_addressed` disk type.

`write_grace_ms` is independent of `cas_request_budget.operation_deadline_ms`, so a large grace plus a long remount can exceed a client's own request timeout; this is accepted because the client's own timeout then bounds the wait, and operators should size `write_grace_ms` near one lease TTL as the natural ceiling.

GCS generation-dialect mode is explicit: `http_client = gcp_oauth` enables the dialect for the existing OAuth client, and `http_client = gcs_hmac` selects `PocoHTTPClientGCSHMAC`; there is no endpoint auto-detection.
Without `http_client = gcs_hmac`, existing disks retain byte-identical wire behavior; GCS generation binding is explicit opt-in only.
The cache disk and policy remain opt-in because cache population and cache-mediated writes slow cold or single-pass workloads even though warm repeated reads benefit.
A new algorithm is admitted only with explicit `<blob_hash_allow_new>1</blob_hash_allow_new>` opt-in; reopening with an unadmitted algorithm and no flag fails with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.
The selectable blob hash defaults to `cityHash128` v1.0.2 and adds `xxh3-128` and `sha256`; the algorithm is encoded in blob paths and the feature is pre-release with no data migration.
`PoolConfig` is split into `RefLedgerConfig` and `MountConfig` slices while the aggregate `PoolConfig` remains public and external callers remain unchanged.

Review finding №14 leaves the `CityHash128` default as a design decision: `sha256` is available for hostile shared-pool threat models, while same-trust-domain replicas retain the default under the current model.
Review finding №29 leaves an experimental gate for `metadata_type=content_addressed` as upstream/release work, while the fork's soak and CI lanes intentionally remain ungated.
`CasBlobHashingWriteBuffer.cpp` must guard its OpenSSL include and SHA-256 implementation with `#if USE_SSL`, using fail-closed `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` behavior when SSL is unavailable.

`ContentAddressedSettings` is a declarative settings table that becomes the single source of defaults, rejects unknown non-object-storage keys, validates `gc_interval_sec`, `gc_shards`, and `server_root_id`, and parses enum-valued strings once into typed accessors.

The relink recovery work cap and global concurrency limit are source constants with no configuration knob, token bucket, cache segmentation, or fairness machinery; a nonzero cold-confirm share is the tripwire for revisiting that decision.
The metadata storage type string is changed from `content_addressed` to `cas`, and no compatibility alias is retained because the branch is unreleased.
The proposed adaptive GC cadence keys folding on per-shard journal pressure by size or age rather than changed-shard count, with a pool-specific `gc_interval_sec` direction of roughly 30–60 seconds.

The consistency review recommends settling CAS configuration on one scheme before release, preferably bare keys under the disk node such as `gc_enabled`, `gc_interval_sec`, `root_shards`, `dedup_cache_bytes`, and `scratch_path`.
CAS-over-S3 jobs use RustFS rather than MinIO OSS because the incarnation pool requires enforced conditional deletes
The capacity fix independently tests equality acceptance and cap-plus-one refusal for each predicate while keeping the other predicate slack

`SYSTEM JEMALLOC ENABLE PROFILE` is deprecated in the studied build and `jemalloc.prof.active = 1` can be misleading without actual samples; reliable profiling required `<jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>1</jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>` in the server configuration and a restart.

To capture a jemalloc heap profile on a build where `SYSTEM JEMALLOC ENABLE PROFILE` is deprecated, set `<jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>1</jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>` in server config and restart, then read symbolized samples via `SELECT line FROM system.jemalloc_profile_text SETTINGS jemalloc_profile_text_output_format='symbolized'` (jeprof-compatible with embedded symbols, no binary needed).

The GC scheduler uses gc_interval, gc_fold_threshold, gc_fold_max_defer_rounds, gc_snap_generations_to_keep, gc_shards, gc_meta_pool_size, mount_lease_ttl_ms, manifest_sweep_{list,delete}_budget_keys, and rebuild_edge_budget.
The local scratch directory configured by local_scratch_path must hold one complete part's staged blobs, and temporary files are deleted after upload.
The content_addressed factory defaults include gc_enabled=true, gc_interval_sec=60, root_shards=32, blob_hash=cityhash128, dedup_cache_bytes=64 MiB, and dedup_head_first_min_bytes=1 MiB.
Manifest backpressure delays writer-origin mutations between manifest_soft_limit and manifest_hard_limit and rejects mutations at or above the hard limit with LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
Manifest staging enforces a maximum of 1,048,576 entries, 256 MiB encoded size, 16 MiB total inline bytes, and 1 MiB per inline entry.
Lazy journal trim compacts a shard when trimmable events reach `gc_trim_min_events` (default 256, with 0 meaning eager) or encoded body size reaches `gc_trim_body_soft_limit` (default 8 MiB).
`PoolConfig::gc_snap_generations_to_keep` defaults to 3, and 0 disables generation retention pruning.
The mount lease expiry is `expires_at_ms = now_ms + config.mount_lease_ttl_ms`, and the keeper renews at `config.mount_renew_period`.
Conditional requests with bodies at least `expect_continue_min_bytes` negotiate `Expect: 100-continue`; the default threshold is 1 MiB and the per-disk setting can lower it.
The user-facing integration settings added outside the CA directory are `expect_continue_min_bytes`, `http_client = gcs_hmac | gcp_oauth`, and the internal conditional-write knobs in `WriteSettings`.
The adaptive large-blob HEAD-before-PUT threshold `dedup_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB.
The shipped factory default for `root_shards` is 32.
`shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` defaults to 200 and a value of 0 disables its TTL.
A CAS database used by the soak harness is created with `lazy_load_tables = 1` so transient startup recovery failures are retried on access instead of cached as terminal `FAILED` table-load errors.
`cas_request_budget.recovery_retry_budget_ms` defaults to 120 s for bounded recovery retries during CAS table startup.
`dedup_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB; below that threshold a speculative conditional PUT is preferred to a HEAD plus PUT unless the dedup cache already says the blob is present.
The default mount lease cadence is `mount_renew_period` 10 seconds with `mount_lease_ttl_ms` 30 seconds, and renewal uses token-guarded `putOverwrite` with `seq + 1`.
`gc_snap_generations_to_keep` defaults to 3; setting it to 0 keeps all generations for forensics.
Unknown content-addressed disk settings are rejected; `gc_enabled` defaults to `true`, `gc_interval_sec` defaults to 60 seconds, and `gc_shards` defaults to 1.
The planned GC skew margin defaults to `mount_lease_ttl_ms / 2` and comes from pool configuration without introducing a new user setting.
The proposed unified heartbeat cadence is 3–5 seconds, satisfying the watermark freshness requirement, the `mount_lease_ttl_ms` = 30 s TTL/3 rule, and GC acknowledgement latency bounds.

Production mount-reclaim polling is derived as approximately `mount_renew_period / 2`, with the margin approximately one poll interval; the wait uses the existing `mount_lease_ttl_ms` and `mount_renew_period` settings.
The exact CA disk setting controlling the generation-store conditional single-PUT budget is `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes`, with default `1ULL << 30`.
A server configuration template can expand `<server_root_id>{replica}</server_root_id>` per replica using the same macro expansion as the S3 `endpoint`.
The removed configuration keys `content_addressed_gc_grace_sec` and `content_addressed_allow_shared_pool` are not parsed and must not appear in soak configurations.

The validated CAS defaults are `root_shards=32` for the server default, 64 shards in soak configurations, and `gc_trim_body_soft_limit=8 MiB`; the 96 KiB experiment could not constrain the cursor-age-bound journal tail, while the 256-event count gate remains the effective trimmer.

The default `gc_fold_threshold = 1` preserves today's behavior for changed rounds and defers only zero-delta idle rounds; `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds = 8` is inert at threshold 1 and matters when batching is enabled with a threshold greater than 1.

`PoolConfig::gc_fold_threshold` is a `uint64_t` defaulting to 1, and `PoolConfig::gc_fold_max_defer_rounds` is a `uint64_t` defaulting to 8; the pure predicate is `shouldDeferRound(size_t, bool, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t)`.
The cache-over-CA test policy is named `cas_cache`, with CA disk `disk_ca_s3` wrapped by `disk_ca_s3_cache` using `<type>cache</type>` and a one-billion-byte local cache.
The retained part-folder view cache defaults to 64 MiB, `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entries` defaults to 10000, and `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` defaults to 16 MiB.
`cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 0` disables retained view caching and is a supported permanent operational configuration.

`manifest_decode_cache_bytes` defaults to 128 MiB and `0` disables manifest decode caching; the existing manifest-cache key remains `(ManifestId, Token)` so token changes force a miss and fresh decode.

The retained-view settings are `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 64 MiB`, `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entries = 10000`, and `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes = 16 MiB`; zero bytes disables retention.
The initial default for `ref_state_cache_bytes` is 256 MiB, and the obsolete Phase 1 design uses byte-bounded LRU caches for coherent namespace views and indexed run blocks.
The initial target size for a ref-base run is `Q = 8 MiB`, and ref-base PUTs satisfy `ref_base_puts <= ceil(S_next / Q) + 1` for `S_next` bytes in the complete next base.
`snapshot_min_log_age_ms` delays snapshot coverage of young logs to reduce the late-predecessor completion window, but it is a wall-clock risk reduction and not a correctness proof.

`cas_staging_backend` accepts `local` or `s3`, and `cas_s3_staging_min_bytes` defaults to approximately 64 MiB; blobs below the threshold remain on the local path and inline blobs at or below `INLINE_CAP` are unaffected.
Writable startup rejects configurations where `attempt_timeout + lease_safety_margin >= mount_lease_ttl`, and effective timeout-controller values are exposed in logs.

The current S3 defaults are a 1-second connect timeout, 30-second send/receive request timeout, 500 automatic retries for up to 501 HTTP attempts, a 30-second mount lease TTL, and a 10-second renewal period.

The initial configuration invariant is `attempt_timeout + lease_safety_margin < mount lease TTL`; the current 30-second attempt timeout with a 30-second lease TTL is rejected for protocol-significant writer operations.

CAS-specific settings include `cas_s3_connect_timeout_ms`, `cas_s3_attempt_timeout_ms`, `cas_s3_operation_timeout_ms`, `cas_s3_read_retry_attempts`, `cas_s3_conditional_write_retry_attempts = 0`, `cas_s3_retry_initial_backoff_ms`, `cas_s3_retry_max_backoff_ms`, and `cas_mount_lease_safety_margin_ms`.
`PoolConfig::skip_access_check` skips `runCapabilityProbe` while keeping a CAS mount writable; owner, epoch, mount, and watermark bootstrap writes still occur.

`CachedPartFolderAccess::CacheParams::explain_enabled` defaults to `false`; when disabled, `recordDecision` takes neither the journal mutex nor a journal allocation, while `getView` computes one cache key and reuses it.

`registerContentAddressedMetadataStorage` must use the `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes_` member name, throw `DB::Exception` with `NO_ELEMENTS_IN_CONFIG` when `server_root_id` is missing, and reconcile the `cas_` prefix on part-folder-cache keys.

The measured decision is to retain the factory default `dedup_cache_bytes` of 67108864 bytes (64 MiB); 256 MiB produced flat `CasBlobHead`, `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided`, PUT-class, and hit-rate results, so `MetadataStorageFactory.cpp:267` remains unchanged.

The proposed `part_folder_validate` setting has modes `always`, `age <X>`, and `never`; `always` is the current and default behavior, `age <X>` skips a body-validation `HEAD` for views validated within X seconds, and `never` removes the body re-proof while leaving `StrictValidate` callers unchanged.

Rev.6 defines the observation threshold as `mount_lease_ttl_ms + mount_lease_ttl_ms/20 + poll_interval_ms`, sets `materialization_grace_ms` to 30000 by default, uses seal id `RefTxnId{my_epoch - 1, UINT64_MAX}`, and bumps snapshot codec version 1 to 2 with `sealed_from`.

`materialization_grace_ms` is a `PoolConfig` setting with default 30000 and an XML key of the same name; an unclean or fenced mount boundary waits this grace before trusting recovery listings, while a clean boundary skips the wait.
`materialization_grace_ms` defaults to 30000 ms and is configurable.
The Round-B plan defines `part_folder_validate` as a string setting with `always`, `age <N>`, and `never` modes, defaulting to `always`.
The Round-B plan defines `dedup_cache_bytes` as an existing cache setting with a documented 64 MiB default and proposes measuring 64 MiB, 256 MiB, and 1 GiB variants.
A normal reference transaction is limited by `ref_txn_max_ops = 1000`; a transaction containing `RemoveNamespace` is a removal-class transaction subject to the 64 MiB byte budget.
`gc_interval_sec` and `gc_shards` must both be at least 1; zero values must fail with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` before opening a content-addressed pool.
The recovery retry budget defaults are `recovery_retry_budget_ms = 120000`, `recovery_retry_initial_backoff_ms = 1000`, and `recovery_retry_max_backoff_ms = 30000` in `CasRequestBudget`.

The opt-in database setting `lazy_load_tables` defaults to `false`; when enabled, a table attaches as a `StorageTableProxy` and its construction closure is discarded only after successful construction, so a failed construction is retried on the next access.
The proposed CAS recovery retry budget is a pool-level disk-configuration setting with a default of 120 seconds and exponential waits of 1, 2, 4 seconds and so on, capped at 30 seconds per wait.
For CAS databases, the design recommends creating the database with `ENGINE = Atomic SETTINGS lazy_load_tables = 1`.

The default `content_addressed_log` configuration should include `partition_by`, `max_size_rows`, `reserved_size_rows`, `buffer_size_rows_flush_threshold`, and `flush_on_crash`, while its `<ttl>` is a commented-out example.
The v2 ref-ledger budget uses an item cap of 1000, `ref_txn_max_ops` of 5000, and a per-operation encoded-size cap of 4 KiB; normal `ref_txn_max_bytes` is removed.
The proposed per-part concurrency setting is `cas_commit_concurrency`, with a default of 16.
`PoolConfig::cas_commit_concurrency` is planned as a `uint64` setting with default 16, while `cas_commit_pool_size` is a server setting with default 100 for the dedicated CAS commit pool.
The parallel-write implementation plan uses `cas_commit_concurrency` default 16 and a process-wide dedicated `cas_commit_pool_size` default 100, separate from the writer pool.
Normal ref-ledger admission uses `ref_txn_max_ops` 5000 and `kMaxRefBatch` 1000; the former byte-estimate admission and give-back spill are not used.

The normal-class whole-transaction decode cap is 20 MiB, the removal-class byte budget is 64 MiB via `ref_removal_max_bytes`, and normal-class operations have a 4 KiB per-operation cap enforced at admission and decode.
Stage 1 adds one server-level CAS upload-pool size setting and rejects an uninitialized or zero-sized pool; non-CAS disks and engines have no behavior change.
The stage-1 pool setting `content_addressed_blob_upload_pool_size` defaults to 16, rejects 0, and the pool getter throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before server or test initialization.

The condemned-upload memory setting `content_addressed_condemned_upload_memory_bytes` defaults to 0, meaning derived capacity of pool size multiplied by 64 MiB; the semaphore releases its permit only after `putOverwrite` returns and the body is destroyed.

Stage-1 ref admission uses a 4096-byte per-op limit checked both during admission and decode, a 20 MiB normal-class decode cap plus writer runtime throw, and a 64 MiB `ref_removal_max_bytes` budget with no op cap for removal-class transactions.

The 64 MiB CAS upload value is a chosen default per-task memory budget, not a blob-body size cap; blob bodies are uncapped and an overweight body is admitted exclusively using its actual header-plus-source weight.
`force_owner_claim` is an opt-in per-disk setting that permits a writable open with a differing configured server uuid to claim the server-root as WRITE only after a mount-slot death certificate.
`write_grace_ms` is a disk-level `ContentAddressedSettings` setting with default `0`; zero disables the feature and preserves today's immediate write failure behavior.

The default `gc_fold_threshold` is 1, so a touched active shard is folded and trimmed each round while idle rounds can defer; the proposed production cadence is roughly `gc_interval_sec` 30–60 seconds with journal-pressure triggering.

The idle-GC skip-unchanged mechanism uses `gc_fold_threshold` with default 1 and bounds deferral with `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`, default 8; `graduationDue` forces a fold before the deferral bound expires.
The CA upload path uses `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` with a default of 1 MiB, causing a HEAD-before-PUT for large blobs; on fresh data the measured 498/498 HEADs missed and avoided zero PUTs.
Resident-snapshot incremental GC uses `gc_checkpoint_records=4096` and `gc_checkpoint_rounds=64`; trimming is allowed only at or below the durable cursor, not merely the resident cursor.
`shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` defaults to 200, and absence is never TTL-cached.
A CAS disk is an `object_storage` disk with `metadata_type` set to `cas`; `<readonly>1</readonly>` disables mount-slot claims, capability probes, and writes.
The suggested retained-view setting is `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes = 64 MiB`.
Setting `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes` to `0` disables retained `PartFolderView` caching without bypassing the facade.
The view cache is bounded by `cas_part_folder_cache_bytes`, `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entries`, and `cas_part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes`.

The CAS configuration currently mixes `cas_scratch_path` with six `content_addressed_*` keys: `content_addressed_gc_enabled`, `content_addressed_gc_interval_sec`, `content_addressed_root_shards`, `content_addressed_dedup_cache_bytes`, `content_addressed_dedup_head_first_min_bytes`, and `content_addressed_gc_snap_generations_to_keep`.
The `system.cas_gc_log` table is created only when the `cas_gc_log` server setting is specified, and shipped `config.xml` enables it by default.
FoldSeal has separate limits of 64 KiB per line and 256 MiB per object

Fold-seal catalog admission reserves the full worst-case shape using saturating arithmetic: the widest fixed frame, one widest rfl row per catalog entry, and one widest btr plus cnd row for each persisted gc_shards value
v2 Proto bodies use one whole-body zstd frame when raw_len is at least the default 4 KiB threshold, while readers accept compressed and uncompressed bodies unconditionally
v2 caps Proto decode raw_len at 1 MiB for singletons, 64 MiB for CARS root shards, and 256 MiB for CAPT, retired sets, outcome logs, and fold seals
v2 stream objects have no body cap because resident memory is one block with a hard cap of 1 MiB plus a bounded footer index
v3 compression is whole-object single-frame zstd selected per type: Always types use a .zst key suffix and all other types are raw without a suffix
v3 line caps are 64 KiB for singleton and ref objects, 64 KiB descriptor lines for cas_part_manifest, 4 KiB for cas_run records, and exactly 256 bytes for the cas_blob header
Embedding every visited namespace in every fold seal is not bounded because fold seals have a 256 MiB control-object limit and namespace churn is unbounded
The `disk_transaction_wait_for_blob_removal` server setting defaults to `1` and makes the server wait for background blob removal to complete before acknowledging the operation.
Per-query jemalloc profiling uses `jemalloc_enable_profiler = 1`; `jemalloc_collect_profile_samples_in_trace_log = 1` additionally records per-query `JemallocSample` rows in `system.trace_log`.

The proposed root-shard journal controls are `max_unprocedded_journal_records_to_throw` for a hard write-failing limit and `max_unprocedded_journal_records_to_delay` for delaying writes when the journal is long.
`gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` defaults to 5000 manifest deletions per GC round, and the value `0` means unbounded cleanup.
The manifest orphan sweep lists at most 1000 keys and deletes at most 100 keys per round, so it cannot promptly drain a large budget-induced manifest-deletion debt.

`scratch_path` is a server-local filesystem directory for staging write-buffer data, defaults to `<clickhouse-path>/disks/<disk_name>/cas_scratch/`, and a relative override is anchored to the server data path.
`staging_backend` accepts `local` or `s3`; `local` is the default and stages in-flight part data locally, while `s3` enables S3-native staging.
`blob_hash` accepts `cityhash128` or `sha256`, and the pool records the choice so reopening with a disagreement fails closed.
`blob_hash_allow_new` defaults to `false` and must be enabled to admit a new blob-hash algorithm into an existing pool's recorded algorithm set.
`gc_enabled` defaults to `true`, and `gc_interval_sec` defaults to 60 seconds with a minimum value of 1 second.
`gc_shards` defaults to 1, must be at least 1, and is creation-time-only because persisted GC state is authoritative on reopen.
`deduplication_cache_bytes` defaults to 64 MiB, and `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB with `0` disabling the pre-upload `HEAD`.
`gc_snapshot_generations_to_keep` defaults to 3, while `manifest_sweep_list_budget_keys` and `manifest_sweep_delete_budget_keys` default to 1000 and 100 per round respectively.

`part_folder_cache_bytes` defaults to 64 MiB and `0` disables retention as a supported permanent operational configuration; `part_folder_cache_max_entries` defaults to 10000 and `part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` defaults to 16 MiB.
`part_folder_validate` defaults to `always`, also accepts `never` or `age <seconds>`, and controls how often a `ForceFresh` read re-proves a cached manifest body with `HEAD`.
`manifest_decode_cache_bytes` defaults to 128 MiB, and `0` disables decoded-manifest caching.
`gc_meta_pool_size` defaults to 16 and bounds the thread pool used for GC freshness-metadata writes during condemn, spare, and delete operations.
`publishCkpt` has `MAX_CKPT_CAS_ATTEMPTS = 100` attempt-bounded retries.
The CAS system-log members and their default table/config names are cas_gc_log and cas_log; CREATE_PUBLIC_MEMBERS stringifies the member name for both the default table name and the config prefix.
The server setting names are cas_blob_upload_pool_size and cas_condemned_upload_memory_bytes, and the system table is system.cas_mounts.

The CAS settings are named `deduplication_cache_bytes`, `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes`, and `gc_snapshot_generations_to_keep`; no compatibility alias for the former abbreviated names is provided.

`deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` sends a `HEAD` request before the upload body when `source.size >= cfg.deduplication_head_first_min_bytes`, allowing an already-present upload to be skipped; `0` disables this behavior.
`content_addressed_gc_grace_sec` is rejected as an unknown setting and there is no core retire-grace throttle associated with it.
`gc_round_graduation_budget` and `gc_round_redelete_budget` are `UInt64` settings with default `5000`; `0` means unbounded, and matching fields are carried through `PoolConfig`.
`gc_round_sweep_namespace_budget` defaults to `20` and `gc_round_sweep_recovery_op_budget` defaults to `5000`; both use `0` for unbounded work.
`gc_round_ref_cleanup_budget` defaults to `5000` and `gc_round_prefix_wholesale_budget` defaults to `20000`; `0` means unbounded for both settings.
`gc_round_outcome_entry_budget` defaults to `5000` and caps the cumulative number of `OutcomeEntry` rows appended across redelete and spared loops in one round; `0` is unbounded.
`gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` defaults to `5000` and limits the `manifest_deletes` phase; exhaustion records `skipped_budget` and leaves the undeleted manifests for a later reclaimer.
`gc_round_handoff_prefix_wholesale_budget` defaults to `5000` and is stored separately from the prune-only `gc_round_prefix_wholesale_budget`; its budget is consumed by the post-CAS hand-off reclaim.

The CAS S3 write plumbing uses `s3_skip_check_objects_after_upload`, `s3_force_single_part_upload`, `s3_single_part_upload_max_bytes_override`, `s3_max_unexpected_write_error_retries_override`, and `s3_client_override` for mutable-key overwrite tolerance, GCS single-part requirements, and per-write retry policy.

PocoHTTPClient injects Expect: 100-continue by default for any conditional S3 PUT >= 1 MiB (S3Defines.h DEFAULT_EXPECT_CONTINUE_MIN_BYTES = 1 MiB), applying to all S3 traffic including the pre-existing non-CAS Iceberg conditional-commit path, with no CAS-specific gate; this exists because of a real ~40-minute production stall (B118) but has zero test coverage. Proposed fix: scope it to CAS-owned writes via a WriteSettings flag (as done for s3_force_single_part_upload), or document the expect_continue_min_bytes default in release notes, plus add a mock-HTTP-server test for the 100-continue / body-skip branches.

`stageManifest`'s inline caps, enforced fail-closed before any body write (OQ7): max entries per manifest 1,048,576; max encoded manifest size 256 MiB; max total inline bytes per manifest 16 MiB; max single inline entry 1 MiB.

Manifest backpressure (B164b): when a root shard's encoded size crosses `manifest_soft_limit`, `mutateShard` introduces a linear write delay for writer-origin mutations (0 at the soft limit, `manifest_max_delay_ms` near `manifest_hard_limit`); at or above `manifest_hard_limit` the mutation is rejected `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; GC mutations are never delayed; a batch at the hard limit degrades to solo re-flushes so only the offending mutation is rejected and co-batched neighbors proceed.

The content-addressed disk configuration surface rejects unknown keys (with an explicit skip-list for generic object-storage-layer keys) and includes: `scratch_path` (default: server data path), `blob_hash` (default `cityhash128`, options `cityhash128`/`xxh3-128`/`sha256`, fixed at pool creation), `blob_hash_allow_new` (default `false`), `staging_backend` (default `local`; `s3` is opt-in and gated on the conditional-copy probe), `gc_meta_pool_size` (default 16), `manifest_sweep_list_budget_keys`/`manifest_sweep_delete_budget_keys` (default 1000/100), `dedup_cache_bytes` (default 64 MiB, 0 disables), `part_folder_cache_bytes`/`_max_entries`/`_max_entry_bytes` (default 64 MiB / 10000 / 16 MiB), `part_folder_validate` (default `always`; options `always`/`never`/`age <seconds>`), `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` (default 1 GiB), and `skip_access_check` (default `false`, skips the boot capability probe).

After weighing the clamp-attribution findings, the CAS `root_shards` default was raised from 8 back to 32 (the queue mechanism had already removed the contention argument for fewer shards; 32 shards yields a ~25 KB healthy journal tail with ~1.4x batching and 4x discovery-key fan-out), soak configs were raised to 64 shards for extra `rustfs#3231` margin, and `gc_trim_body_soft_limit` was restored from the 96 KiB experiment back to an 8 MiB backstop because the trim cap cannot bind body size at all — body size is cursor-age-bound (round-cadence-bound), not trim-bound, and the working trimmer is the 256-event count gate.

`trim_enabled` in the GC scheduler is a test-only seam (production always runs with it true); `setTrimEnabledForTest`/`setRebuildEdgeBudgetForTest` exist only for tests. Scheduler config keys are `gc_interval`, `gc_fold_threshold`, `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`, `gc_snap_generations_to_keep`, `gc_shards`, `gc_meta_pool_size`, `mount_lease_ttl_ms`, `manifest_sweep_{list,delete}_budget_keys`, `rebuild_edge_budget`; the heartbeat cadence is `hb_interval = max(50ms, interval/4)`.

The delete ThreadPool sizing (gc_delete_pool_size) for the meta-descriptor raw-body redesign starts at a default of 16 and is left to be validated/tuned by the soak task (Task 7 step 4), not fixed at design time.
No CA code capped `s3_max_connections` to backend permits, leaving a risk of 503 and retry storms under high concurrency.

Every technical claim in the consolidated documentation must be traceable to an old document or the code, and each target document must label relevant sections `DONE`, `TODO`, `REJECTED`, or `DESIRABLE`.

The consolidation keeps all `docs/superpowers/models/*.tla` and `*.cfg` sources untouched and also keeps the active D1 spec, plan, and model; their prose results and readmes may be consolidated separately.
The consolidation is explicitly synthesis rather than concatenation: new documents should remain manageable, and claims must not be invented.
New pages under `docs/en/` require frontmatter fields `description`, `sidebar_label`, `sidebar_position`, `slug`, `title`, and `doc_type`, and every heading requires an explicit kebab-case anchor.
CAS is described as experimental because the code is actively cleaned up and backward-incompatible format changes remain possible, while the implementation is intended to work correctly today.
The obscure-name cleanup changes CamelCase `Gc` to `GC`, `Ckpt` to `Checkpoint`, `Txns` to `Transactions`, and `Dedup` to `Deduplication` in user-facing CAS names.

The documentation-consolidation plan requires a small structured `docs/superpowers/cas/` set that captures load-bearing invariants, decisions, failed paths, and technical details without narrative noise.

The planned canonical CAS documentation set includes `README.md`, `01-architecture.md` through `08-testing-and-soak.md`, and `ROADMAP.md`, with topic-structured rather than dated or milestone-structured documents.
Published CAS pages are intended to be skimmable in about two minutes, use short prose with tables and Mermaid diagrams, and stay below a 300-line soft limit and a 500-line hard limit.
The canonical CAS spelling is `CAS` in CamelCase identifiers, SQL keywords, grants, and prose, and `cas` in snake_case table names, settings, config keys, test names, and tags.
CasPool.cpp line 1412's statement that a function has four callers is stale because the classification lists at least six non-test call sites.
Files ending in `.tla` or `.cfg` are never modified or deleted by the CAS documentation consolidation.
The Gate D coverage matrix is reviewed by the user before deletion, and `.tla`, `.cfg`, and `KEEP-IN-PLACE` files remain untouched.

Internal C++ names such as namespace `DB::Cas`, classes `CasPool`, `CasGc`, `CasLayout`, and `CasMountRuntime`, and files such as `ContentAddressedLog.cpp` remain unchanged by user-facing naming unification.

The TLA+ model sources, active D1 work, the consolidation design and plan, current D2 triage, the runfile streaming backlog, and the entire new `cas/` folder are explicitly retained rather than treated as deletion candidates.
Until the design questions are answered, DataPartStorageContentAddressed remains an architectural alternative rather than an implementation commitment.
The standalone `poc/cas_mergetree/` PoC is orphaned, superseded by `ContentAddressed/Core/`, referenced by nothing, and is deleted as repository hygiene.
`docs/superpowers/cas/AGENTS.md` is a persistent survivor that consolidates branch invariants, test recipes, delegation policy, known traps, and pointers for future agents.
Still-valuable, still-actual CAS specifications remain where they are as `KEEP-IN-PLACE`; other old corpus files are deleted only after coverage review.
The spelling indeg_zero in utils/ca-soak/scenarios/BACKLOG.md:273 is retained because it is a dated transcription of a past soak run rather than a live event name.
The user-visible exception texts containing B16/B34 in DataPartStorageOnDiskBase.cpp and MergeTreeData.cpp predate the naming effort and were intentionally left for a separate cleanup.
The renamed test `04328_reader_executor_modeled_cost_profile_event` verifies `ProfileEvents['ReaderExecutorModeledCostMicroseconds'] > 0` in `query_log`; it no longer tests asynchronous metrics.
The `ca-fix` agent performs only one small, precisely specified change and must stop and escalate when the fix is no longer primitive.
A `ca-fix` change that touches more sites than expected or requires a decision must be escalated instead of improvised.
CAS prose should cite symbols rather than line numbers because symbols survive source movement.
CAS prose should not carry mutable counts as claims.
A test or fence claim must state exactly what the assertion checks and must not imply coverage beyond that check.
CAS comments should explain the reason for a non-obvious decision, a complex algorithm, or a non-local invariant, and should not replace clearer code or types.
CAS comments must not reference plans, specs, ledgers, BACKLOG entries, review rounds, finding IDs, or task numbers; they should preserve the reason without unstable provenance.
The `ca-impl` agent treats the written brief as authoritative and asks before implementing when the brief is ambiguous or conflicts with the code.
The `ca-impl` agent must disclose deviations from the brief and explain why any requested work was skipped.
The `ca-review` verdict is written to a file and returned completely in the final message.

The docs consolidation project's own risk register names four risks and mitigations: docs describing a moving target (mitigated by HEAD-time verification and an experimental-format banner), false done/stale verdicts losing knowledge (mitigated by an evidence requirement plus a sampled adversarial audit at Gate M), map agents summarizing instead of extracting claims (mitigated by a one-claim-per-record rule and the Gate M missed-claim audit), and new docs bloating back into walls of text (mitigated by a per-page style gate with a volume limit and a diagonal-reading review test).
The asynchronous metric `ReaderExecutorModeledCostMsPerRequestedMiB` was removed from `ServerAsynchronousMetrics::updateImpl` and `ServerAsynchronousMetrics.h`.
The ProfileEvents `ReaderExecutorModeledCostMicroseconds` and `ReaderExecutorRequestedBytes` remain defined even though the asynchronous modeled-cost metric was removed.
Repository work by the `ca-fix` agent uses new commits only, never rebases, amends, or pushes, and stages changed files by explicit path rather than `git add -A`.
The `ca-arch` agent writes the complete decision answer to a file as well as returning it in the final message.
The `ca-impl` agent reports status, commit hashes, a one-line test summary, and concerns, and writes the full report to the dispatched path.

The scenario scratch high-water sampler was not reliable at scale because its 2-second interval missed the `OPTIMIZE FINAL` spike; direct measurement found 93 GiB while the sampler reported 0.100 GiB.

A background merge can rewrite payload inside S09's mutation measurement window and falsely report pool growth; consolidating with `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` before establishing the baseline isolates mutation carry-forward, while `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` also stops mutations because they use the merge scheduler.

After the per-server-tree relocation, manifests live under `cas/manifests/<srid>/...` and refs under `cas/refs/<srid>/...`; the old classifiers placed the tree in `other`, causing S08 to report 858081 objects and 138 GB as `other` and allowing a real manifest leak to pass the leftover verdict.

The harness `gc_log_rows` query used removed `forgotten_on_delete` and `forgotten_absent` columns, causing `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` on every poll and making every GC verdict in the 2026-07-05 campaign vacuous.
Before scoped and partial fsck, the scenario campaign lost five verdicts because fsck timed out at large object counts and returned no accumulated result.
The campaign harness `gc_log` query still referenced removed columns `forgotten_on_delete` and `forgotten_absent`, causing 213 `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` errors per night and empty `gc_log` capture.
The harness `pool_shape` classifier was stale after per-server-tree relocation: S08 classified 858081 objects and 138 GB as `other` while `_manifests=0` for a 100k-part pool.

The S24 replica-agreement failure was a harness timing issue: the check ran before replication converged because it lacked `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA`, while a post-run check showed identical 280-row replicas and checksum `8663329780789566770`.

Before the observability package, `system.content_addressed_log` could not show a manifest body birth or writer-side precommit removal, so a precommit created and never removed required raw-object decoding to diagnose.
Before `ca-inspect`, diagnosing a CA bucket object required an ephemeral `mc` container, an `od` hexdump, and hand parsing of protobuf or custom binary data even though decoders already existed.

The S16 strict resurrect scenario can fail deterministically when `forced_gc_to_fixpoint` deletes bodies before reinsertion, because reinsertion then performs a plain `blob_put` instead of resurrecting a condemned-but-present token; this is scenario-cycle tuning rather than a product bug.

The S06/S07 replica-agreement oracle sampled the second node roughly 0.8–0.9 seconds before the fetch landed because it lacked `SYNC REPLICA` or a bounded wait; the product was clean after the RustFS file-descriptor issue was fixed.
The S31 dry-run tool inspects only shard 0, so its result is a known tool-only gap rather than a CAS product verdict.
The S38 harness could make `assert_gc_no_failed` vacuous because `observe.py` queried the removed `min_ack` column and swallowed `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`.
The `CasBlobInDegree.h` documentation claiming that `previewDeletes` uses `inDegreeInGeneration` is false; `previewDeletes` uses `zeroInDegree` and a raw `kCondemned` scan.
The B199 recovery test fixture produced a foreign seal by appending `_FOREIGN_DIFFERENT` to valid seal bytes; after the formats-v3 cutover, that byte sequence is no longer a valid seal object.

The ASan battery scripts `build/asan_battery.sh` and `build/asan_battery2.sh` misidentified aborting tests because plain `grep` treated round logs containing embedded NUL bytes from CAS payloads as binary files.

The seven ASan memory-safety findings from rounds 9, 10, 18, 19, 20, 21, and 23 were independently identified from symbolized AddressSanitizer stacks and are unaffected by the faulty grep-based culprit heuristic.

`observe.gc_log_all(cl, since_inject).summary.success` under-counted S38 by returning 0 even though the raw GC log contained 40 post-injection Success rows; a timestamp-format versus `since` comparison is the prime suspected harness cause.

`quiesce_cluster` falsely marked S08 inconclusive because it failed immediately on any transient non-empty `replication_queue.last_exception` instead of applying the sibling backlog-stall grace period; commit `35faaae182c` added the grace period and two regression tests.

Seven ASan gtest findings were test-lifetime bugs rather than product bugs: six stack-use-after-scope cases came from an event-sink vector declared after `Pool`, and `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell` had a heap-use-after-free from reading `store->layout()` after `store.reset()`.

The CAS gtest battery's established `Cas*:CA*:...` filter had never matched about 89–90 tests in the `CaWiring*`, `CaTransaction*`, `CaDedupCache*`, `CaInlinePlacement*`, and `CaPartPathParser*` suites; correcting the filter exposed three bugs in `gtest_ca_wiring.cpp`.

Constructing `ReadBufferFromMemoryFileBase` with `owns_memory=true` and empty data can pass `nullptr` from `std::string_view::data()` to `memcpy` with length zero, violating the nonnull contract under UBSan.

The mount-lease renewal classifier, GCS conditional dialect tests, and dedup-log null-writer tests exposed `LOGICAL_ERROR` construction behavior that aborts debug or sanitizer builds before `catch` can run.
The `DispatchThrowStillDrains` test was racy because it could cancel the first scheduled task before task entry; a latch must prove that already-running work is drained before dispatch unwinds.

A pre-existing ref-writer test could spin forever because its polling loop waited for a pending item that the throwing pre-carve hook had already erased; pinning execution to one CPU reproduced the hang 8/8 times while an idle 32-core machine passed 10/10.

The CI scrape was post-mortem rather than concurrent: `ClickHouseProc.dump_system_tables` stops the server before using `clickhouse local`, and the CA pool is opened under an unrelated identity against the same data directory.
The obvious CAS gtest filter `Cas*:CA*` under-selects entire families such as `RefWriter*` and `CaWiring*`; the release gate must enumerate test families explicitly.

`CaBuildRootPrecommit.tla:300` had an unparenthesized `dupFlag' = dupFlag / (...)` precedence bug that could leave `dupFlag'` unspecified; the bug was latent because both affected sabotage configurations reached their invariant violation first.

The old TLA classifier pattern `[A-Za-z_]+` failed to recognize invariant names containing digits such as `I1ForgetTerminal` and `I2EarnedFarewell`; widening it to `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` was required to avoid false `error` outcomes and false passes based only on nonzero exit codes.

The T15 trace dump SELECT aliased `'${tt}' AS trace_type`, and ClickHouse alias resolution in `WHERE` caused the literal to shadow the table column, so the dump was an unfiltered mix of trace types until fix `52f110e94b3`.
`CaBuildRootPrecommit_empty_trees.cfg` failed because the model's explicit assumption was false when `Trees = {}`; this is a model-domain restriction, not a generic empty-set checker failure.
`CaRefWriterCleanupCore_empty_builds.cfg` reported a temporal violation for `StalePrecommitEventuallyGone` even though `Builds = {}` makes `StaleExists` false and `NoStale` true in every behavior.
The empty-build temporal violation was a defect in supplied TLC 2.19 (2024-08-08, revision `5a47802`), not a model defect: the same jar falsely rejected the tautology `EventuallyTrue == <> TRUE`.

`CaRefWriterCleanupCore_empty_builds.cfg` violates the temporal property `StalePrecommitEventuallyGone` under TLC 2.19, although the same model's independent invariant `NoStale` passes on the four-state graph.
`run_gclease.sh`, `run_gcshardincarnation.sh`, and `run_b140danglemerge.sh` accept any jar because they do not call `check_tlc_pin`; `run_gcrounddefer.sh` does call the pin check.

The CAS gate filter `Cas*:CA*` omitted `CaWiring`, `CaLifecycle`, several `RefWriter*` suites, and `RefTableCacheEviction`; twenty suites, including 17 CAS-relevant suites, were unclaimed by the gate.
`Mode::Native` tests ignore the unique storage root and write keys into the process working directory, making their namespace shared across all Native tests in the binary.

The pinned TLC runner had to recognize both `Temporal properties were violated.` and the named-property form `Temporal property EventuallyFolded was violated.`; otherwise `sab_unbounded_defer` was misclassified as an error.
Stale-edge residue remained permanently nominated-free across 145 GC rounds: the key-set fingerprint did not change and both `pending_gc` and `awaiting_gc` stayed zero.

The epoch-1 cohort was confirmed six-for-six as orphan-sweep deletions of manifests carrying unmatched `+1` edges; the two epoch-4 attributions remain unreliable and must not be presented as eight-for-eight.

The CAS suite gate initially missed `ContentAddressedSettings`, a six-test CAS suite whose file `gtest_content_addressed_settings.cpp` matched neither `gtest_ca*.cpp` nor `gtest_cas*.cpp`; those six tests had never been gated.
Renaming `CaWiring` to `CasWiring` would have merged it with the pre-existing bare `CasWiring` suite and silently combined unrelated tests.
The old README test filter contained dead components `CA*` and `RefSnapshotCodec*`, which matched no suite in either tested binary.
On ClickHouse 26.x, `SYSTEM JEMALLOC ENABLE PROFILE` can leave `prof.active` equal to `1` while producing dumps with zero stacks; a dump must contain `@ 0x` stack lines before the session is trusted.

The soak harness watched the removed `CasRefApplyPoisoned` profile event even though production had renamed it to `CasRefNeedsRecovery`, causing phase-3 preflight to abort until the watch list was updated.

run_cas_gate_per_suite.sh cannot execute parameterized suites whose names contain / because it redirects to a slash-bearing suite-derived log path without creating the nested directory; it also has a fixed 60-second timeout below two passing suites' ASan runtimes.

The first CAS suite enumeration missed a multiline INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P prefix, but the generator caught CasWinnerShape/CASGcCompletedRemovalFenceRace; the invariant must therefore be checked against the built binary rather than only line-based source enumeration.

`utils/ca-soak/scenarios/tests/test_render_tuned_config.py` was a red test because it still expected `<metadata_type>content_addressed</metadata_type>` after the setting value changed to `cas`; the assertion was corrected to `cas`.
`PutHookBackend::casPut` previously bypassed its immediate parent `HidingListBackend::casPut`, silently disabling `before_cas_put` and `ambiguous_cas_count` fault injection when composed.

`PostFoldUnreadableTerminalBackend::existsIgnoringFault` and the internal catalog probe in `CatalogAfterListBackend::list` bypassed `CountingBackend` counters, although only the former was behaviorally safe to route through its parent.
Passing `*before.token` to `casPut` unnecessarily dereferenced an optional before wrapping it again; passing `before.token` directly removes the UB risk without changing the call contract.
The tidy finisher found two broken `NOLINTNEXTLINE` placements and one missed `readability-make-member-function-const` diagnostic; all three were corrected before the final verification gate.
An fsck catalog-resolution ambiguity must be recorded as a finding rather than aborting the entire audit, and stateless golden `05020` must reflect the new report columns.

fsck's manifest-debris pass discovers namespaces via `store.listNamespaces` (`CasFsck.cpp:371`), which enumerates only `cas/refs/` and `roots/` (`CasStore.cpp:1640`), not `cas/manifests/`; a namespace whose only remnant is a staged `cas/manifests/...` body that `Build::abandon`'s best-effort cleanup missed (`CasBuild.cpp:958`) is not enumerated, so fsck under-reports it as unreachable even though the GC orphan sweep (which scans `cas/manifests/` directly) still reclaims it — a fsck diagnostics gap, not a leak.

An ASan battery run found 7 genuine memory-safety bugs among 49 peeled aborts: 6 stack-use-after-scope instances in `CasSweepLateLog`-family tests, root-caused to an event-sink lambda capturing a local `events` vector declared AFTER the `Pool` object, so `~Pool` emits terminate events into the already-destroyed vector (fixed by declaring the vector before the Pool); and 1 heap-use-after-free in `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell`, root-caused to a `const Layout &` held across `store.reset()` (fixed by taking it by value).

The ASan battery's culprit-detection scripts used plain `grep` (not `grep -a`) on archived round logs containing thousands of embedded NUL bytes from CAS blob payloads in stdout, causing silent misattribution: rounds 27-66 (39 consecutive rounds) were all the same unfixed `CasRefSnapshotFormat.RejectsSnapshotIdBelowSealedFrom` abort, never actually excluded, so the peeling loop looped on one bug while accumulating ~30 wrong bystander test names in the known-debt list; the fix switched the scripts to `grep -a` and the exclusion list was corrected from 58 down to 28 verified real culprits.
CI needed 6-hour-job-timeout sharding after a TSan lane finished 10,990/10,990 tests but was killed 16 seconds before it could report the result.

A CI fast-test build broke because `dbms` linked the dead `ch_contrib::crc32c` target left over from a phase-1a change, and the fast-test job does not initialize that submodule; the fix dropped the link so crc32c stayed google-cloud-cpp-only.

CAS GC's `gc_fold_begin`/`gc_fold_end` audit rows write only an anomaly count (e.g. `{anomalies: '1'}`) as `detail`; `recordAnomaly` takes namespace, shard, manifest and reason but none of it reaches the audited row, so a firing cannot be identified or distinguished from other anomaly classes after the fact.
B207 was a fsck phantom-dangle finding across a ref-walk/HEAD-confirm window.

The `ca-fsck` summary previously omitted `corrupted_runs` from its rendered summary line and exit code even though it was counted and part of `clean()`, so a failing seal checksum was invisible twice over; the summary line was moved into `Cas::formatFsckSummary` (reachable from a unit test) with `corrupted_runs` added.
Read-only CA mode skips capability probing, watermark and mount claims, and GC; `fsck`, `ca-gc-dryrun`, `ca-gc-rebuild`, and `ca-inspect` require a read-only disk.
`runFsck` recomputes reachability from authoritative refs rather than GC snapshots and performs no writes.
`runFsck` labels `Reachable`, `Dangling`, `Unreachable`, `PendingGc`, `AwaitingGc`, `Unaccounted`, and `SnapshotOracleMismatch` objects, and `Unaccounted` is never used as a reachability input.
The strongest whole-pool test oracle is `runFsck().dangling == 0` for no loss and `runFsck().unreachable == 0` after reclamation for no leak.
`clickhouse-disks ca-fsck --disk <ca_disk_name>` opens the CAS disk read-only, walks live refs and trees through the production read API, and enumerates the pool prefix with paginated `backend.list`.
Under the ack-floor pipeline, `pending-gc` and `awaiting-gc` present-but-unreferenced objects are expected transient classes rather than leaks.
`unchecked` means the audit could prove neither a healthy frontier nor a broken chain; it is a coverage result that does not make the report unclean or exit nonzero.
A read-only `ca-fsck` records a per-namespace `CORRUPTED_DATA` failure and continues scanning other namespaces instead of stopping at the first damaged namespace.

`ca-fsck` exits nonzero for `dangling`, `chain_broken`, `corrupted_runs`, or `lifeless_keys`, but never exits nonzero solely for `stale_edge`; a zero exit code therefore does not prove a clean pool without checking `stale_edge`.
`clickhouse-disks ca-gc-dryrun --disk <ca_disk_name>` is read-only and derives next-round delete candidates from `gc/snap` and `gc/state` without CAS writes or deletes.
`ca-gc-dryrun` is read-only and write-free, can over-report away from quiescence because it does not fold new owner events, and its output must never drive a real delete.
No obsolete document may be deleted until a coverage matrix maps it to a canonical section and a fresh sanity audit confirms that its load-bearing content is present.

`claimMountAwaitingExpiry` accepts injectable wall-clock and sleep functions so unit tests can advance a fake clock without real sleeping; production uses a system-clock reader and `std::this_thread::sleep_for`.

The CAS harness's transport probes are best-effort: failures return `None` or an empty sentinel rather than raising, and a scenario that requires a missing observation must be marked inconclusive rather than pass silently.

`classify_pool_path` recognizes pool-relative and prefixed keys and returns one of `blobs`, `_manifests`, `refs`, `roots`, `gc`, `_files`, `_pool_meta`, or `other`; `RECLAIMABLE_UNREACHABLE_PREFIXES` remains `(`"blobs"`, `"_manifests"`)`.

`FsckReport` partial mode returns accumulated lower-bound counts with `partial=true` and `partial_reason` when a deadline raises `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED`; without partial mode the timeout exception is preserved.

`runFsck` namespace scoping uses `namespace_prefix`, checks only matching references, performs dangling-only HEAD verification of named blobs, and intentionally skips pool-wide unreachable/pending/unaccounted classification.

`ca-inspect` renders `u128`, token, and hash fields as lowercase hexadecimal and reports decode failures rather than emitting partial or guessed output.
`ca-inspect` requires a read-only-opened content-addressed object-storage disk and performs no CAS, delete, or mutation operation.
The unit-testable `caInspectToJson` interface has signature `String caInspectToJson(const Layout & layout, const String & key, std::string_view bytes)`.
ca-inspect must dispatch .meta keys before the blobs/ body branch, and ca-fsck reports meta_without_body as an invariant violation while body_without_meta is benign pre-birth debris.

`ca-fsck` reports `meta_without_body` for a meta with no body as an `INV-META-BODY` violation, reports `body_without_meta` for a body with no meta as benign pre-meta-birth debris, and `clean()` requires both `dangling == 0` and `meta_without_body == 0`.
Under raw bodies, `ca-inspect` dispatches `.meta` keys to `BlobMeta` decoding and renders non-meta `blobs/` keys as raw blobs with size and a hash-match check rather than decoding an envelope.

`PutHookBackend : HidingListBackend : CountingBackend`; therefore `PutHookBackend::casPut` must route through `HidingListBackend::casPut` to compose both hook layers.

Every positive CAS scenario in the S01-S35 suite must satisfy: SQL correctness (all replicas match the scenario oracle's aggregates), storage correctness (`ca-fsck --detail` reports `dangling = 0`), GC safety (`ca-gc-dryrun` delete candidates are a subset of the `ca-fsck` unreachable set at quiescence), a clean event audit (`system.content_addressed_log` has no error-class event types), no `Failed` GC-round finish rows, no unbounded leftovers after forced GC, and no excessive resource growth beyond the scenario budget.

The soak harness's chaos model applies seeded faults defined by `{t_offset, target in {ch1,ch2,both,rustfs}, action in {kill-9, restart, pause/unpause}, duration}`; faults are bounded so a quiescent checkpoint is always reachable between them, and a server that does not recover within the bound is treated as a correctness failure, not a flake.

`SYSTEM ... GC` reuses the scheduler's existing `Gc` instance (a per-call one-shot would acquire the lease once then back off forever, since the steal protocol needs a stable gc_id); only the log record's Trigger differs (Manual vs scheduled). `SYSTEM ... GC REBUILD [FORCE]` instead constructs a one-shot `Gc` and calls `rebuildBaseline`, which recomputes the in-degree snapshot from raw owner state, mints numbering above every surviving ack, publishes a fresh seal, and CASes gc/state — it is live-conservative, fail-closed on refusals, and never deletes content.

The "no-leftovers pool drain" oracle requires that after DROP, `blobs/` and `parts/` drain back to baseline, inspected directly on the object store (stateless `04290`, integration `test_content_addressed_gc_s3`, `test_content_addressed_shared_pool`).

Migration is recreate-only: pool format generations and backward floors advance together, old-format startup fails closed at pool open, and no dual reader or in-place converter is provided.

Pool recreation is refused while a live mount lease of any format generation exists; after the owner is terminalized, the recreated pool claims normally and a delayed old-writer write is fenced out.

The layout transition to opaque `life_id` keys is a recreate-only generation-6 cut, and the removal lifecycle's `_cleanup` deletion and `ref_lives` fold-seal transition is a separate recreate-only generation-7 wire cut; older generations are refused rather than dual-read or migrated.

The carve apply phase creates a temporary worktree at `tmp/carve-worktree` from `git merge-base $BASE $SRC`, checks out or removes each classified source file in manifest order, and commits each non-empty group with its group message.

The carve completeness invariant requires `git diff <branch>..$SRC --name-only` restricted by the exclude pathspecs to be empty; the script prints unrestricted differences as the discarded report summarized by exclude category.

Within `tests/queries/0_stateless/`, added files belong to the new CAS stateless-test group and modified files belong to the old-test-tag group; this requires `--name-status` plus `added-only` and `modified-only` path matching.

The carve script must hard-fail on an unmatched diff file, a completeness-invariant violation, or an existing target branch without `--force`; an empty group is warning-only, and the script must not use sleep-style waiting or push.

The carve stateless-test group matches only added files under `tests/queries/`, while the CI/tag group matches only modified files under that tree; this prevents new tests and old-test tag edits from sharing a commit.

The planned completeness check compares `git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD $SRC_SHA`, counts only paths matching EXCLUDES as discarded, and reports every non-excluded difference as a lost file before failing.
