The user-facing disk commands are `cas-fsck`, `cas-gc-dryrun`, `cas-gc-rebuild`, `cas-inspect`, and `cas-drop-member`; the deprecated `fsck` alias and `CommandFsckDeprecated` factory and registration were removed, while C++ class names such as `CommandCaInspect` were retained.
`clickhouse disks --query 'help'` lists the five `cas-*` commands and no `fsck`; querying `fsck` exits 36 and prints the available-command listing.

The temporary-hard-link `BACKUP` path is rejected for CAS with a fail-closed exception because it clones files through a non-part temporary path; Atomic and UUID databases use the pointer-holding path that round-trips.
`MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup` uses a `restore_tx` whole-part transaction for atomic restore, mirroring `freeze`.

The classic `clickhouse-backup` (Altinity) freeze-and-copy mode is incompatible with CAS because there are no local metadata files and no filesystem shadow (shadow lives in-pool as refs); only its embedded mode, which wraps native `BACKUP`, applies.

Logical export (Iceberg/Parquet/datalake) is the ultimate independence tier (readable without ClickHouse, directly queryable by other engines) but is lossy: `AggregateFunction` states do not survive Parquet, and `LowCardinality`, codecs, skip indexes, projections, and physical `ORDER BY` layout are all lost; restore is a full re-insert, the longest RTO in the survey.
Fence-out settles liveness only; a fenced member's watermark, precommits, staging debris, roots, and mount slot remain until deliberate operator decommission.
Read-only CAS mode supports a WORM deployment with one writer server and multiple read-only mounters sharing the pool.

The current backup scope can omit `gc/*` because GC state is rebuildable with `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` or `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild`; the durable data scope is `blobs/ + cas/ + roots/ + _pool_meta`.

The ack-floor migration is pre-release and does not support persisted-data compatibility or mixed-version pools; it removes watermark objects, `fence_version`, per-round retired sets, and fence/recheck paths, starts with an empty retired list, and carries folded tokens and cursors through existing seals.
CAS pool layout changes from v3 metadata are handled by recreating development pools; there is no migration, compatibility scaffolding, dual read path, or configuration flag.
The staging capability probe must perform a conditional copy and demand a real 412 on a second copy; support of conditional `PutObject` alone does not prove conditional-copy support.
The all-tree CAS change is pre-release and does not add compatibility scaffolding; pools are recreated and ref-log and snapshot payload formats may change freely.

The eight-step codecs-v3 migration order is bootstrap, control plane, refsnaplog, blob meta, runs, part manifest, blob envelope, and finish; each format cuts over atomically in one commit without a dual-read arm.

Phase 1 creates `Core/Formats/` with the moved and extended `CasFormat` registry, `CasTextFormat`, a shared format test battery, and a README registry skeleton without converting any production format.
Phase 2 uses a hard per-object cutover with no proto-then-text fallback; a half-migrated tree is acceptable because the objects are CAS-by-token or write-once and each cutover is atomic.

The protobuf graveyard is deleted only after grep proves that no production or test code references `cas_format.pb.h`, `clickhouse::cas::format`, or `cas_format.proto`; phase 2 removes `Core/Proto/` and the `clickhouse_cas_proto` build and link wiring because the eight control-plane objects were its only consumers.

The GC sequence removes probe A first, then enables catalog-authoritative destructive GC and runs a sequential destructive baseline before adding `MultiDelete` or parallel deletes, so performance effects can be separated from correctness regressions.

The generation-6 opaque-life layout cut and generation-7 unified ref-life wire cut are recreate-only format boundaries with no compatibility parser, copy-forward path, or fallback that reinterprets older name-keyed objects as current life-keyed files.

The branch reconstruction goal is to build only upstream fixes, the CAS subsystem, its integration, tests, CI wiring, and user-facing documentation as a readable grouped commit series on top of `altinity/antalya-26.6`.
The carve manifest excludes `docs/superpowers/`, `.superpowers/`, `utils/ca-soak/`, `utils/cas-gate/`, `utils/cas-carve/`, `tmp/`, `.gitignore`, and `tests/broken_tests.yaml`.

Files under `docs/superpowers/`, `.superpowers/`, `utils/ca-soak/`, `utils/cas-gate/`, `utils/cas-carve/`, `tmp/`, `.claude/`, `.gitignore`, and `tests/broken_tests.yaml` are deliberately excluded from the carved branch as worklogs, model/report artifacts, gate infrastructure, agent tooling, artifacts, or test metadata.

The carve classifier cannot distinguish junk files placed inside an included directory glob, so hygiene of included source directories remains a review concern; file moves may change which grouped commit carries a file without changing the feature tip.

The coverage audit considers the backup/restore source a thin RESTORE bug-fix specification rather than architecture: `BACKUP` read-side works, while `RESTORE` must materialize each part through one whole-part commit rather than per-file autocommit.
The pre-release pool format does not owe compatibility scaffolding or a dual protocol; a format bump is preferred because no persisted production data exists.
Prefix recreation requires a fresh prefix or exact owner and lease terminalization plus writer drain before reuse

Existing pre-release or soak pools require a quiesced format bump and recreation; startup against the old format must fail closed with a message naming pool recreation, while any preservation requires a separate offline migration protocol.
A pool-format policy should fail closed at mount for a newer `pool_format_version`, keep immutable blob/tree/envelope formats non-migratable, and state explicitly that downgrade is unsupported.
The current decommission feature is implemented without the durable roster through `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER` and `ca-drop-member`; roster removal remains a future hook.
`allow_s3_native_copy` cannot optimize native `BACKUP` from CAS because a blob contains an envelope header and may use inline or shared placement, so raw `CopyObject` cannot produce file bytes.
A CREATE-side targeted lifecycle assist is a possible latency optimization, but it must use the normal durable terminal, cleanup, retirement, and cursor-pruning protocol and cannot bypass it.

The carve script does not promise per-commit buildability, hunk-level splitting of mixed files, history rewriting or preservation, pushing, pull-request creation, or building; only the reconstructed tip must equal the source tree minus excluded paths.

A reference-only `FREEZE` was rejected because `shadow/` is contractually filesystem-readable through hardlinks for external backup pipelines; the backup design instead uses snapshot, mirror, fetch, and restore verbs.
The deliberate member-removal command is `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER '<server_id>' FROM DISK '<disk>'`, with CLI equivalent `clickhouse-disks ca-drop-member`.
The SQL command `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD [FORCE] [<disk>]` uses the same global `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` access right as a regular GC command.
`clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild [--force]` requires a read-only CA mount but writes exactly one `gc/state` CAS on success.
Offline `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild [--force]` requires `<readonly>true</readonly>` and must never claim a live server's mount.

Writer startup recovery performs one namespace `LIST`, selects the greatest valid snapshot, GETs it, GETs and replays later logs in `RefTxnId` order, then caches the complete state before enabling mutations.

CA stateless retries require unique disk names as well as unique paths because the disk registry is keyed by name; `${CLICKHOUSE_TEST_UNIQUE_NAME}` and `${CLICKHOUSE_USER_FILES_UNIQUE}` are used for the test fix.

The fail-closed CAS test teardown is `DROP TABLE <table> SYNC`, then `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET '<disk>'`, verify `vanished(forgotten)` in `system.content_addressed_mounts`, and only then remove the pool directory.

Before each carve regeneration, run `utils/cas-carve/carve.sh --check`; if the base advances, merge it into the working branch, let the merge-base move, and remove groups reported as empty when their fixes were absorbed upstream.
The planned apply phase uses `git worktree add -b $BRANCH $WT $MB`, commits each group with `git commit -F -`, and removes the temporary worktree on exit while retaining the branch.
A fresh soak pool is created by `docker compose down -v` followed by `up -d`, because the compose RustFS container is ephemeral and teardown wipes the fixed `test/soak_pool/` prefix.

`ca-drop-member` refuses a victim whose mount lease is alive or contended; with `mount_lease_ttl_ms=30000` and `mount_renew_period=10000`, the decommission path must wait for lease expiry because it has no `FORCE` variant.

`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD [FORCE] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name] disk_name` rebuilds a CAS disk's `gc/state` baseline by rediscovering the complete ref universe and refolding manifest edges into a fresh generation.

Both `server_root_id` and `disk_name` are required string literals for `SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER`; `server_root_id` is an opaque server-root path that may contain `/` and therefore cannot be written as an unquoted identifier.

For the CAS naming-unification migration, old `content_addressed`/`ca` names embedded in many `.reference` test files must be changed in the same commit as the corresponding code change; correctness for this migration is checked by grep review of user-facing surfaces, not by running the stateless test suite.
A first-release CAS pool format needs a self-describing version breadcrumb, a format freeze, a durable roster, and rollout machinery for `max_content_addressable_pool_format`.

Existing tables need a migration path using `ALTER TABLE ... MOVE PARTITION` to repack onto a `content_addressed` disk, with a mixed-version rule of read-new-before-write-new and a fail-closed format self-check.

A CA-aware cross-disk offload should reuse `checksums.txt` `file_hash`, stream directly to `blobs/<H>/0` without local scratch, verify the digest by default, and prefer metadata-only relink for same-pool moves.

The new CAS S3 functional-test CI lane calls `CH.start_rustfs()`, which only checks for a pre-existing `ci/tmp/rustfs` binary and returns `False` if missing; unlike `setup_minio.sh` for MinIO, no tracked script downloads/extracts the RustFS binary, so the lane fails deterministically on a clean CI runner. Fix direction: add a tracked `setup_rustfs.sh` mirroring `setup_minio.sh` that pulls/extracts the `rustfs/rustfs:1.0.0-beta.8` static binary into `ci/tmp/rustfs`, invoked before the CAS s3 job's `start()`.

Six ProfileEvents—`ContentAddressedGenerationResurrectionsTotal`, `ContentAddressedDuplicateGenerationBytes`, `ContentAddressedTombstonesTotal`, `ContentAddressedGenerationsObserved`, `ContentAddressedHashesObserved`, and `ContentAddressedOrphanBytesEstimate`—have zero increment sites and describe a removed design.
Mount events emitted inside `Store::open` are dropped because the CA event sink is installed only after open completes.

The previously observed S01 memory bug was caused by `Build::putBlob` materializing a staged `BlobSource` into a `String`; streaming through `uploadFromSource` reduced a 2 GiB INSERT peak from 13 GiB to 4.33 GiB.

D2 found that the S23 idle-pool `s3_ops` metric incorrectly summed `*Microseconds` ProfileEvents as operation counts; the measured CAS counts were `CasRootList=0 CasRootGet=0 CasGcGet=71 CasGcPut=24 CasGcList=9` and `S3ReadRequestsCount=17`.
Container-cgroup `memory.peak` includes page cache and was measured at 5–21 times the ClickHouse-tracked peak, so memory verdicts based on it are unreliable.
The campaign harness hid sustained 10–20% S3 read-error rates because verdict tables asserted operation counts but not error rates.
CAS had no `CurrentMetrics` or `AsynchronousMetrics` gauges; its introspection surface consisted of historical log tables and monotone counters.
Mount and lease state, including slot holder, renewal health, and fencing, was visible outside `err.log` only after adding the proposed introspection package.

CAS retry-later failures were opaque because the message said `retry budget exhausted` even for a pre-attempt fence rejection, and the failures were logged at Information level without populating `system.replication_queue.last_exception`.

Review finding №30 is real for started disks: `system.content_addressed_mounts` skips listing exceptions and can make a failed listing appear as no mounts, although not-started disks are legitimately skipped.

The initial S23 RSS failure was allocator retention and fresh-boot warmup rather than a GC or log-flushing leak: the 86-second empty-pool run had sawtooth RSS, while `MemoryTracking` grew only about 50–70 MiB and the remainder was allocator dirty-page residency.

The corrected S23 `MemoryTracking` failure was generic ClickHouse boot warmup: the non-leader `ch2` grew more than the leader despite running zero GC folds, and the CAS pool contained zero blobs, manifests, refs, and roots.

S38 failed twice because no `ref_late_log_detected` event appeared during the 240-second post-injection poll window after injecting a dead-epoch late log at key `.../_log/0000000000000001-fffffffffffffffe`.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` currently reports the querying server's `is_leader`, `pending_reclaim`, `last_success_age_seconds`, and `wedged_namespace_count` values on every peer row.

The GC scenario harness once queried the removed `min_ack` column, converted the resulting `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` into an empty list, and thereby made every GC verdict vacuously true until the observation error path was fixed.
Deferred GC rounds previously logged as `round 0` because the defer path returned before assigning `report.round`, making skipped rounds indistinguishable from empty folds.

`Gc::CasGc.cpp` phase markers are already inconsistent: the audit found 17 `PHASE N/19` markers with 9 and 17 missing and 15 duplicated, while the test phase list has 19 names including `pre_fold_ref_drain`.
Three hammer runs listing about 19 million keys produced zero holes before the rare LIST violation occurred live within four minutes of an ordinary soak.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` can silently return partial results when obtaining the pool or listing mounts fails because the exception is caught and omitted.

A GC scheduler retry loop used a fixed interval without backoff, failure counting, or a circuit breaker, and `system.content_addressed_mounts` exposed only `last_success_age_seconds` for the resulting health state.

`system.remote_data_paths` did not push down `WHERE disk_name = ...`, causing it to walk every disk and recursively LIST the shared CA-s3 ref namespace; the CA-s3 lane measured 872 LIST requests with 436 first-attempt timeouts.
The mount-lease keeper can be silent at the default log level during a fence-to-remount episode, leaving renewal failure, fence arming, remount phases, and completion absent from the server log.

All scenario GC verdicts became vacuous when `framework/observe.gc_log_rows` queried the removed `min_ack` column, caught `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, and returned an empty row set; `assert_gc_no_failed` then passed on empty input.

The consistency review identifies `CasDbgExistsHit`, `CasDbgExistsMiss`, `CasDbgMetaHit`, and `CasDbgMetaMiss` plus the `casDbgSampleHeadMiss` sampler as throwaway debug instrumentation exposed through permanent `system.events` metrics and a hot S3 HEAD path.
The soak criterion zero wedged-forever lanes contradicts the accepted possibility of a permanently quiet unacknowledged wedge until a later foreground flush or remount opportunity
Quarantine backoff bounds only anchor and repair point reads; every fold still pays for two global ref-prefix enumerations, held-namespace grouping, Probe A comparisons, and larger fold seals
The `gc_anomaly` event must capture a `HEAD` verdict while a LIST/arithmetic disagreement exists, because present and absent are opposite defects and cannot be distinguished reliably after the fact.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC RUN` creates a fresh `Cas::Gc` and is unsynchronized with the background loop, so repeated manual calls cannot accumulate lease-steal observations and may run duplicate leaders.
The `CasGcIsLeader` and `CasGcPendingReclaimEntries` `CurrentMetrics` gauges are process-global rather than per disk, so one CA disk can hide another disk's stuck GC.

`utils/ca-soak/soak/signals.py` lists `("fold_ref_list", "ref_folding_aborted")` in `DETECTOR_METRICS`, but the server emits the metric under phase `fold_ref_group`; `summarize_phases` silently skips the missing phase, so `fold_ref_list.ref_folding_aborted` never appears in the detector summary or formatted operator line.
`utils/ca-soak/scripts/soak_watch.sh` still issued `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS content_addressed_log`, but that table no longer exists after the CAS naming change.
`CasObjectPut` has never existed in `src/Common/ProfileEvents.cpp`; the soak query's `CasObjectPut` alternative was removed, leaving the working `CASBlobPut` metric name unchanged.
Formatting an error with `fmt::format(...)` before passing it to `S3Exception` loses the static `message_format_string`, degrading grouping in `system.text_log` and `system.errors`.

The two new CAS system logs (content_addressed_log, content_addressed_garbage_collection_log) ship enabled-by-default, yet SystemLog.h documents content_addressed_log as "off by default" -- the comment and config.xml default disagree and need reconciling.

On the studied Altinity build, `SYSTEM JEMALLOC FLUSH PROFILE` writes a `.heap` file plus an empty `.heap.collapsed` and no `.symbolized` file, and `system.asynchronous_metrics`'s `jemalloc.prof.active` can read 1 even when `prof.thread_active_init=0` and zero backtrace samples are actually captured, making the async metric misleading for confirming profiler state.

During the 4h chaos soak, the detail=False summary fsck exceeded its 180 s bound at ~183 GB / 2.14M objects at the gc_checkpoint, so the harness's `dangling==0` safety gate was skipped (`fsck_status: skipped`) rather than failing — the quadratic discovery/LIST cost blinds the correctness oracle at this pool size (tracked as B146/B154).

During the 4h chaos soak (SOAK-4H-DISK-INFEASIBLE), the `max_pool_gb=40` insert-pacing throttle could not hold the cap: the pool crossed 40 GB by ~t+30min and kept climbing (~5 GB/min decelerating to ~1.8 GB/min under full throttle) because RustFS performs no background compaction and MergeTree merge/mutation write-amplification plus non-reclaim outpace insert-pacing; growth stopped cleanly only when inserts stopped, at a ~183 GB plateau.

During the definitive consistency soak, a GC round (round 3) did zero work but still took 764 seconds, which was flagged as an observability gap (no signal distinguishing a genuinely idle round from a stalled one) rather than a correctness bug.

D2 found S20 (replicated fetch and relink) failed because the follower's `CasRootCas` counter read 0, noting the CAS counters may not be scoped per-node; recommended fix is to scope the CAS counter per node or make the verdict record-only.

Risk register #9 (Medium, confirmed): six `ContentAddressed*` `ProfileEvents` (`ProfileEvents.cpp:876-881`) have zero increment sites, relics of the pre-rebuild generation/tombstone GC design; always-zero counters imply "no resurrections/orphans" on dashboards, which is actively misleading. Suggested action: delete them after verifying no dashboard depends on them.

Risk register #15 (Low, confirmed): mount events emitted inside `Store::open` (`CasStore.cpp:331-337`) are dropped because the event sink is installed only after `open` returns, so first-mount claim/conflict decisions never reach `system.content_addressed_log`. Suggested action: pre-install the sink before `open` if first-mount audit matters.

Risk register #18 (Low, confirmed): a single `SingleWriterSlot`/`MountLeaseKeeper` renew failure emits two separate `mount_conflict` audit rows (one classified, one a timeline marker), so a naive `count()` over the audit log over-reports conflict occurrences.

A single mount-lease renewal failure emits two audit rows (a classified `mount_conflict` plus a separate `renew_failed` timeline marker), causing a naive count of `mount_conflict` events to over-report failures.

An earlier revision of the soak audit had falsely declared `CasRootGet` (a backend counter of GETs on the `roots/` prefix) removed; it was in fact still live, and the oracle's counter swap to `CasRefLogBodyGets` stands only on consumer-isolation grounds, not on `CasRootGet` being dead.
Per-event CA audit logging is best-effort: a full SystemLog queue drops rows with a warning and never blocks the Core operation.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` reports one row per mount slot and classifies state as `live`, `expired`, `terminated`, `fenced`, or `corrupt`.
`CasInstrumentedBackend` is an operation-counting ProfileEvents decorator, not a fault-injection backend.
A GC round emits one `Start` row and one `Finish` row in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`; a `Start` without a matching `Finish` indicates a hung or failed round.
Positive CAS scenarios must have no `Error` finish rows in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`; `NotALeader` rows on non-leaders are expected.
The backup destination is a real CAS pool that runs standard GC over shadow namespaces, and `clickhouse-disks ca-fsck` verifies it.

GC observability includes heartbeat acknowledgement lag, B170 condemn/spare/graduate/delete/fence-out events, retired-list size and oldest-entry age, and an invariant alert for changed shards whose pre-fold events are not folded.

In the mount-recovery plan, `claimMountAwaitingExpiry` exposes an optional `on_wait_start` callback that fires once with the observed lease and latched deadline so `Store::open` can emit an operator-visible log.
Conditional deletes performed by `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` are recorded by `BlobStorageLogWriter` for all outcomes, with the S3 error attached when applicable.
The `gc_fold_clamp` event records namespace, shard, manifest, reason, and `at_version`, making clamp forensics queryable instead of requiring archived server-log archaeology.

The corrected GC-log observation includes `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, `entries_redeleted`, `fence_outs`, `min_ack`, and `anomalies` along with deletion, outcome, duration, and error fields.

`s3_error_rates(node)` reports read/write error and request counters plus rates, returning `None` when counters are absent rather than fabricating zero; `end_checkpoint` stores the rates as an informational verdict.
The harness field `cont_mem_peak_incl_cache` is explicitly cache-inclusive cgroup memory evidence; verdicts use `peak_mem_resident` for resident-memory claims.

The dev-scale S13 smoke passed all safety checks, including `fsck dangling=0`, replica agreement, bounded abandoned-precommit residual, no failed GC rounds, and `dryrun ⊆ unreachable`; its lone inconclusive result was only an observability gate.
The dangling-precommit regression scenario is S30, whose `no unbounded leftovers` verdict must show no `_manifests` leak after the fix.

The side-effect-free supersede peek must cause exactly one `blob_retire_replaced` event with `detail["superseded_token"]`, one `CasGcRetireReplaced` increment, and no accompanying `blob_retire` or `CasGcRetiredCondemned` increment.

The facade `explain` surface is bounded test/log-only state with decisions such as hit, mutable refresh, mismatch, miss, oversized bypass, strict bypass, force-fresh read, and invalidation; it has no SQL surface.
`graduationDue` is computed from seal summaries as `pending_total > 0 || oldest_nonpending_condemn_round < current_round` and requires zero retired-list I/O.

The audit classified lower coverage in `CasGc`, `CasStore`, `CasInspect`, and `CasOrphanManifestSweep` as mostly unreachable from the unit sweep, with CLI rendering, cursor/list-budget arms, and multi-process lease/fencing arms covered by integration or soak paths.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` should expose per-disk `is_leader`, `pending_reclaim`, `last_success_age_seconds`, and `wedged_namespace_count` health columns.
`system.content_addressed_mounts.server_uuid` is typed as `UUID`, while `started_at_ms` and `expires_at_ms` are typed as `DateTime64(3)`.

Every new introspection counter must have at least one emit site and at least one test asserting a nonzero counter delta; a declared counter without an emit site is considered the S13 INTROSPECTION-1 anti-pattern.

The decommission audit is persisted as `member_decommission` begin, per-namespace, and end events in `system.content_addressed_log`, while `system.content_addressed_mounts` shows the victim progressing from `fenced` or `terminated` to row disappearance after slot deletion.
The 2026-07-13 soak recorded 1,128,370 PUTs and 5,704,432 GETs across both nodes during the measured window.
An effective committed-part repoint emits a `system.content_addressed_log` event, a warning-level log, and a ProfileEvent.
The all-tree soak recorded zero unreachable objects and zero dangling objects at both recovery checkpoints and the final converge checkpoint.
`CasRefRepoint == 0` is a valid soak assertion for cards without `FREEZE`, `ATTACH`, `DETACH`, `MOVE`, or `REPLACE PARTITION`, while attach/detach lifecycle cards legitimately repoint.
Every committed-part repoint emits `CasEventType::RefRepoint`, writes a `LOG_WARNING`, and increments a ProfileEvent.
The permanent S39 regression is intended to exercise a degraded-but-alive object store, because prior chaos coverage faulted nodes but not S3 while nodes remained alive.

The MOVE test gate includes `MOVE PART` and `MOVE PARTITION` in both directions, concurrent SELECTs, `fsck` with `dangling=0`, bounded GC reclamation, restart complete-or-rollback behavior, and dedup-on-TO-CA.

The COW map's randomized property test must compare insert, update, erase, find, size, ordered iteration, and materialize operations against `std::map<String, RefCommittedRow>`, including copy-then-mutate isolation.

The COW implementation must pass equivalence tests against `std::map`, an O(1)-copy assertion, byte-identical `snapshotOf` output, the existing `Ca*:Cas*` battery, and a trace check that `__copy_construct_tree` is no longer a top ref-table stack.
A failed S40 fault schedule or zero outage-induced insert failures makes the run vacuous and must fail its anti-vacuity verdict instead of passing silently.
The CA integrity oracle can remain clean during this loss because no dangling CAS ref exists; only a row-count or checksum oracle detects the missing acknowledged rows.

The failpoint regression test must make the first deduplicated INSERT fail before Keeper registration, retry the identical row after disabling the failpoint, and observe `count() = 1` rather than the pre-fix false-dedup result `0`.
The stabilization campaign rule is that there are no tolerated known reds; tactical tolerance requires a tracked return item, and standing exceptions require a complete RCA approved by the user.

The S23 jemalloc growth is bounded rather than an unbounded leak because its rate decelerates from about 30 to 16.7 MiB per minute and live bytes correspond to a bounded set of active system-log parts reclaimed by merges or TTL.

The 11 campaign INCONCLUSIVE scenarios were pre-existing `ci`-scale instrumentation limitations rather than product bugs, including short GC-log windows, blob-cache masking of fetch counts, unreachable manifest/RSS thresholds, and unavailable compose baselines; full scale is required for final answers.

CAS ProfileEvent descriptions should use a lead sentence such as `Number of ...` or `Total ... in microseconds`, followed by a separate interpretive sentence; event names and value types remain unchanged.

The uncertainty exception includes the observed mount-holder identity and the keeper's local sequence, while `MountConflict` carries the observed identity and distinguishes the branch through its `outcome` string; no new ProfileEvent is required.
S42's detailed fsck oracle must fail closed when `stale_edge` is absent, because `stale_edge` is detail-mode-only and a missing key can indicate a binary that predates the invariant.

`CasUnresolvedReason::NoAttemptSent` distinguishes a provably unwritten key from an ambiguous unresolved PUT, and `CasRefAppendPreAttemptRefused` preserves observability after the no-wedge behavior removes the wedge as evidence.
An unmatched remove delta is currently a silent no-op at the edge reducer, so the instrumentation round added an unmatched-remove counter rather than changing the reducer's semantics.

The `S42` verdict treats a consistent on-disk and in-memory state as the deciding result; targeted post-durable-install counters are reported rather than gating, while the generic anti-vacuity guard remains gating.
`Verdict.reported` records a genuinely non-gating observation without affecting run status, and must not be used to soften an assertion or convert unavailable data into a pass.
A successful force-claim must emit a warning and a `CasEvent` audit record naming the displaced uuid, the new uuid, and the death certificate used.

Counters such as `CasGcProbeAHolePresent` and `CasGcProbeAHoleAbsent` are process-local and can be erased by chaos restarts, whereas `gc_anomaly` audit rows survive; both carriers are needed for field diagnosis.

The S42 consistency verdict separately reports post-restart equality, clean fsck `dangling`/`unaccounted`/`stale_edge` results, and the snapshot integrity oracle; `snapshot_oracle_checked == 0` is inconclusive rather than a pass.
Every added ca-soak counter must be registered in `utils/ca-soak/soak/signals.py` or the harness will not read it.

The classified renewal mismatch reason is retained by `MountLeaseKeeper` before `onRenewMismatch` throws, so `onRenewFailed` can emit it in the fence warning; the reasons include `same_epoch_state_uncertain`, `superseded`, `foreign_writer`, and `vanished`.

Stage A's soak PASS criteria require zero data loss, no wedge surviving a foreground flush or remount resolution opportunity, clean fsck, bounded `unaccounted` growth attributable to suppressed deletes, and no uninjected ERROR-severity log lines.

The authoritative release counter and ERROR line are emitted only after the final release attempt fails; intermediate INFO lines may still appear, so settled-late tests scope silence to the authoritative message class.

A sender-side relink refusal must identify one of `fence`, `unrecovered`, `wedge`, `poison`, `budget`, or `no-such-part`; the receiver logs the transient reason at INFO and acts only on the certified answer and identity pair.

The T14 audit distinguishes salvage figures, which are re-derivable from archived logs, from controller live-pass figures, which are unreproducible and ledgered verbatim; the two sources are not silently blended.
S3 operation counts derived from rate-limited `WriteBufferFromS3` Trace lines are lower bounds; ProfileEvents counts from `gc_phases` are exact.

A healthy destructive soak must perform destructive work, leave `ca-fsck --detail` without dangling or stale edges, reach zero backlog, preserve hold/anomaly suppression of irreversible paths, avoid a second full ref LIST after probe-A removal, and expose phase timings and S3 counts.
A `Removing` namespace with no terminal record must be surfaced after a configured number of GC rounds; GC must append nothing while it is stuck.

`explain(PartRefKey)` is structured diagnostic state containing retention status, the last decision, manifest reference, and estimated bytes, and is intended only for tests and log lines.

Freshness-meta validation requires CAS gtests, a deterministic GC-delete-versus-writer-resurrect race test, ASan, a CA-s3 lane with zero promote aborts and zero fsck dangles, and a soak with meta_without_body equal to zero.

The retired-in-snapshot validation requires the S30 resurrect-churn/recurring-hash scenario and the S33 concurrent-leader scenario to pass; S33 guards the concurrent-leader reclaim-leak regression and S30 covers the resurrect-supersede path.

The one-hour soak success criteria are two consecutive final `fsck dangling=0 unreachable=0` reads, an empty `ca-gc-dryrun`, no logical-error exceptions, and bounded snapshot/log tails; host logs are archived before teardown.

Round B measures each lever with 10-minute phase-3 comparative soaks using the same seed and one variable per run, classifying results from per-family `ProfileEvents` deltas summed through `metric_log` because `system.events` resets on chaos restarts.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` must expose a non-gated lifecycle snapshot with `lifecycle`, `lifecycle_reason`, and `lifecycle_since` even when `store()` is refused for a not-live disk.

A future CAS soak intended as a performance specimen must dump system tables to `utils/ca-soak/logs/` before `compose down`, or persist `/var/lib/clickhouse` on a named volume, because the existing compose setup loses those tables with the container.
A passing dev-scale soak is never treated as specification-scale validation because each card records its actual scale and verdict.
For CPU, off-CPU, and memory investigations, scenario reports must rank `system.trace_log` stacks separately for `CPU`, `Real`, and `Memory` trace types.

The unattended campaign watchdog is intended to run every 20 minutes and check fresh progress artifacts, disk usage, CPU starvation, Docker debris, and heavy-build versus soak overlap before intervening.
Phase durations in `system.cas_gc_log` do not sum to `duration_ms`; the `Finish` row's `duration_ms` is authoritative for total round time.
Post-soak validation should mine system.query_log ProfileEvents for PartsLockWaitMicroseconds, S3 request counters, and Keeper wait events to identify SELECT outliers.

`SYSTEM CAS GC RUN` returns one result row per disk with the columns `disk`, `acquired_lease`, `deferred`, `round`, `candidates_marked`, `objects_deleted`, `objects_absent`, `objects_replaced`, `objects_spared`, `manifests_deleted`, `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, `entries_redeleted`, `fence_outs`, and `anomalies`.

A successful `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` returns `disk`, `performed`, `round`, `generation`, `namespaces`, `shards`, `committed_refs`, `live_precommits`, `unowned_alive_manifests`, `edges`, and `clamped_shards`.

`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` returns `server_root_id`, `namespaces_removed`, `namespaces_already_removed`, `committed_refs_removed`, `precommits_removed`, `manifest_debris_removed`, `staging_objects_removed`, `mountpoint_objects_removed`, `slot_removed`, and `warnings`.
The focused `CasGcRefWalkPlan` test for unmatched adopted parents verifies one event, one exact-id log line, and unchanged absence from plan, parent-state, and successor-state output.

During the 4h chaos soak, the soak harness's own `pool_objects` telemetry returned `None` for the entire run and `pool_bytes` returned `None` on roughly half the ticks under write load; the throttle fails closed on `None` (treats it as `_THROTTLE_MAX`), and an independent `du`-based resource monitor gave ground truth instead — the soak's own pool telemetry is unreliable at scale.

`system.part_log`'s `NewPart` row shares the same underlying ProfileEvents as the originating `INSERT` query's `system.query_log` row (confirmed via `sumMap(ProfileEvents)` cross-checks), so summing them together double-counts S3/Cas cost; `MergeParts`/`MutatePart`/`DownloadPart` are genuinely additive on top of `query_log` because their originating `Optimize`/`Alter` query_log rows show zero S3 ProfileEvents (background execution is captured only by part_log).

`system.trace_log`'s three trace_types answer different questions and must not be conflated: `CPU` shows where processor cycles are spent (group by full stack, not just leaf frame); `Real` shows wall-clock time including blocking waits, where most top entries are healthy idle capacity and the useful signal is a thread blocked inside the product's own internal queue/lock; `Memory` samples allocation events (not resident memory), and its leaf frame is always the profiler's own capture routine, so the first one or two frames must be skipped before reading the real allocation site.

S23's initial idle-RSS-growth failure correlated with elevated S3 error rates in the same window (read 8.6%, write 17.2% on one node); S3 retries allocate transient upload/download buffers that jemalloc keeps resident as dirty pages, inflating RSS without inflating tracked memory, which is one of two identified amplifiers of the outlier (the other being fresh-boot warmup variance).

`part_log.ProfileEvents` shows `s3_put=0` while `cas_cond>0` for a given part operation because `S3PutObject` increments on upload-pool threads outside the part-op scope; use `CasConditionalWriteAttempts` to attribute per-part S3 writes instead.

GC's per-hash `.meta` writes run on a bounded side pool and escape the GC round's `ProfileEvents` scope, so round-level `cas_cond` undercounts GC's actual write volume; this is tracked as `CasGcMetaWriteAnomaly`.

The CA stateless suite (~26 CA-specific tests, `04278`-`05009`) covers black-box disk equivalence, correctness-under-active-GC, no-leftovers, GC introspection via `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` and `system.content_addressed_log`, Replicated support, transactions, freeze/backup/restore/fetch-partition, mutations/lightweight-delete/patch-parts, projections, dedup window, and GC snap prune; 10 tests carry `no-content-addressed-storage` and are gated out under the CA-default job.
The asynchronous CAS metric format strings are `CASGcIsLeader_{}`, `CASGcPendingReclaim_{}`, `CASGcLastSuccessAgeSeconds_{}`, and `CASGcWedgedNamespaces_{}`.
Before multi-tenant deployment, the default grants for `system.content_addressed_log` and `system.content_addressed_mounts` should be verified for low-privilege users.

The first relink measurement is the steady-state share of confirms hitting a cold table; a materially nonzero share falsifies the warm-by-construction premise and triggers reconsideration of the rejected recovery bounds.

A long or wedged GC round currently becomes visible only after the fact; the planned observability includes a duration watchdog, LIST/fold progress events, and an alert for an unbalanced `gc_fold_begin`/`gc_fold_end` pair.

CA product operability still required a `SYSTEM` control surface for starting and stopping GC, putting a pool read-only, and running checks; product-side GC stop existed only as a soak-harness workaround.
The server OOM finding of approximately 49 GiB RSS at hour four had not been reproduced after the streaming `putBlob` fix and required a long soak to confirm resolution.

The GC bottleneck study requires per-phase wall time, request counts by verb, bytes, pages, retries, and timeouts; it also requires a namespace-churn reproduction rig with controllable arrival rate and an unsaturated endpoint.

The mount fence-recovery implementation still requires live validation under induced S3 latency to prove renewal cadence remains within its period, a live lease does not expire, no spurious `gc_fence_out` occurs, and genuine fence-out recovers as a higher-`writer_epoch` incarnation.
A distinct-manifest counter per GC round would make the manifest re-read ratio continuously observable and test the large-window redundancy prediction.

CAS introspection should expose pool format and backend capabilities, namespace roots and generations, manifest lifecycle counts, blob reachability, GC cursors, decoded key/object explanations, and machine-readable dry-run reports.

The T8 healthy-pool soak should check zero `no usable checkpoint` anomalies in addition to zero `unproven` and zero frontier-probe budget, because a namespace with no usable checkpoint now suppresses through an anomaly rather than silently.
`gc_round_sweep_namespace_budget = 20` should be observed in T8 soak testing because it is a per-round throughput limit that can retain namespaces when more than 20 debris namespaces share one page.

To make a CAS soak's tracked-memory gate reflect CAS behavior rather than the profiler firehose, either disable the harness's 10 ms query profiler for S23 or subtract the `DB::SystemLog` flush working set from the tracked-memory measurement.
The CA praktika job runs the complete stateless suite with a CA disk as the default MergeTree storage, using local object storage and RustFS-backed S3 variants.
gc_scheduler is lazily created without a mutex in runOneGcRoundForTest and runGarbageCollectionRoundNow, so concurrent SYSTEM ... GC calls could race construction.
S3 412 responses are classified by `S3Exception::getExceptionName()` and are not retried; retrying unmodeled 412 errors caused a RustFS retry storm and long CA stalls.
The first 1-hour soak found that a 51-second pause concurrent with a GC round could brick a writer until manual restart; the self-remount rule addresses this S13 liveness failure.
D2 classified S19 and S26 replica-agreement failures as harness synchronization races because the checks did not run `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` before comparing replicas.

D2 classified S13's failure to become healthy within 240 seconds after killing ch1 as a harness/chaos issue downstream of the connection refusal, not a D1 regression; the recommended fix is to re-run and inspect the kill/restart mechanism and health timeout.
The harness end-checkpoint `forced_gc_to_fixpoint` races the background GC tick, producing `GC round raced background tick (ABORTED)` and causing seven of fifteen runs to end inconclusive.

When a blocked renewal resumes after GC fenced the expired slot, its token-guarded `putOverwrite` receives `PreconditionFailed` and the old code reports the misleading `touched by a foreign writer — failing closed, never re-minting` message.

A read-only `ca_ro` disk over the same pool and `server_root_id` as writable `ca` causes MergeTree part discovery to find parts on both disks and fail restart with `UNKNOWN_DISK` and `ASYNC_LOAD_WAIT_FAILED` when `ca_ro` is absent from policy `ca`.
A full-scale S13 run wedged during quiesce because RustFS returned `503 Service Unavailable`, leaving merges at `progress=1.0` and causing no-timeout `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` to block.
The S13 fitted rerun reproduced the same wedge with 8 KiB payloads and 459 GB free, disproving near-disk-full and payload size as the primary cause.

The CAS startup write/delete capability probe runs before the `skip_access_check` gate, so a mistyped bucket or transient DNS failure can prevent startup even when operators requested the start-now-fix-later path.

`LocalObjectStorage.ListObjectsHandlesPathWithEmbeddedNul` can spin at 100% CPU because an embedded-NUL path can make the object walk loop without advancing; the issue is outside CAS and requires a bounded standalone reproduction followed by a fix or justified test retirement.

RustFS multipart degradation can leave a merge retrying indefinitely: a 15 GB pool produced about 83 GB under `.rustfs.sys/tmp`, multipart `writePart` operations timed out, and the merge loop repeatedly retried after 6 GiB had already committed.
The S01 8 GiB scenario exposed rustfs multipart temporary-space churn with an observed approximate blob ceiling of 2 GiB.
The S03 full-scale scenario exposed rustfs PUT degradation near 6.4 GB of sustained writes and was classified as infrastructure rather than a product failure.

S08's default 900-second budget is too short for its sequential 20,000-partition create phase: the phase took about 933 seconds at a steady 21–25 partitions per second over synchronous HTTP INSERTs, with no hang or pause.

`quiesce_cluster` previously failed immediately on a transient replication-queue `last_exception` during S08's 20,000-fetch workload; adding the existing `no_progress_grace_s` grace period made transient errors non-fatal while persistent errors still fail.

The S36 and S37 placement failures at `ci` and `full` scale were caused by card parameters producing parts larger than the `max_data_part_size_bytes = 4194304` routing threshold on the `hot` volume of the `ca_local` and `ca_local3` policies; ClickHouse correctly routed those parts to `ca`.

In S36 run `20260718T002431_S36_seed1`, part `0_0_0_0` was already on disk `ca`, so the initial-local-disk check failed and `MOVE PART ... TO DISK 'ca'` raised `Code 479` because the part was already on `ca`.
S37 leg 4 failed because all six 15 MiB mixed parts landed on `ca`; the report measured `mixed_bytes_per_part = 15728640` and `route_threshold_bytes = 4194304`.

The `param_table` entries for `ci` and `full` in `cards/s36_s37_disk_move.py` were not threshold-aware: both S36 `rows_per_part*payload_bytes` and S37 `mixed_rows*mixed_payload_bytes` exceeded the 4 MiB routing line.
S08's 20000 sequential single-row HTTP INSERTs take about 880–900 seconds at `ci` scale, consuming the default 900-second timeout without stalls; this is a timing budget, not a hang or regression.

The consistency soak found that GC round duration and pool growth under mutation churn were pre-existing round-cadence scaling behavior, not regressions in the F1-F11 GC-path changes; a checkpoint reduced the pool from 132 GB to 3.7 GB.

A lazy `StorageTableProxy` caused `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` to misidentify a table as not replicated after chaos recovery; the proxy must be materialized for the check, and the lazy proxy itself took about 18 milliseconds to materialize in the reproduction.
A CAS pool directory removed while mounted caused the lease-renewal thread to raise `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and the exception constructor aborted debug and ASan builds in CI PR #2073.

In the reported PR #2073 CI incident, a mount-renewal timeout was followed about ten seconds later by a confirmed mismatch that reached the base `LOGICAL_ERROR` path and aborted the server during exception construction.
`fsck` can read `gc/state` and then stream source-edge runs after a snap-prune retires that generation, producing `CORRUPTED_DATA` on an otherwise healthy pool.

The `RefWriterRecoverySeal.EmptyDeadRegionCarveOutStillReportsSameProcessNamespace` red was caused by a fixture combining no durable epoch, an empty data subtree, and a present mount object, a state production normally avoids because `allocateWriterEpoch` precedes mount publication.

The 4-hour soak harness initially classified the mount-fenced error `INVALID_STATE` code 668 as a hard failure even though its message says to retry after the disk recovers to Live; the classifier had recognized only `ABORTED` plus substrings.

The observed msan incident had a renewal PUT hang inside its retry loop, a silently expired `deadline_boot_ms`, and a later silent `setMountDeadline` re-arm without epoch bump or self-remount; this produced a roughly two-minute durable-write fence window with no transition logs.

The lease-blip remediation's remaining risk is an interleaving in which the disk recovers between the broken-part decision and the detach move; on a double blip or a single-replica pool, the queued fetch may have no source and the part can be absent until manual re-attachment.

The T14 harness failed its health gate while both nodes were pingable but tables were not loaded, approximately 96 seconds before the user table finished attaching; the failure was caused by startup latency rather than user-table part loading.

A corrupt terminal record under the proposed removal protocol leaves the cleanup item `Pending`, prevents `RemovalReady`, and permanently wedges the name until `FORCE REBUILD` or decommission intervenes.
S18 may encounter the pre-existing `B3` freeze/shadow bug; the card records a freeze failure as inconclusive with a backlog anomaly instead of a hard failure.
The local staging write path has no free-space reservation or scratch filesystem guard, and stale `<rand>.tmp` files survive unclean restart because local scratch initialization has no sweeper.

A transient S3 `NETWORK_ERROR` during CAS ref-table startup recovery can leave an `AsyncLoader` job permanently `FAILED`; ClickHouse `AsyncLoader` has no retry or requeue path for a failed table job, so the table remains unavailable until restart or an explicit new load job.
The fence-race `/Replacement` test defect was an invalid fixture: it published a `Live` successor catalog row without the successor life’s `_ckpt`; the production fence guarantee remained intact.
CAS startup capability probing can abort `DiskSelector::initialize()` for unrelated disks because the probe bypasses `skip_access_check` and per-disk startup failures are not isolated.
`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD FORCE` without an explicit disk can bypass healthy-state guards on every CA disk, and routine GC access is currently coupled to the force-rebuild access type.
The stale `CasRefApplyPoisoned` probe caused the S38 run `20260729T115218` to raise because the binary did not expose the probed counters.

The sanitizer failures in `CASRefCheckpointJoin.EncodedCkptSizeIsIndependentOfCardinality` and `CASRefWriterStalePrecommitSweep.BoundedBatchesAndInterruptionResumeAcrossMounts` were caused by CPU-bound encoding racing real-wall-clock deadlines, not by sanitizer-detected product defects.
Without the `ReadBufferFromFileView` position fix, packed-file readers over remote-like buffers can return wrong rows without a checksum exception, including with `optimize_read_in_order`.

Without `Expect: 100-continue`, some S3-compatible stores stream a doomed conditional PUT body, close the connection mid-upload, or return a retryable 500, causing retry storms and stalled merges or inserts.
`LocalObjectStorage::listObjects` must reject an embedded-NUL path because an injected `\0` in `icebergLocal(...)` could make `recursive_directory_iterator` loop indefinitely.

A 4h active-workload chaos soak at WORKERS=6 fills the disk in ~60-90 min; root cause is rustfs#3231 (upstream, open): overwriting a >128 KiB object in an un-versioned bucket leaks the previous incarnation's data directory, so every `casPut` of a `cas/refs/<...>/<shard>` body leaks one uuid dir (observed 1600+ dirs on one busy shard key; `cas/refs` reached 39 GB of a 45 GB pool vs 7.2 GB of real blob data), and the metacache walk over those dirs produces `list_merged err Io(timeout)` / `walk_dir timeout` LIST storms at ~600k files. Mitigation: WORKERS=2; durable fix is lowering ref-shard `casPut` rate (journal batching) and/or moving shard bodies under the 128 KiB inline threshold, or the upstream RustFS fix.

`ca-fsck` times out (>180s) at approximately a 150 GB pool because `ObjectStorageBackend::list` re-enumerates the whole `roots/` prefix per page, an O(N^2) cost in the manifest backlog; the fix is to paginate at the source and separate shard objects into a dedicated prefix.

S37's single failing verdict (22/23) was diagnosed as the scenario card's own oracle bug rather than a product defect: the card expected 100 rows but the true count across both legs is 100+100=200, and the checksum stayed stable across the kill with rows=200 even when the mover no-op'ed; this masks a never-verified atomicity property and was tracked as a BACKLOG verify item rather than a shipped fix.

fsck's `corrupted_runs` finding was invisible on the fsck summary and treated as non-fatal even though it is a `clean()` term; separately the entry-gate fsck budget was inverted (subprocess timeout 180s vs scan deadline 600s), making the `--partial` degrade path unreachable from the harness, and 4 of 39 checkpoints in a 4h soak lost their whole fsck gate as a result.

Turning on fsck's `--partial` degrade path without further changes would fabricate a consistency proof: a timed-out scan returns `dangling=0`, and the soak harness's `wait_for_pool_consistent` counts that fabricated zero as a clean read; the remaining `FsckTimeout` path still substitutes fabricated zeros and is tracked as BACKLOG `{#fsck-fabricated-clean-on-timeout}`, a landmine guarded today only because every consumer happens to check first.

D2 classified S31 (ca-gc-dryrun under gc_shards>1) as INFRA: `docker-compose-gc_shards2.yml up -d` returned rc=1 and the cluster never became healthy within 240s, producing 0/0 verdicts (errored at reset) rather than executing any test.

D2 found S21 (read-heavy many-ref) failed because the test ran `SELECT ... FINAL` against a plain `ReplicatedMergeTree`, producing `ILLEGAL_FINAL` on 12/48 queries, and separately its column-prune check (`1col=0 all=0`) was vacuous at dev scale because blobs were fully cached; recommended fix is to drop FINAL or use a ReplacingMergeTree and gate column-prune at a scale where blobs aren't fully cached.

D2 found S10 (patch parts + lightweight deletes) left a deleted bucket with 60 rows and patch parts observed = 0 (which may merge away quickly); classified as SCALE/TIMING, recommending verification at bigger scale with sync/settle before the count rather than treating it as a product bug.

The emulated S3-compatible backend (rustfs) answers `TokenMismatch` (HTTP 412) rather than `NotFound` for an `If-Match` DELETE issued against an already-absent object, so idempotent re-executions of a delete log as `outcome=replaced` instead of `absent`.

Plain-object CAS loops (`casPutObject`/`casRemoveObject`, used for namespace files and mountpoint objects) run through the backend's default retry policy rather than `CasRequestController`, so they get no single-attempt client and no lease-relative deadline — bounded only by a local `MAX_CAS_ATTEMPTS=100` — meaning a flaky S3 could let such a write outlive the mount lease, the exact hazard the RFC timeout model forbids for the ref lane.

The two CAS GC SQL verbs use inconsistent naming: `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GARBAGE COLLECTION` spells the phrase out while `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` abbreviates it to `GC`, giving operators an inconsistent user-facing vocabulary.

The `ca-fsck` entry gate timed out on a 5.5 GB pool (exceeded 180s) with `reachable=0` after 160s, meaning the scan had not finished its first phase; the timeout now degrades honestly to a logged skip, but the gate does not run exactly when the pool is large enough to matter.

S08's apparent 900-second timeout was root-caused as a genuine time budget, not a hang: an isolated instrumented rerun showed the create-phase alone (20,000 sequential single-row HTTP INSERTs) takes ~880-900s at a steady ~20-25 parts/sec with zero stalls, essentially consuming the whole default scenario timeout before any post-creation checkpoint starts.

S08's end-checkpoint false-INCONCLUSIVE was caused by `quiesce_cluster`'s `drain()` raising instantly on the first sighting of any `replication_queue` entry with a non-empty `last_exception`, with no grace period (unlike its sibling backlog-stall check); fixed in `35faaae182c` by adding `error_since`/grace-period tolerance (`no_progress_grace_s`) plus two regression tests.
`FORCE` bypasses only the healthy-baseline refusal in `rebuildBaseline`; it does not bypass a competing leader or failed `gc/state` CAS.
A raw subtree deletion such as `rm roots/<server>/…` is destructive offline maintenance and is not equivalent to `dropNamespace`, because it bypasses the journal and fenced index pruning.
The RustFS overwrite-leak workaround is a test-harness-only orphan reaper scoped to `roots/`; production CA code is unchanged.
Read-only `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` performs a check-only startup probe, creates no GC or heartbeat thread, and throws a `READONLY` exception from mutating entry points.
A legitimate CAS conditional-PUT collision can count as `S3_ERROR` or `PreconditionFailed` before being reclassified as `PutOutcome::PreconditionFailed`.
A rebuild first health-checks the current state and refuses a healthy state unless `FORCE` is supplied; a broken or absent state proceeds through the recovery path.

The rebuild command surface is `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD [FORCE] <disk>` and is logged through `CasGcScheduler` in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` with `gc_rebuild` audit events in `system.content_addressed_log`.

`clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild --disk <name> [--force]` opens the disk read-only without claiming the server-root mount or creating a heartbeat, takes the independent GC lease, and exits nonzero on refusal.
Rebuild refusal conditions are any missing or invalid committed manifest body, undecodable ref shard, unreadable mount body, healthy current state without `FORCE`, or failure to acquire the GC lease.
The planned SQL rebuild surface converts `performed == false` into `BAD_ARGUMENTS` with the refusal text, while also recording the refusal in the GC log.
The `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` tool must use a read-only open, print rebuild counters one per line, print `refusal=<text>` on refusal, and never claim a live server's mount.

The generic `SingleWriterSlot` message `touched by a foreign writer` is reserved for an own-UUID, same-epoch, unfenced token violation; GC-fence recovery must report `fenced by GC after lease expiry` instead.
Under S22's injected 503, 429, slow, and reset faults, 336 faults produced zero workload errors, replica agreement, and `dangling=0`; bounded retries absorbed the faults.

If `gc/state` is lost, attempt-local ref-base runs are not independently authoritative; offline rebuild may conservatively union surviving runs and logs, may over-protect storage, and returns writable authority only after an explicit recovery action adopts a new baseline.

If GC loses its cursor state, writer recovery remains valid because snapshots and logs are authoritative; destructive GC stays disabled until an explicit offline rebuild establishes a verified current-owner baseline.
Any conditional-copy probe error or non-enforcing result selects local staging and logs that S3 staging is unavailable; it must never silently fall back to unconditional overwrite.
Read-only retries are bounded by both attempt count and total wall-clock duration; exhausted budgets fail closed and defer the higher-level GC round or recovery attempt.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` requires a distinct `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GC_REBUILD` privilege and an explicit disk; omitting the disk is a syntax error and naming a non-content-addressed disk is `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.

If any decommission drain step cannot confirm emptiness, the slot remains terminated with its farewell stamp, the report contains a warning, and a rerun is expected to complete the job; the operation reports blobs as `unreferenced`, never as `freed`.
Lowering `materialization_grace_ms` increases the risk that a late-materializing predecessor write is dropped by the recovery seal and later reported as debris.

The planned S3-fault regression has a short-fault leg below lease TTL that must preserve the lease and a long-fault leg above lease TTL that must fence, back off, recover, and finish with `fsck` reporting `dangling=0`.
S39's long-fault assertions require a populated `system.replication_queue.last_exception` and successful post-recovery writes before running an `fsck`-to-fixpoint check.
The MOVE-to-CA smoke contract is that `disk_name` changes `default → ca_smoke → default`, row checksums remain identical, and neither `Code: 236` nor a `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` exception occurs.

For other concurrent-read observations, CAS fsck is designed to fail closed or report an inconclusive result: fresh reference checks treat a concurrently deleted blob or manifest as still referenced, checksum failures are catalogued as `CorruptedRun`, and timeouts set `partial=1`.

The CI scrape is conditional on a failed functional-test result, and the stop operation is best-effort; therefore a force-claim liveness guard must be real even though the normal scrape is post-mortem.

A terminal record unreadable before folding blocks legitimate removal in `Removing` and must be surfaced as a stuck terminal-corrupt removal; after the terminal has folded and cleanup evidence is durable, later physical inaccessibility is leak-only cleanup failure.

For a name in `Removing` or `RemovalReady`, creation returns a typed retryable error stating that terminal fold, cleanup completion, and cursor retirement are pending; a DROP-driven targeted fold is not part of the correctness baseline.
A scenario with `needs_infra` set is marked inconclusive and its `run` method is not executed when the two-replica plus RustFS compose cannot provide the required infrastructure.

A lazy CAS table reattached as a `StorageTableProxy` can block its first-access build in the ref-namespace LIST inside `CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered` for the entire object-store outage; the table self-heals after the store returns because the proxy job remains `OK` rather than entering a terminal `AsyncLoader` failure.

`clickhouse-disks` exposes the logical `@cas@`-stripped view, whereas raw S3 listing exposes the physical archive; recursively removing a raw subtree is destructive maintenance and is not equivalent to `dropNamespace`.
S22 requires bounded object-store `503`, `429`, slow-response, and connection-close faults to increase visible latency without data loss, unbounded retries, or committed partial refs.
`CommandFsck::executeImpl` does not throw for `stale_edge` in either summary or detail mode, so a detail scan with nonzero `stale_edge` can print a `note:` and still exit with code 0.
A referenced-but-missing or corrupt GC run, retired list, or adopted fold seal raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` and refuses the GC round until an operator performs GC rebuild.

Per-object drain failures during `SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` are recorded as warnings and leave the slot in a terminated-but-not-fully-drained state that a later invocation can resume, rather than raising an exception.
A non-empty `warnings` result from `SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER` means some drain was not confirmed and the mount slot remains as a resume anchor.

The arm-(a) decommission warning reports pool member decommission underway: all N namespace(s) are still owned by this member; upcoming GC rounds perform the final cleanup — re-run this command afterwards to retire the slot, with a count from matching catalog entries; arm (b)'s stale-cut warning remains distinct.
CommandFsck exposes a janitor-pending detail label and a non-throwing note with the pending count, bytes, and lives; it no longer claims that ca-decommission refuses these keys.
clickhouse-disks cas-drop-member prints server_root_id= rather than srid=, and its read-only error uses the same public name; no tree consumer parses the old srid= output key.
`ReadBufferFromS3::processException` must check `CurrentThread::get().isQueryCanceled()` so a canceled query does not retry until `s3_max_single_read_retries` with backoff.
`MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` must fail with an ordinary exception when `current_writer` is null instead of relying on `chassert`.

The CAS backup threat model defines five threats: T1 bucket/region loss, T2 operator error (`DROP TABLE`, bad mutation, wrong `rm`), T3 a CAS-layer bug (notably a GC bug deleting live data), T4 credential compromise, and T5 format dependence (whether restore requires a CAS-capable ClickHouse, any ClickHouse, or no ClickHouse at all).

As an RTO optimization when a full fetch is too slow, the storage policy can combine a fresh writable CA disk with the backup pool mounted as a readonly disk (claiming no lease or epoch, under the fsck/ca-gc-dryrun discipline): reads work within minutes straight off the backup, writes go to the fresh pool from minute one, and fetch degrades into a background hot-partitions-first drain by ordinary move machinery.

RustFS stores each object as a directory containing an `xl.meta` file plus erasure part files (MinIO-style layout), which is the source of the roughly 2.2x on-disk store amplification observed relative to distinct payload size.

A full CA-s3 lane post-mortem exonerated the B86 log-policy removal for the observed timeout growth: ProfileEvents on every stalled query showed zero CAS/RustFS wait, with threads parked on HTTP socket reads to public internet buckets (e.g. `clickhouse-datasets-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`) — the timeouts were external internet weather, not a CA regression.

The DoS/amplification risk of `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` (SEC-6): rebuild does a full-universe discover-and-fold, O(all shards + all journals), so an attacker with SYSTEM privilege (or who can trigger repeated failures that tempt operators to rebuild) can make it an expensive, pool-wide, memory-heavy sweep sharing SEC-4's decode/fold exhaustion surface; recommended mitigation is rate-limiting/single-flight on the command plus streaming the fold.

The reviewer verified that rebuild adds no attack surface beyond SEC-3's total-compromise bar: an adversary who crafts an internally consistent owner state with refs silently removed could get rebuild to compute a baseline missing those edges, but the trimmed-history baseline guard detects truncated journals and fails closed, so producing an exploitable crafted state already requires full owner-plane write access (already total compromise). Residual open items: confirm the REBUILD RBAC grant is dedicated/narrow (not bundled into a broad SYSTEM grant), and confirm rebuild runs under GC leadership so it cannot race a live round into a split-baseline.
